entry.summary: This study argues that graph neural network message-passing layers are almost exclusively benchmarked on classification and asks whether the same designs help for scalar regression on graphs such as molecules and neural architecture blueprints. It systematically evaluates message-passing variants in regression settings that the field usually overlooks. The concern is that community progress may be overfit to classification metrics.

entry.title: Origins and mitigation of double descent in reduced order modeling

author.name: Andrei A. Klishin, J. Nathan Kutz, Krithika Manohar

entry.summary: Develops a unified data-noise averaging theory explaining when double descent appears in sparse sensing and reduced-order reconstruction, attributing the error peak to catastrophic amplification of a pathological signal component. Provides quantitative risk-curve predictions and mitigation strategies via sensor placement and regularization.

entry.title: Same Evidence, Different Target: Decoding How Diagnostic Evidence Bears on Causal Questions from Language-Model States

author.name: Weiyi Kong, Zhuoran Li

entry.summary: Constructs paired prompts that repeat identical diagnostic evidence while changing the causal target, labeling each case by whether the evidence favors, challenges, leaves unresolved, or misses the claim. Uses linear probes on hidden states to test whether models internally represent the evidence-to-target relation rather than exploiting lexical overlap.

entry.title: Breaking the Curse with BAND: Nonparametric Distribution Estimation in High Dimensions

author.name: Shuo-Chieh Huang, Chien-Ming Chi, Jau-er Chen

entry.summary: Proposes estimating high-dimensional joint distributions through a sparse Bayesian network where each conditional is fit with sparsity-aware conditional mean regression. Achieves polynomial total-variation convergence rates with dimension growing polynomially in sample size, beating classical histogram-density rates.

entry.title: Relation Geometry in Semantic Space of Language Models

author.name: Zhihan Cao, Hiroaki Yamada, Simone Teufel, Tatsuya Hiraoka, Kentaro Inui, Hitomi Yanaka, Takenobu Tokunaga

entry.summary: Investigates how much knowledge about lexical-semantic relations is encoded in the geometry of language model embedding spaces, testing whether relata for a given relation occupy distinct regions and whether relational properties like symmetry and asymmetry are reflected. Provides a systematic three-perspective geometric analysis.

entry.title: WildShadowRemover: In-the-Wild Video Shadow Removal via Detail-Preserving Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Jiamin Xu, Cong Wang, Zheng Dong, Chi Wang, Renshu Gu, Weiwei Xu, Gang Xu

entry.summary: Adapts a pretrained video diffusion model with LoRA for shadow removal in unconstrained real videos, adding a detail injection module to the frozen decoder and frequency-decomposed modulation guided by shadow masks. Targets the scarcity of in-the-wild video shadow removal training data.

entry.title: HeteroPROPMT: A Real-time and Privacy-Preserving Heterogeneous Collaborative Perception Framework

author.name: Armin Maleki, Hayder Radha

entry.summary: Proposes a real-time framework for collaborative perception among vehicles that use different sensors, models, and training domains, avoiding retraining of fusion heads or sharing of proprietary metadata. Uses prompt-style adaptation to align heterogeneous feature spaces for privacy-preserving fusion.

entry.title: Eddeep: a deep-learning framework for fast eddy-current distortion correction in diffusion MRI

author.name: Antoine Legouhy, Ross Callaghan, Yuchuan Qiao, Whitney Stee, Philippe Peigneux, Hojjat Azadbakht, Hui Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a two-stage deep learning pipeline for correcting eddy-current geometric distortions in diffusion MRI, first standardizing volume appearance via supervised image translation and then registering volumes. Aims to match iterative state-of-the-art correction quality at much lower compute cost.

entry.title: From Spatial Semantics to Temporal Context: Leveraging Gaze Trajectory for Weakly Supervised Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Shaoxuan Wu, Xiao Zhang, Xiaodi Zhao, Yunzhi Tian, Yilin Tang, Jun Feng

entry.summary: Uses clinician gaze trajectories, not just fixation points, as weak supervision for medical image segmentation, modeling the temporal order of visual inspection while suppressing noisy exploratory fixations with uncertainty estimates. Offers a cheaper annotation route that fits existing clinical workflows.

entry.title: 3DGBGS: 3D Granular Ball Gaussian Splatting for Compact Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Meng Yang, Shuyin Xia, Dawei Dai, YiWang

entry.summary: Introduces adaptive granular-ball organization to anchor-based 3D Gaussian Splatting, replacing fixed voxelization of sparse point clouds with a coarse-to-fine adaptive structure. Targets compactness and quality for non-uniform point distributions in novel view synthesis.

entry.title: Long-Tailed 3D Point Cloud Dataset Distillation

author.name: Jiahao You, Xu Han, Jinfeng Xu, Xianzhi Li

entry.summary: First study of dataset distillation for 3D point clouds under long-tailed class distributions, where both training and test splits are imbalanced. Adds modules that explicitly account for the imbalance rather than only optimizing geometry or forcing a class-balanced synthetic set.

entry.title: Speech2Grasp: Data-Efficient Transfer of Text-Conditioned Grasp Detection to Speech in Humanoid Robots

author.name: Hung Nguyen, Kim Nhat Minh Nguyen, Van Duc Vu, Van-Danh Le, Hoang Huy Le, Dinh Tuan Nguyen, Pham Tuyen Le, Van-Truong Nguyen, Quan Nguyen

entry.summary: Tests whether a text-conditioned grasp detection model can be transferred to spoken instructions with minimal data, finding that a lightweight projector suffices to map speech into the existing text space while preserving semantics. Validated with real humanoid robot grasping experiments.

entry.title: Do LoRA Read Directions Encode Visual Concepts?

author.name: Zhao Pengfei

entry.summary: Compares the semantic coherence of read directions learned by standard, ReLU, and TopK LoRA adapters against matched random directions in the residual stream of a CLIP model, using a clarity metric. Learned directions are more consistently coherent than random ones, but random directions sometimes look convincing too, so a single striking activation grid is not evidence that a concept was learned.

entry.title: Diagnosing Fine-Grained Inconsistency Classification in Financial Disclosure Text

author.name: Aman Kumar, Lasitha Vidyaratne, Dipanjan D Ghosh, Arnab Chakrabarti, Ahmed K Farahat

entry.summary: Studies fine-grained classification of inconsistency types in financial disclosures across numerical, temporal, referential, factual, and normative categories, comparing frozen embedding classifiers, fine-tuned encoders, evidence-augmented variants, and prompted LLMs on a synthetic benchmark of nearly six thousand instances. Argues that detecting a conflict is insufficient because different types require different downstream checks.

entry.title: Vision-TL-Action: Neuro-Symbolic Trajectory Generation from Visual Observations and Temporal Logic

author.name: Zezhi Liu, Zhiwei Zheng, Hanqian Luo, Deyun Qin, Shizhen Wu, Yongchun Fang

entry.summary: Vision-TL-Action generates robot trajectories from multi-view images plus a coordinate-free temporal logic task graph, fusing symbolic task nodes and visual tokens via cross-attention to condition a flow-matching trajectory generator. The point is to force genuine perception-to-symbol grounding rather than letting the task specification smuggle in exact object coordinates.

entry.title: Sensor-Placement-Agnostic Sonomyography: Toward Continuous High-Dimensional Control by Users with Tetraplegia

author.name: Gavin Sueltz, Vikram Athithan, Emma Ferran, Maria Herrera, Carson J. Wynn, Laura A. Hallock

entry.summary: Describes a real-time sonomyography interface that infers intended movement from ultrasound images of muscle using sparse optical flow, achieving continuous one-degree-of-freedom control after only three calibration poses and a preliminary two-degree-of-freedom extension. It was tested with three participants who have cervical spinal cord injury.

entry.title: Toward a Unified Statistical Theory of Unsupervised Pretraining and Supervised Neural Knowledge Graph Learning

author.name: Jifan Zhang, Miklos Racz, Suqi Liu

entry.summary: Develops a two-stage theory for knowledge graph learning in which unsupervised pretraining on heterogeneous corpora is followed by supervised multi-relation learning, and proves a nonasymptotic risk bound that separates pretraining representation error from labeled-sample error. The framework subsumes several existing scoring-function designs that were previously chosen heuristically.

entry.title: Compute growth doesn't make a software intelligence explosion more likely

author.name: Karthik Tadepalli

entry.summary: Argues against a common shortcut in software-intelligence-explosion debates, showing that exponentially growing physical compute does not change whether the feedback loop of AI-automated AI research becomes explosive. The claim is that the explosion condition depends on returns to research effort, not on the level or growth rate of compute stock.

entry.title: FAS-R1: A Unified Multi-Task MLLM for Reasoning Face Anti-Spoofing

author.name: Hongyang Wang, Yichen Shi, Hongrui Li, Yiru Huo, Jun Feng, Zitong Yu

entry.summary: FAS-R1 is a multimodal LLM for face anti-spoofing that jointly outputs authenticity decisions, attack-type labels, and spoof-region localization, trained with long chain-of-thought supervised warm-up followed by task-specific reinforcement learning. The goal is explainable, evidence-grounded spoof detection rather than bare binary labels.

entry.title: Shared Symbolic Backbones for Physically Consistent Multi-Output Symbolic Regression

author.name: Manuel Rodriguez

entry.summary: This method performs symbolic regression for coupled multi-output systems by evolving a shared symbolic backbone of latent units that several outputs reuse through sparse additive or multiplicative read-outs, with discrete structure from evolution and continuous parameters from gradient descent. The motivation is physically consistent, interpretable models of process systems whose states share physical parameters.

entry.title: FakeIDet3-DB: Refining Digital Attacks and Patch Extraction for Secure ID Benchmarking

author.name: Mu\~noz-Haro Javier, Teruel Andres, Tolosana Ruben, DeAlcala Daniel, Vera-Rodriguez Ruben, Morales Aythami, Fierrez Julian

entry.summary: FakeIDet3-DB is described as the first database of digital manipulations applied to real government-issued identity documents, spanning classical edits such as copy-move and generative manipulations such as face swapping and inpainting, with patch extraction protocols for forensic model training. It aims to close the domain gap left by synthetic ID templates that lack authentic high-frequency security patterns.

entry.title: FPSGen: Flexible Point Cloud Scene Generation with BEV-Supported Transport Flows

author.name: Wenzhe He, Meng Wang, JiaWei Qian, Jinfeng Xu, Ying Liu, Ruihui Li

entry.summary: FPSGen generates outdoor point-cloud scenes by first predicting a bird's-eye-view prior and constructing point sources independently of partial LiDAR scans, removing the train-inference mismatch that leaves prior completion methods sparse at distance and incomplete in occluded regions. It also allows generation from layout cues when LiDAR observations are unavailable.

entry.title: Dual Inversion for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models: From Both Prompt and Noise Perspectives

author.name: Xiaolong Liu, Junjian Li, Yuan Xiao, Jiaqi Deng, Dayong Ye, Tianqing Zhu, Huan Huo

entry.summary: This paper argues that prompt inversion alone is insufficient to reverse engineer a target image from a text-to-image model, since latent noise encodes structural information, and therefore proposes jointly inverting both prompt and noise. It positions gradient-based methods as unstable and gradient-free methods as visually unfaithful.

entry.title: Phoneme- vs. Character-Level Targets and Selective State-Space Models for Intracortical Brain-to-Text

author.name: Lucas Zamora Vera, Jose A. Gonzalez-Lopez

entry.summary: Using a public intracortical brain-to-text benchmark, the authors run a controlled two-by-two comparison of recurrent versus hybrid Mamba decoders and phonetic versus character output targets under a single CTC training protocol. The recurrent phonetic configuration remains strongest, with the selective state-space hybrid competitive but not superior.

entry.title: Actions Have Consequences: Detecting Outcome Performativity using Intervention Testing

author.name: Brandon Gower-Winter, Georg Krempl

entry.summary: The paper formalizes detection of outcome performativity, where a prediction causally changes the outcome it predicts, by intervening with different prediction groups and testing whether the resulting outcome distributions differ significantly. It derives and empirically validates sample-complexity bounds under several assumption classes.

entry.title: Meta-Learned Reward Shaping for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback

author.name: Yunpeng Chu

entry.summary: MeRLa proposes meta-learning a task-aware potential-based reward shaping function across auxiliary tasks before RLHF, combining task discrimination, entropy regularization, and potential conservation so that the shaped reward preserves the optimal policy while densifying the learning signal. The claimed benefit is faster and better-aligned convergence than static task-agnostic reward models. Potential-based shaping is the theoretically safe way to add reward density.

entry.title: From Unsupervised Subgroups to Hypothetical State-Intervention Policies: An Evaluation of Selected Subgrouping Methods in Observational Health Data

author.name: Vasundhara Acharya, Bulent Yener

entry.summary: This study asks whether unsupervised subgroups built only from pretreatment covariates, without using exposure, outcome, or estimated treatment effects, can serve as interpretable units for budget-constrained policy prioritization in observational health data. The framework combines causal-discovery-informed covariate selection, discovery-evaluation splitting, inductive clustering, uncertainty-aware selection, and doubly robust held-out evaluation. It is a disciplined answer to unstable conventional subgroup analysis.

entry.title: Benchmarking ConvLSTM for One-Day-Ahead IMDAA Rainfall-Field Prediction across Four Indian Cities

author.name: Tanmay Ghosh, Shaurabh Anand, Rakesh Gomaji Nannewar, Nithin Nagaraj

entry.summary: Across four Indian cities and 23 monsoon seasons of reanalysis data, ConvLSTM did not consistently outperform naive, statistical, tree-based, or simpler neural baselines for one-day-ahead rainfall-field prediction. Most evidence favoring convolutional recurrence comes from dense high-frequency radar sequences rather than coarse daily grids. The negative result cautions against defaulting to deep spatiotemporal models on sparse data.

entry.title: RAG-HAR+: Towards Cost-Efficient LLM-Based Human Activity Recognition for Edge Deployment

author.name: Hansi Karunarathna, Nirhoshan Sivaroopan, Chamara Madarasingha, Anura Jayasumana, Kanchana Thilakarathna

entry.summary: RAG-HAR+ extends training-free retrieval-augmented human activity recognition from wearable sensors by strengthening retrieval quality so that fewer LLM inference calls are needed, targeting cost-efficient edge deployment. Conventional deep HAR requires dataset-specific training, large labeled corpora, and re-adaptation whenever sensors or activity taxonomies change. The retrieval-first design trades LLM calls for cheaper nearest-example lookup.

entry.title: AIGen: Automating AI Bill of Materials Generation Through Hybrid MLOps Integration

author.name: Federica Pepe, Daniele Bifolco, Costantino Martignetti, Aureliano D'Amici, Fabiano Izzo, Damian A. Tamburri, Massimiliano Di Penta

entry.summary: AIGen automatically generates AI Bills of Materials conforming to the SPDX 3.0 AI and dataset profiles by combining mining heuristics with LLM assistance on top of the MLflow MLOps stack, producing machine-readable inventories of datasets, weights, pipelines, and runtime dependencies. Standards-compliant tooling for AI supply-chain documentation is currently scarce. It supports emerging regulatory and procurement requirements.

entry.title: Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Transformer for Coherent Emergency Department Forecasting

author.name: Filipa Lino, B\'arbara Tavares, Carlos Santiago, Cl\'audia Soares, Manuel Marques

entry.summary: This hierarchical spatio-temporal transformer forecasts emergency department demand simultaneously at hospital, regional, and national levels so that predictions aggregate coherently instead of contradicting one another across administrative tiers. Most existing approaches forecast independently at a single level, producing forecasts that fail to reconcile. Coherence matters because staffing, regional coordination, and national capacity planning all depend on the same underlying demand.

entry.title: Inverse Learning of Latent Risk-Neutral Densities from Irregular Option Quotes

author.name: Lennon J. Shikhman, Michael Galarnyk, Aadi Dash, Nicholas A. Welsh

entry.summary: This study separates accurate option pricing from accurate recovery of the underlying latent risk-neutral density, using a synthetic benchmark with known ground-truth densities alongside a chronological market benchmark on Indian index options. A simple two-component lognormal mixture wins on aggregate price and distributional error metrics, while learned operators such as DeepONet and a quote transformer show narrower advantages on tail quantiles and misspecified families. A conditioning analysis explains why rankings differ across metrics.

entry.title: From Classification to Regression: Using a Fruitfly to Solve Equations

author.name: Shady E. Ahmed, Panos Stinis

entry.summary: Inspired by fruitfly olfactory sensing, this paper reformulates regression as similarity-weighted retrieval over a finite library of representative local patterns rather than fitting a complex global surrogate, exploiting the fact that scientific data often occupies limited recurring regions of input space. Predictions combine stored responses weighted by query similarity in a learned embedding. It is applied to nonlinear dynamical systems, data-driven regression, and physics-informed learning.

entry.title: Self-Adaptive Learning and Model Predictive Control for Tracking Unknown Dynamics with No Regret

author.name: Atharva Navsalkar, Hongyu Zhou, Vasileios Tzoumas

entry.summary: Presents an online learning-for-control method that trains multiple lightweight predictors from scratch and adaptively selects among them to track targets with unknown, possibly switching or adversarial dynamics. Provides finite-time near-optimality and no-regret style guarantees for use in robotic tracking and pursuit tasks.

entry.title: Chaos Is a LADDER: Domain Generalization Beyond Invariance via Reweighting

author.name: Yuhang Jiang, Fengchuan Zhang, Sanguo Zhang, Guojun Zhu

entry.summary: Argues that domain generalization should not always chase invariance, since domain style can modulate how causal features map to outcomes. Proposes a reweighting method that uses style to locate an unseen target domain among sources and decide which domain-dependent prediction rules to trust.

entry.title: BATS: Resource-Efficient Volumetric Segmentation with Boundary-Aware Mixed-Resolution Tokens

author.name: David Hagerman, Roman Naeem, Fredrik Kahl

entry.summary: Presents a 3D medical segmentation architecture that predicts where boundaries lie and allocates fine-resolution tokens only near boundaries, thin structures, and small targets while representing homogeneous regions coarsely. This input-dependent mixed-resolution hierarchy cuts activation memory and inference cost versus dense multi-scale models.

entry.title: A large-scale corpus of religious radio broadcast transcripts from webstream recordings in the United States

author.name: Samuel Bestvater, Athena Chapekis, Skyler Seets, Anna Lieb, Sono Shah, Aaron Smith

entry.summary: Releases a large corpus of transcribed and speaker-diarized US religious radio broadcasts, captured from 785 webstreams over one month and covering signals of more than two thousand stations, totaling over 700,000 recordings and 60 million lines of speech. Segments and labels content by programming format for social-science analysis.

entry.title: Evaluating Regional Bias in LLMs From Abstract Stereotype to Concrete Social Decision-Making

author.name: Jiayuan Di, Haoyi Yang, Yufei Luo, Jiahui Qu, Yiming Wang

entry.summary: Builds a framework linking abstract regional stereotypes to concrete decisions, rating all 34 Chinese provincial-level regions on warmth and competence and then testing paired-choice decisions in education, occupation, and social interaction across six models. Reveals substantial and structured regional bias that propagates from stereotype ratings into allocation-like choices.

entry.title: BG-REAL: A Public Real-Data Anchored Benchmark for Background Manipulation Detection and Localization

author.name: Bugra Alperen Uluirmak, Rifat Kurban

entry.summary: Releases a benchmark for detecting and localizing manipulations that occur in image backgrounds rather than on salient foreground objects, built from real segmentation data with matched authentic controls and quality-controlled masks. Covers six edit families with 7,000 samples plus synthetic controls.

entry.title: MoSAIC: Aligned Intervention Supervision for Part-Local Motion Style Transfer

author.name: Nazanin Amini, Kevin Desai

entry.summary: A latent diffusion framework for transferring gestures or gaits from reference motions to selected body parts while preserving the source action, timing, and root trajectory. Addresses the lack of paired training targets by routing region-factorized reference features and supervising with aligned interventions.

entry.title: Registration-Grounded Spectral Fusion for Unregistered WLI/NBI Endoscopic Lesion Segmentation

author.name: Pengyu Jie, Wanquan Liu, Rui He, Pengcheng Li, Weiping Wen, Deyu Meng, Junwei Han, Chenqiang Gao

entry.summary: Fuses white-light and narrow-band endoscopic images for lesion segmentation when the two views are misaligned, first estimating feature correspondence and then predicting where that correspondence is trustworthy. Reliability estimates gate selective complex-domain fusion to avoid mixing non-corresponding tissue regions.

entry.title: SpatialQ: Understanding 3D Gaussian Splatting Scene Quality via Visual-based MLLM

author.name: Jingxuan Su, Shenglin Wang, Tiesong Zhao, Ge Li, Wei Gao

entry.summary: Builds a multimodal LLM-based quality assessment framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes that accounts for spatial structure and cross-view consistency rather than only per-image perceptual fidelity. Aims to make MLLM judgments stable enough for quality regression.

entry.title: PRISM-Net: Patient-specific reference-guided inter-breast symmetry matching for three-class breast DCE-MRI classification

author.name: Boya Zhang, Shuaiwen Zhou, Di Kong, Mingxu Wang, Wenbiao Du, Yiman Zhong, Yuexin Duan, Xiawei Yue, Liuquan Cheng, Xiru Li

entry.summary: Classifies breast DCE-MRI into no-lesion, benign, and malignant at the breast level by using the contralateral breast as a patient-specific reference, without explicit registration. Bilateral feature matching is used to suppress patient-specific background variability that confounds classification.

entry.title: Step-Attention Refinement of DINOv3 Features for Efficient Anterior Eye Segmentation

author.name: Philippe Baumstimler, Jean-Mathieu Gagnon, S\'ebastien Gagn\'e, Mathieu Duchesneau, Cl\'ement Playout, Lama S\'eoud

entry.summary: Adapts a distilled self-supervised vision transformer backbone to anterior eye segmentation with a step-attention module that progressively refines multi-level features before dense prediction. Targets robustness under heterogeneous clinical acquisition with scarce annotations.

entry.title: Towards Grounded GI Endoscopy VQA via Multi-Task Learning on Small VLMs

author.name: Itbaan Safwan, Ramail Khan, Muhammad Annas Shaikh, Muhammad Atif Tahir

entry.summary: Fine-tunes small vision-language models on gastrointestinal endoscopy question answering with auxiliary grounding and description tasks built cheaply from existing masks and Grad-CAM weak labels. Aims to make internal representations reflect the visual evidence behind clinical answers.

entry.title: Archetypes or ability? Clustering for modelling student mathematical competence

author.name: Benjamin Mawdsley, Tom Quilter, Richard Turner, Sarah Jackson, Paul Edwards

entry.summary: Applies Bernoulli mixture modeling to exam responses from over 119,000 UK students to test whether mathematical competence decomposes into discrete acquired skill sets. Finds few distinct clusters and that overall ability dominates, challenging assumptions built into many personalized learning systems.

entry.title: Model-Driven Requirements Configuration with Three-Valued Uncertainty Scoring

author.name: Ahmed Ibrahim

entry.summary: Proposes a neuro-symbolic multi-agent architecture where an LLM heuristically traverses a formal requirements lattice while a deterministic symbolic validator enforces structural conformance and logical consistency, plus three-valued scoring of pre-validation uncertainty. Targets requirements engineering where unconstrained LLM output is often invalid.

entry.title: TraceCoder: Explainable and Auditable Code Generation with Position-Key Snippet Versioning

author.name: Rwaida Alssadi, Muntaser Syed, Balaji Kasula, Lamine Deen, Majed Alotaibi, Mohammed Alghamdi, Tyler Ton, Ali Alqarni, Marius Silaghi

entry.summary: TraceCoder records per-repair provenance for LLM-generated code, including benchmark reference, round, failure text, and model explanation, and renders the history as annotated heat-mapped source with a fractional position-key indexing scheme for stable snippet identity. The aim is post-hoc auditability of black-box coding agents.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning on Cost-Constrained Quadrupedal Hardware

author.name: Javier C. Weddington, Bence P. \"Olveczky, Stephen A. Baccus

entry.summary: The authors study locomotion RL on a very cheap quadruped where a measured actuator transport delay above 50 ms turns the task into a partially observable problem, and adopt a biologically inspired handling of delayed and noisy feedback to close the sim-to-real gap. The contribution is making RL viable on hardware that most sim-to-real work avoids.

entry.title: Audio-Anchored Fusion of Multi-Ratio DiT Reconstruction Residuals for Cross-Domain Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Haotian Mo, Jie Liu, Siqi Shen, Songzhu Mei, Xinhai Chen, Xiangyang Wang, Yigui Feng, Shuai Li, Gencheng Liu, Keqi Yang, Qinglin Wang

entry.summary: The authors use a diffusion transformer trained only on genuine speech as a frozen reconstruction probe, taking residuals at several masking ratios as domain-sensitive cues, and fuse them as a gated additive correction on top of a WavLM representation for cross-domain audio deepfake detection. They report equal-error-rate results on ASVspoof 5 and in-the-wild data with multi-seed variance.

entry.title: A Graph-Native Bitemporal Memory Store for Conversational AI Agents

author.name: Alp Niksarli, Gopesh Baheti

entry.summary: This paper describes an agent-local long-term memory store built on a property graph with vector indexes and a full bitemporal model, separating when a fact was true in the world from when the system recorded it. The design supports point-in-time retrieval and keeps personal data out of third-party memory services while avoiding context-window bloat.

entry.title: A Physics-Informed Framework for PID Tuning of Chemical Processes Using Large Language Model Agents

author.name: Zhoupeng Shou, Xiaodong Hong, Congjing Ren, Jingdai Wang, Yongrong Yang, Zuwei Liao

entry.summary: This framework formalizes how plant engineers iteratively retune PID controllers into a language-model workflow: hosted models receive closed-loop response features, diagnoses, and internal-model-control demonstrations to propose and correct gains, while a small local model is supervised fine-tuned on simulation-verified targets for on-premises deployment. It covers both large and small model settings for industrial control.

entry.title: Understanding Context Sampling in TabPFN on Small Tabular Datasets

author.name: Mohammed Abdullah

entry.summary: This empirical study examines how the choice and size of the in-context prototype set affects TabPFN predictions on small tabular datasets, testing whether larger contexts stabilize predictions, whether accuracy depends on preserving the training distribution or covering feature space, and whether expensive selection like K-means or farthest-point sampling beats random draws. It uses repeated context sampling across fifteen OpenML datasets.

entry.title: Guarding Organizations Against Malware Risk: A Novel Graph-Based Malware Detection Method

author.name: Yinan Gao, Jiarong Xu, Xiaohang Zhao, Xiao Fang

entry.summary: The authors propose a graph-based malware detector that explicitly identifies cohesive groups of basic blocks realizing meaningful program behaviors, arguing that byte-based classifiers are easy to evade and that existing program-graph models lack expressive behavioral representations. The framing is organizational cybersecurity risk in information systems.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Face-to-Speech Synthesis via Latent Space Adaptation of a Style-Diffusion TTS Model

author.name: Carlos Mu\~noz-Romero, Jose A. Gonzalez-Lopez

entry.summary: The authors synthesize plausible voices from a single static face image by training a lightweight face adapter and softly tuning upper face-encoder blocks to map face-recognition features into the style space of a frozen style-diffusion TTS model. They report high naturalness on held-out identities from an audiovisual TED-talk corpus, comparable to ground truth on an automatic mean-opinion-score predictor.

entry.title: Journey Operators for Structured Multi-Axis Composition

author.name: Mahesh Godavarti

entry.summary: This paper develops a framework in which each data item carries a small transformation per structural axis, so composition along an ordered axis is direction-sensitive while composition across independent axes is order-invariant, with paths between positions defining relative-position operators. It is a general formalism for multi-axis structure in sequences, images, trees, audio, and volumes.

entry.title: AI as Friction for Reflection Support in Ideation

author.name: Janin Koch, Xiaohan Liao, G\'ery Casiez

entry.summary: This position and design paper argues that generative creativity tools wrongly optimize for removing friction, because the act of accepting, rejecting, and reworking ideas is how designers build the rationale needed to think with and communicate their ideas, especially in group ideation. It proposes deliberately introducing friction to support reflection-in-action.

entry.title: Kairos: Numerically Robust News Recommendation under Item Cold-Start via Cholesky-based LinUCB

author.name: Finn Hertsch

entry.summary: Project Kairos handles severe item cold-start in regional news recommendation, where articles have very short lifetimes and article pools are shallow, using contextual bandits rather than data-hungry deep models. It replaces numerically fragile Sherman-Morrison inverse updates with direct rank-1 Cholesky factor updates to keep the covariance matrix positive definite under ill-conditioned data. The emphasis is numerical robustness for continuous long-running operation.

entry.title: TREA-Net: A Transferable Residual Epidemiological Adaptation Network for Dengue Incidence Forecasting

author.name: Inesh Shukla, Madhurima Panja, Tanujit Chakraborty, Chittaranjan Hens

entry.summary: TREA-Net forecasts dengue incidence in settings with little historical surveillance data by augmenting neural forecasting backbones with projections from an environmental susceptible-infected-recovered model and learning a lightweight gated residual correction transferable across regions. Pretrained zero-shot time-series models often miss local epidemiological dynamics. The hybrid mechanistic-plus-residual design targets low-data public health deployment.

entry.title: Surrogate assisted diversity estimation in neural ensemble search

author.name: Alexandr Udeneev, Petr Babkin, Oleg Bakhteev

entry.summary: This work makes neural ensemble search tractable by representing candidate architectures as directed acyclic graphs and training two independent surrogate models, one predicting individual accuracy and one estimating ensemble diversity, to guide a dual-objective search. Jointly optimizing member architectures and ensemble composition otherwise explodes the search space. Surrogate estimation avoids repeated expensive training.

entry.title: Single-Beat Cuffless Blood Pressure Estimation Using Ear-PPG and ECG with a Lightweight Hybrid Learning Framework

author.name: Kindeep K. Dhatt, Tengyue Wu, Hanbang Hua, Yayun Du

entry.summary: This wearable framework estimates blood pressure from single cardiac beats using synchronized chest ECG and ear-clip reflectance photoplethysmography, each paired with a six-axis inertial unit for motion artifact handling. Most prior cuffless approaches average over multi-second windows, an assumption violated when signals are intermittently corrupted in real-world use. The result is that discriminative blood-pressure information survives at beat-level granularity.

entry.title: Voronoi Histograms for Adaptive Vectorization of Expected Persistence Diagrams

author.name: Kaifeng Zhang, Kai Ming Ting

entry.summary: This paper vectorizes expected persistence diagrams with Voronoi-diagram-based histograms, replacing predefined smooth point transformations such as Gaussians or persistence landscapes with adaptive partition-based counting. Expected persistence diagrams already reduce the cost of computing topological features from point clouds. The tradeoff is losing smooth functional approximation in exchange for data-adaptive resolution.

entry.title: Shape-Based Inductive Bias for Glioma Grading from Tumor Contours

author.name: Puneet Velidi, Michelle F. Miranda, Farouk Nathoo, Ashery Mbilinyi, C\'edric Beaulac

entry.summary: Treating glioma grading from tumor contours as a shape problem rather than a pixel problem, this work aligns closed contours functionally, separates global deformation from residual Fourier shape, and feeds frequency-ordered tokens to a compact multilayer perceptron. On patient-disjoint five-fold cross-validation over BraTS 2020 contours the small MLP beats ResNet-18 and ViT-Tiny on balanced accuracy. It demonstrates the value of matching inductive bias to the actual signal.

entry.title: Knowledge before Reasoning: EC-Reason-Bench, a Training-Free Diagnostic Benchmark for LLM Enzyme Classification

author.name: Linyu Li, Zhi Jin, Yichi Zhang, Dongming Jin, Yuanpeng He, Huanyao Zhang, Xuan Zhang, Gadeng Luosang, Nyima Tashi

entry.summary: Diagnoses why general-purpose LLMs collapse on full enzyme commission number prediction despite getting the coarsest level right, decomposing the failure into output structure, external knowledge, reasoning, and related levers. The training-free benchmark measures how much accuracy can be restored without any weight updates.

entry.title: Credit Cards, Confusion, Computation, and Consequences: What Can We Uncover About Language Model Reasoning?

author.name: Arnav Hiray, Agam Shah, Caleb Lu, Meghaj Tarte, Harsit Mittal, Sudheer Chava

entry.summary: Releases a financial-literacy numerical reasoning benchmark of 1,800 questions derived from real credit card agreements, including first-person consumer phrasings. Finds program-of-thought prompting consistently helps, especially weaker models, and that errors stem mainly from misapplied financial rules and missed contractual conditions rather than arithmetic.

entry.title: Dissecting Sensitivity to Training Language in Self-Supervised Speech Learning Using Neural Audio Codec Tokens

author.name: Daigo Takizawa, Tomohiko Nakamura, Samuele Cornell, William Chen, Satoru Fukayama, Shinji Watanabe

entry.summary: Systematically varies the training language of a neural audio codec versus the pretraining language of a codec-based self-supervised speech model, holding the other fixed, to isolate where language sensitivity originates. Finds downstream performance is insensitive to the codec training language, implying codecs can be reused across languages without retraining.

entry.title: Knowledge-guided Disentanglement with Atomic Actions for Action Recognition

author.name: Tianci Wu, Siqi Cao, Guangming Zhu, Jiang Lu, Siyuan Wang, Longfei Zhang, Jincai Huang, Jun Sheng, Liang Zhang

entry.summary: Uses LLMs to decompose complex actions into fine-grained atomic components, then trains an action recognition model that disentangles concurrent activities with this semantic guidance. Aims to improve recognition of subtle simultaneous actions where holistic video representations fail.

entry.title: HERMES: A Hybrid Ensemble for Head-and-Neck Tumor Segmentation, TN Staging, and Recurrence-Free Survival on PET/CT

author.name: Kai Wang, Meixu Chen, Elie Nasr, Ryan Lanning, Moyed Miften

entry.summary: A containerized ensemble system for a head-and-neck cancer challenge that segments primary tumors and lymph nodes from PET/CT, then derives compact geometry features aligned with clinical staging axes to predict T/N stage and recurrence-free survival. Uses segmentation-mask-derived features instead of generic radiomics.

entry.title: Semantic-Aware Temporal Adaptation for UAV Anti-UAV Tracking

author.name: Xiaozhen Qiao, Da Zhang, Yubin Guo, Junyu Gao, Zhiyuan Zhao, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Tackles tracking an adversarial drone from a moving drone camera, where both platforms move and appearance cues are unreliable. Uses a stable language description of the target plus temporal adaptation to stabilize matching under rapid viewpoint and scale changes.

entry.title: R-SLPR: Region-based Small-to-Large Point-cloud Registration with Contrastive Learning

author.name: Yusen Wan, Zeyuan Chen, Qianshi Zou, Xu Chen

entry.summary: Reformulates registering a small partial point cloud against a much larger global reference as a region-retrieval problem followed by refinement, trained with contrastive learning. Addresses the common robotics case of severe scale mismatch and low overlap that standard learned registration assumes away.

entry.title: NeoRacer: An Open, Standardized 1:12 Scale Autonomous Race Car for Benchmarking and Education

author.name: Koneshka Bandyopadhyay, Ansh Mehta, Bassel El Mabsout, Renato Mancuso

entry.summary: NeoRacer is an open-source 1:12 scale autonomous racing platform built on a Jetson Orin Nano with LiDAR and a high-frame-rate camera, intended as a standardized, affordable benchmark and teaching vehicle. It addresses the reproducibility and access gap created by bespoke or expensive research race cars.

entry.title: SciFigQual-Bench: A Benchmark for Scientific Figure Quality Assessment with Full-Manuscript Context

author.name: Zihan Deng, Chuanzhi Xu, Huiqi Liang, Haoyang Li, Xiaozhen Zhong, Lequan Yu

entry.summary: SciFigQual-Bench evaluates scientific figures in full-manuscript context across five dimensions including clarity, layout, caption fit, context relevance, and misleading risk, going beyond visual-surface comparison of charts. It argues that image-quality benchmarks built for natural photographs or AI-generated images do not transfer to scholarly figures.

entry.title: Where Physics Meets Privacy: Federated PINNs for Privacy-Preserving Brain Tumor Biomechanical Modeling

author.name: Mahmuda Akter Sristy, Md Al-Mahfuz Chowdhury, Momota Ahsana Meem, Sajid Ahamed, Kazi Irfan Subhan

entry.summary: Combines federated learning with physics-informed neural networks that embed linear elasticity equations to model brain tumor biomechanics without pooling patient data across sites. Simulated multi-site training is used to argue for privacy-compliant tumor deformation modeling.

entry.title: Object Detection for Autonomous Driving in Chinese Rural Scenes: An Experimental Study on Real-Synthetic Data Mixing and Model Evaluation

author.name: Danning Zhu, Ziyan Lin, Jing Wu

entry.summary: Builds a mixed real and synthetic object detection dataset for Chinese rural road scenes and benchmarks thirteen detectors across different real-to-synthetic data ratios. Provides empirical guidance on data mixing strategy for underrepresented driving environments.

entry.title: Dense Soft Weighting for Radar Ego-Velocity Estimation

author.name: Atar Babgei, Chenyu Zhao, Michael Breza, Julie A. McCann

entry.summary: Replaces the usual CFAR thresholding step in radar odometry with a dense soft-weighting front end that assigns every range-Doppler cell a continuous confidence, preserving weak returns that still carry motion information. This aims at robust ego-velocity estimation where cameras and LiDAR degrade, such as smoke or darkness.

entry.title: Value Generalisation 2: The Missing Hole in AIs’ abilities

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: Argues that current language models lack a human capacity the author calls strong generalisation, and that this single gap explains puzzles such as why experts extract far more value from models than novices, why capability and failure coexist oddly, and why benchmark success has not translated into full general intelligence. It is the technical motivation post for the value generalisation agenda.

entry.title: The Human Utility Factor: A Computable Welfare Metric That Reframes AI Governance as a Constrained Optimisation Problem

author.name: Sivasathivel Kandasamy

entry.summary: Proposes the Human Utility Factor, a differentiable welfare metric combining agency, wellbeing, and economic stability as functions of automation depth, redistribution intensity, and employment coverage, yielding a closed-form optimal automation level and minimum redistribution threshold. It reframes AI governance as constrained optimization rather than qualitative principles.

entry.title: Zero-Fi: Zero-Shot Wi-Fi-Based Human Activity Recognition via Contrastive Signal-Language Alignment

author.name: Yitong Shen, Cheng Guo, Peiliang Wang, Jingzhe Zhang, Yi Sheng, Haopeng Zhang, Hongfei Xue, Yili Ren

entry.summary: Zero-Fi aligns Wi-Fi channel-state features with natural-language activity descriptions in a shared embedding space, following the contrastive vision-language recipe, so that new activity classes can be recognized without any labeled Wi-Fi samples. It targets the closed-set limitation of most Wi-Fi sensing systems.

entry.title: Collaborative Weighting with Pessimistic Critic for Mitigating Overestimation in Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Gong Gao, Xiao Lai, Ziqi Xie, Guojie Chen, Xianhui Liu, Weidong Zhao

entry.summary: This paper attacks persistent value overestimation in off-policy actor-critic learning by combining a pessimistic critic with a collaborative weighting scheme over transitions, aiming to avoid the failure mode where prioritized sampling over-emphasizes high-uncertainty transitions and amplifies bias. Evaluation targets continuous-control benchmarks.

entry.title: The Art of Not Forgetting A Local Learning Architecture for Continual Learning

author.name: Ashmith Atmuri, Yashaswini Rao Bhogarajula

entry.summary: CMP is a continual-learning architecture that encodes inputs as sparse relational codes, stores them in a two-tier competitive memory, and learns via local updates rather than end-to-end backpropagation, tested on domain-incremental byte-level language modeling. It reports substantially less backward transfer than a parameter-matched transformer trained with online elastic weight consolidation.

entry.title: Scientific Knowledge Discovery in the Age of Large Language Models

author.name: Eleni Adamidi, Serafeim Chatzopoulos, Thanasis Vergoulis

entry.summary: This book-chapter survey reviews 34 peer-reviewed studies that apply generative language models to literature retrieval and screening of candidate studies against eligibility criteria, characterizing model access, prompting and architectural choices, ground-truth sources, and evaluation practice. It was assembled from a screened pool of about 1,589 records.

entry.title: Crossing-Free Probabilistic K-Line Forecasts Without Retraining

author.name: Runyao Yu, Yuchen Tao, Yujie Chen, Wentao Wang, Derek W. Bunn

entry.summary: KQSP is a training-free, parameter-free projection that reconciles probabilistic forecasts of open, high, low, and close prices so that neither quantiles nor candlestick constraints cross, and it can be applied to the outputs of any forecasting model. Prior fixes required custom architectures, output reordering, or penalized training objectives.

entry.title: Defending Against Backdoor Attacks via Alignment Checking in Model-Contrastive Federated Learning

author.name: Hongliang Zhang, Zhongyuan Yu, Guijuan Wang, Tianqing He, Wenshuo Ma, Xiaosong Zhang, Jiguo Yu

entry.summary: FedDAB defends federated learning against backdoor attacks in two phases: a model-contrastive regularizer in the local objective to make benign updates more consistent in direction and magnitude, then an alignment check that screens each local update. The motivation is that existing defenses conflate benign heterogeneity-induced deviation with stealthy malicious updates.

entry.title: CoCaRS: Correlation Calibration-Based Redundancy Suppression for Heterogeneous Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Fengming Yu, Haiwei Pan, Kejia Zhang, Chunling Chen, Jian Guan, Baoying Ma

entry.summary: CoCaRS improves knowledge distillation between architecturally different teachers and students by calibrating feature correlations rather than simply decorrelating them, on the grounds that aggressive redundancy suppression also destroys useful structural information. It targets the representation mismatch caused by differing inductive biases.

entry.title: SciFigAlign: Scoring Scientific Figures by Fine-tuned Alignment of Visuals with Manuscript Evidence

author.name: Chuanzhi Xu, Zihan Deng, Huiqi Liang, Chengkun Yue, Zhanlin Cui, Pengfei Ye, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: SciFigAlign scores scientific figures by fine-tuning a model to align visual content with manuscript evidence, arguing that classical image-quality metrics judge perceptual appeal, CLIP-style methods judge generic image-text match, and zero-shot judges produce overly concentrated scores. The target is whether a figure legibly and faithfully supports the paper's claims.

entry.title: Neural Architecture Search for Traffic Prediction: A Survey of Methods, Challenges, and Future Directions

author.name: Truong Giang Vu, Li Yang, Richard W. Pazzi

entry.summary: A survey of neural architecture search applied to traffic prediction, covering search spaces suited to spatial-temporal structure, methods, open challenges, and cross-city generalization failures of hand-designed graph and transformer models. It argues NAS is a systematic alternative to manual architecture design in intelligent transportation systems. The contribution is organizational rather than new results.

entry.title: Learning Dynamic User Personas from Implicit Interaction Streams via Iterative Refinement

author.name: Haifeng Wu

entry.summary: IRIS learns dynamic user personas for LLM personalization purely from implicit behavioral signals in everyday conversation, refining persona representations in a prediction-driven closed loop without pairwise preference labels or demographics. It proposes an evaluation protocol based on behavior prediction, persona stability, and decision prediction. Validation is a proof-of-concept on synthetic interaction data.

entry.title: Retrospective Orthogonal Design: Response-Surface Reconstruction from Observational Data

author.name: Lawrence Fulton, Christopher Fulton, Arvind Sharma, Aleksandar Tomic

entry.summary: Retrospective Orthogonal Design reconstructs conditional mean response surfaces from observational data on a probability-balanced lattice, preserving observed cell means, completing unsupported cells, applying weighted tensor-product contrasts, and interpolating piecewise-affinely over Freudenthal polyhedra to obtain an orthogonal design matrix. The motivation is that regression estimates and sequential sums of squares become specification- and order-dependent under multicollinearity. Resolution and completion are chosen by validation with a held-out test set.

entry.title: Parameterized Fair Resource Allocation under Diversity Constraints

author.name: Keke Huang, Yik Yu Ng, Laks V. S. Lakshmanan, Xiaokui Xiao

entry.summary: Replaces hard diversity constraints in group-fair resource allocation with tunable inequality-aversion parameters inspired by economic risk models, softening the feasibility restrictions that lead to poor allocations. Applies to recommendation, housing, and course assignment settings.

entry.title: Early Failure Prediction from Near-Anomaly Detection: A Proactive Approach

author.name: L\'ea Billet (LAAS, INSA Toulouse, ANITI), Louise Trav\'e-Massuy\`es (LAAS-DISCO, Comue de Toulouse, ANITI), Elodie Chanthery (LAAS), Alexandre Gaffet

entry.summary: Introduces the notion of near-anomalies, samples near the normality boundary that are likely to become anomalous, and an unsupervised detector based on the Christoffel function to flag them early. Validated on printed-circuit-board in-circuit test data with synthetically generated near-anomaly samples.

entry.title: Symphony of Bias: Exploring Gender Associations with Musical Instruments in Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Farhan Farsi, Shayan Bali, Mohammad Heydari Rad, Negar Heidary, Donya Rooein

entry.summary: Introduces a parallel text, image, and audio dataset probing whether multimodal models reproduce cultural gender-typing of 22 musical instruments, evaluating ten models across male, female, and non-binary associations. Enables comparison of bias magnitude across modalities within the same conceptual domain.

entry.title: Generation or Judgement? A Paradigm Perspective on LLM-Based Emotion-Cause Pair Extraction in Conversation

author.name: Weijie Feng, Hongchuang Wang, Binbin Liu, Zhiyong Cheng

entry.summary: Shows that how emotion-cause pair extraction is formulated matters more than expected: pair-level judgement beats dialogue-level generation in all 18 controlled comparisons. Diagnoses the gap by showing that most relations missed by generation are still recognized when queried as explicit individual pairs.

entry.title: Lag-aware cross-hand alignment for dual-hand action segmentation

author.name: Fatemeh Ziaeetabar

entry.summary: Introduces a lightweight module that estimates time-varying delays between left- and right-hand feature streams for dual-hand action segmentation, including a learned null state that blocks transfer when no compatible cross-hand transition exists. Supervision targets are derived automatically from frame-level labels.

entry.title: Comparing the Performance of Foundation Model Derived Embeddings with Traditional Approaches for Distant Metastasis Prediction in Head and Neck Cancer

author.name: Erich Schmitz, Meixu Chen, Bowen Jing, Jing Wang

entry.summary: Compares embeddings from a medical imaging foundation model against traditional radiomics and segmentation-dependent pipelines for predicting distant metastasis risk in head and neck cancer. The goal is to remove the need for expert tumor delineation in prognostic modeling.

entry.title: When Fish Look Alike: Tracking Identities with Dual-branch Elasticity

author.name: Vran Lee, Xin Liu, Yijie Wei, Yeqiang Liu, Hwa Liang Leo, Zhenbo Li

entry.summary: A multi-object tracker for dense homogeneous targets such as schooling fish that avoids expensive re-identification networks by using an adaptive geometric correspondence association mechanism. Designed for edge deployment where appearance features degrade under occlusion and clustering.

entry.title: Controlled Experiments on Lane Changing by Transitional Autonomous Vehicle: Dataset and Behavioral Insights

author.name: Abhinav Sharma, Md Abdullah Al Hasan, Danjue Chen, George F. List

entry.summary: Releases a controlled field dataset of 78 mandatory lane-change trials by a partially automated vehicle on a public road, with RTK-GNSS trajectories characterizing lead and lag gap evolution and collision risk during the maneuver. It supplies rare, repeatable behavioral ground truth for modeling mixed human-automated traffic.

entry.title: Value Generalisation 3: Pre-aligned AIs

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: The third post in a series proposes pre-aligned AI, systems designed so that moral behavior generalizes alongside capabilities because values are bound to empirical concepts that improve with the world model. The stated ambition is inverting the usual alignment tax so that careful actors gain rather than lose from capability increases.

entry.title: How a medical database developed at MIT evolved into a global standard of data-sharing

author.name: Emma Foehringer Merchant | Institute for Medical Engineering and Science

entry.summary: Traces how an MIT and Beth Israel effort begun in 1975 to digitize and share arrhythmia recordings grew into a widely used open medical data resource and a template for clinical data sharing. It highlights how shared, annotated datasets accelerate downstream biomedical machine learning.

entry.title: Optimizing Sensor Placement for Hydrogen Leak Detection in Enclosed Infrastructure: A Comparative Study Using CFD-informed Genetic Algorithm and DeepSets Neural Surrogate

author.name: Fangnian Wang, Nicholas Tan Jerome, Thomas Jordan, Frank Simon

entry.summary: Combines CFD simulation of 180 hydrogen leak scenarios in an enclosed garage with genetic algorithm optimization and a DeepSets neural surrogate to place detection sensors proactively rather than reactively. Compares the surrogate-accelerated approach against direct CFD-informed optimization.

entry.title: Field Codes for Distributed Coupling Samplers and Certified Empirical Transport

author.name: Hung Mai, Hai Nguyen, Luong Doan, Ngoc Vu, Khanh Nguyen, Nhung Duong, Tuan Do

entry.summary: Formulates communication tasks for empirical optimal transport and gives a compiler that turns any approximate transport field into an exact-marginal sampler carrying a scalar certificate bounding the Wasserstein distance. Shows certificate accuracy depends on the public target-partition diameter while field error controls residual communication only under a margin condition.

entry.title: Detecting seizure onset and offset times using human intelligence: A critical-transitions-based approach

author.name: Andrew Flynn, Cian McCafferty, Klaus Lehnertz, Fran\c{c}ois David, Vincenzo Crunelli, Gordon Lightbody, Sebastian Wieczorek

entry.summary: Proposes a seizure onset and offset detector grounded in the theory of critical transitions rather than opaque learned classifiers, avoiding heavy preprocessing. Evaluates agreement with expert annotations via ROC analysis on voltage recordings.

entry.title: DIRECT: Direct Decoding for Efficient and Aligned Sequence Labeling with Large Language Models

author.name: Yilei Wang, Jiaxin Gan, Kexuan Zhang, Ling Li, Wentao Zhang, Peichao Lai

entry.summary: Improves LLM-based sequence labeling with preference optimization after supervised fine-tuning plus constrained decoding that enforces fixed output formats and restricts predictions to candidate label sets. A template-filling scheme generates only label tokens to cut inference cost.

entry.title: Risk-Aware Motion Planning with Learned Trajectory Primitives and Probabilistic Safety Assessment

author.name: Marc Kaufeld, Dian Zhuang, Johannes Betz

entry.summary: Combines a radial basis function network that generates jerk-minimal candidate trajectories with analytic collision-probability scoring and optimization-based refinement for urban autonomous driving. The learned primitives shrink the MPC search space, cutting solver cost while retaining probabilistic risk awareness.

entry.title: FleetScape: A Mixed Reality Sandtable for Spatial Supervision and Control of Scalable Drone Fleets

author.name: Peisen Xu, J\'er\'emie Garcia, Peter Cleveland, Ooi Wei Tsang, Christophe Jouffrais

entry.summary: FleetScape is a mixed-reality sandtable interface for supervising drone fleets, externalizing mission, safety, and environmental layers spatially and supporting fluid handoff between manual intervention and autonomy. It is evaluated with a high-fidelity building inspection simulation.

entry.title: Value Generalisation 1: a Research and Deployment Program

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: Outlines a proposed research and deployment program on value generalisation, the ability of a system to correctly extend human values to genuinely novel situations, and seeks collaborators and funding. The author leans toward a commercial vehicle on the grounds that purely academic alignment techniques tend to be ignored or stripped for capability gains.

entry.title: A Methodology for Designing Knowledge-Driven Missions for Robots

author.name: Guillermo GP-Lenza, Carmen DR. Pita-Romero, Miguel Fernandez-Cortizas, Pascual Campoy

entry.summary: Presents a methodology for building knowledge graphs into ROS 2 robotic missions, covering condition definition, task structuring, planning, graph representation, and high-level mission specification. Demonstrated on a simulated drone search-and-rescue scenario in the Aerostack2 framework.

entry.title: Weight and Height Estimation from a Single Human Image Captured in the Wild

author.name: Hira Yaseen, Arif Mahmood, Waqas Sultani

entry.summary: Explores single and multi-task deep networks for estimating weight, height, and body mass index from a single in-the-wild image, dealing with variation in pose, camera geometry, and background. Positions BMI estimation as a health-relevant computer vision task.

entry.title: Enhancing Automated Machine Learning via Homogeneous Train-Test Splitting Methods

author.name: Yearn Tan Yin Tze, Charles Grellois

entry.summary: This paper compares random, stratified, Kennard-Stone, Duplex, and SPXY train-test splitting across fifteen UCI datasets, measuring distributional similarity with chi-square, Kolmogorov-Smirnov, and maximum mean discrepancy tests, and examines the downstream effect on AutoML model evaluation. Geometry-based splits produced more homogeneous partitions than random splitting under imbalance and clustering. The concern is that split choice silently distorts reported model quality.

entry.title: Stable and Budget-Feasible Coalition Formation for Clustered Federated Learning: A Hedonic Potential-Game Approach

author.name: Cengis Hasan

entry.summary: Models clustered federated learning as a hedonic coalition-formation game with transferable surplus and monetary transfers, so clusters are sustainable only if participants prefer their assignment and payments stay budget feasible. Shows the symmetric allocation case is an exact potential game with guaranteed Nash-stable partitions and converging better-response dynamics.

entry.title: Where Detectors Fail: Closing the Tail-Domain Gap with Expert-Guided Mutual Distillation

author.name: Xuan Feng, Guihong Liu, Tianlong Gu, Shuai Zhao, Xuemin Wang, Chenzhong Bin, Yang Liu, Bo An

entry.summary: Improves cross-domain generalization of multimodal fake news detection by learning what evidence to trust at input, representation, and decision stages, including coherence-based input calibration and expert-guided distillation. Prototype-anchored domain-specific students learn mutually to handle tail domains.

entry.title: Convex Collision-Free Regions

author.name: Tomoyo Kikuchi, Takashi Kanai

entry.summary: Proposes explicitly constructing local convex feasible regions from mesh edge-edge and vertex-face configurations to guarantee non-penetration in deformable body simulation, decoupled from any particular nonlinear solver. This improves robustness for secondary collisions and codimensional contacts relative to implicit feasibility formulations.

entry.title: The EU Energy Performance of Buildings Directive, but make it Biosecure

author.name: Kate Delbeke

entry.summary: Analyzes the EU Energy Performance of Buildings Directive, which for the first time writes indoor environmental quality into law, and argues its implementing regulations largely ignore the link between ventilation and airborne pathogen transmission. It identifies a concrete policy window for embedding biosecurity considerations into building standards.

entry.title: Sim2Win: A Team-Agnostic, Event-Based Pre-Match Outcome Prediction and Tactical Profiling System for Football

author.name: Mouad Zemzoumi, Amine Abouaomar

entry.summary: Sim2Win predicts football match outcomes from team-agnostic tactical profiles built from rolling event data across 178 teams, clustering playstyles and training classifiers on tactical matchup representations. It reframes outcome prediction as tactical decision support that generalizes to unseen teams.

entry.title: ServerlessT2I: Efficient Text-to-Image Workflow Serving on a Serverless Platform

author.name: Xiaoxiao Jiang, Suyi Li, Sheng Yao, Tianyu Feng, Lingyun Yang, Dapeng Nie, Haoran Yang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.26566v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) workflows are increasingly deployed on serverless platforms because users often compose customized workflows and invoke them inte...

entry.title: Searching for Robust Augmentations to Improve Out-of-Domain Generalization in Dermoscopic Skin Cancer Classification

author.name: Alexander Kozachok, Ilya Latyshev, Evgeny Karpulevich, Elena Kozachok, Egor Ushakov, Oleg Samovarov

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.26765v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Background/Objectives: Dermoscopic skin lesion classifiers often lose accuracy under domain shift across imaging devices, illumination, and capture a...

entry.title: MediaWiki Code2Code Search: Neural Retrieval for the Semantic Discovery of Open-Source Software Entities

author.name: Francesco Tosoni

entry.summary: This system indexes about 1.29 million functions, types, and templates across more than 2,500 MediaWiki repositories to support code-to-code semantic search based on computational intent, using a split architecture that separates GPU-heavy offline indexing from CPU-only serving with a compressed FAISS index. The reported index is dramatically smaller than a flat alternative.

entry.title: ScratchSim: A Procedural Synthetic Data Pipeline for Surface Scratch Detection

author.name: Paul Julius K\"uhn, Saptarshi Neil Sinha, Tiago Kleist, Richard Hoffmann, Arjan kuijper, Michael Weinmann

entry.summary: ScratchSim is a procedural Blender-based rendering pipeline that generates large volumes of automatically annotated synthetic surface-scratch data with configurable materials, camera modes, and domain randomization. The authors compare synthetic-only, real-only, mixed, and synthetic-pretraining strategies across two objects and three lightweight edge-deployable detectors.

entry.title: Universality and Approximation Rates of Graph Neural Networks with Random Features

author.name: Lukas Gonon, Thilo Meyer-Brandis, Niklas Weber

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.26699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate message-passing graph neural networks with random node features. Random node features are known to enhance the expressiveness of graph n...

entry.title: Domain adaptation for handwriting trajectory reconstruction from IMU sensors

author.name: Florent Imbert, Romain Tavenard, Yann Soullard, Eric Anquetil

entry.summary: A companion study on sensor-equipped digital pens tackles the domain gap between adult and child handwriting, where similar traces produce very different inertial signals because of differences in writing speed and gesture confidence. Domain adaptation techniques are investigated to make trajectory reconstruction work for children in classroom learning settings. The motivation is educational handwriting support tools.

entry.title: Few-Shot Open-Set Audio Classification via Transductive Prototype Refinement and Class Logit Enhancement

author.name: Tianyan Deng, Yanxiong Li, Rui Gao, Jiahao Du

entry.summary: Tackles few-shot open-set audio classification by weighting query samples with a latent inlierness score during transductive prototype refinement, so likely unknown-class samples contaminate prototypes less. Adds decoupled scoring and logit enhancement over a frozen audio encoder.

entry.title: No Data Is Not No Risk: Visibility Aware Graph-Based Inference of Business Conduct Risk

author.name: Tsuyoshi Iwata, Johannes Laurmaa, Ryohei Hisano

entry.summary: Frames corporate misconduct risk prediction as positive-unlabeled node classification over an ownership graph, arguing that absent incident reports often reflect low media visibility rather than genuine low risk. Tests whether inter-firm relations improve prediction of future recorded incidents for low-visibility firms.

entry.title: Investigating reservoir computing for branch predictionin pipelined processors using emerging CMOS memristor devices

author.name: Harvey Samuel George Johnson, Sendy Phang

entry.summary: Explores implementing reservoir computing with emerging memristor devices for CPU branch prediction, developing a design framework in industry-standard hardware description languages. Verifies the reservoir on sequence detection before benchmarking branch-prediction accuracy on standard CPU workloads.

entry.title: Steering Instruction Hierarchies at Inference Time

author.name: Siqi Zeng, Sewoong Lee, Han Zhao, Julia Hockenmaier

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.26228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Instruction hierarchies are a core safety assumption of language model deployment: higher priority inputs, such as system prompts, should override conf...

entry.title: Evaluating Prompt Scope and Demonstration Similarity in Local LLM Machine Translation

author.name: Mihael Arcan

entry.summary: Studies how prompt scope (one target language versus several at once) and demonstration selection affect translation quality for small locally run instruction-tuned models across nine EU languages on FLORES devtest. Compares against dedicated OPUS-style machine translation baselines for English into Romance and Germanic languages.

entry.title: When Does Span-Guided Detoxification Help? Human Preferences and Evaluator Diagnostics in a Controlled Comparison

author.name: Kyungwon Park

entry.summary: Compares span-guided detoxification, which restricts edits to annotated harmful spans, against unguided rewriting in a blinded human evaluation on curated and HateXplain inputs. Finds a trade-off rather than a winner: localized edits are preferred when they preserve stance, while broader rewrites are preferred when fuller mitigation is needed.

entry.title: Dual-Path LLM Reasoning for Multimodal Few-Shot Knowledge Graph Completion

author.name: Jinlan Liu, Zhiying Tu, Yongchao Xing, Yicheng Liu, Bolin Zhang, Dianbo Sui, Dianhui Chu, Hongliang Sun

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-path framework for multimodal few-shot knowledge graph completion that combines multimodal LLM type priors with factual support structure to build a calibrated relation graph. Explicitly aims to exploit LLM priors while suppressing hallucinated or noisy evidence for emerging entities and relations.

entry.title: Making benchmarks outputs directly useful for AI safety and security

author.name: Pierre Peigné

entry.summary: Suggests that as benchmarks saturate, evaluation tasks should be redesigned so the work models do while being tested is itself useful for safety and security, such as hardening sandboxes and trusted execution environments or reducing overhead of zero-knowledge proofs of training. The proposal frames red-team and blue-team style evaluations as dual-purpose infrastructure.

entry.title: Gene regulatory innovations from transposable elements in primate cerebellum development

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature Communications study reporting that transposable elements contributed gene-regulatory innovations during primate cerebellum development, surfaced through a machine-learning subject feed. No abstract text was included in the provided record, so the computational methods and specific findings cannot be assessed here.

entry.title: A Picture Says Thousands of Words - Harnessing Dermal Exposure Data from Images through Hybrid Deep Learning for Enhanced Safety Assessment

author.name: Hua Qian, Manisha Kotha, Tuan Tran, Jennifer Shin, Haining Zheng

entry.summary: Uses Mask R-CNN to isolate human subjects in 170 indoor painting images and a color-based algorithm to segment exposed skin, producing exposed-skin ratios that agree with human estimates about eighty percent of the time. The goal is scalable semi-quantitative dermal exposure assessment for occupational safety.

entry.title: Multimodal fusion of visual and morphometric features for avian bone classification

author.name: Nevio Dubbini, Lisa Yeomans, Marco Pavia, Ramazan Parmaksiz, Ayse Atas Hooglugt, Gabriele Gattiglia, Beatrice Demarchi

entry.summary: This proof-of-concept fuses convolutional image features with osteometric measurements to classify bird bones by skeletal element and taxonomic family, using more than 10,000 museum images segmented automatically with a two-stage BiRefNet and SAM2 pipeline. It targets zooarchaeological identification, where expert labor is a bottleneck.

entry.title: AtmosERC: Modeling Dialogue-Level Affective Atmosphere for Emotion Recognition in Conversation

author.name: Weijie Feng, Tongwei Zhang, Binbin Liu, Zhiyong Cheng

entry.summary: Models a dialogue-level affective atmosphere as a latent tendency shaping utterance emotions, using a relation-aware graph extractor over utterance and speaker nodes to filter heterogeneous context signals. Applies the estimated atmosphere to improve emotion recognition in conversation.

entry.title: Global Sensitive-Based Input Shaping for UAV-Payload Precision Motion Control

author.name: Karan Baker, Sanjay Maharjan, Tariq Hlayel, Oladapo Ogunbodede, Dutch Dunphy, Adrian Stein

entry.summary: Designs input shapers for suspended-payload drone transport using global sensitivity analysis and Shapley value attribution to systematically allocate robustness against uncertain payload mass and cable length. Simulations compare against non-robust, robust, and minimax baselines.

entry.title: An Attention-Based Framework for Alzheimers Disease Classification Using Resting-State fMRI

author.name: Harshiddhi Pathak, Gowtham Reddy N, Mrinal Acharya, Manjunatha Mahadevappa

entry.summary: This work classifies Alzheimer's disease from resting-state fMRI by treating brain regions as tokens and applying transformer self-attention directly to functional connectivity matrices, aiming to capture long-range inter-regional dependencies that handcrafted connectivity features miss. It reports improvements over conventional machine learning baselines.

entry.title: Lightweight Image Classification of Raptor Species for Edge Devices: Rare-Species Dataset Expansion via Video Frame Extraction, Knowledge Distillation, and TensorRT Deployment

author.name: Takeshi Nishikawa

entry.summary: Applies knowledge distillation from a DINOv2-L teacher into small vision backbones for classifying raptor species on edge hardware, with the goal of reducing bird collisions at wind turbines. The authors expand a rare-species dataset via video-frame extraction and report macro recall around 0.935 under a leakage-aware group split, deployed via TensorRT.

entry.title: Harnessing Large Language Models for Intelligent Resource Allocation in the Internet of Everything

author.name: Haijun Zhang, Zhuojun Duan, Zijun Wu, Xu Ma, Yuzheng Ren

entry.summary: Proposes using large models as semantic reasoners for dynamic task and resource scheduling across heterogeneous Internet of Everything devices, integrating task semantics, network state, and constraints into a scheduling decision model. Positioned as a vision-plus-mechanism paper for AI-native networks.

entry.title: An Informativeness-based Clustered Federated Learning Method for Reliable Traffic Prediction in Managed Wi-Fi Networks

author.name: Luca Barbieri, Gianluca Fontanesi, Lorenzo Galati Giordano, Alfonso Fernandez Duran, Thorsten Wild

entry.summary: Proposes a clustered federated learning pipeline for predicting access-point traffic in managed Wi-Fi networks, using a two-stage procedure that generates candidate clusterings and filters them by informativeness criteria. Aims to group access points whose data distributions justify a shared model.

entry.title: Online Handwriting Trajectory Reconstruction from Kinematic Sensors using Temporal Convolutional Network

author.name: Wassim Swaileh, Florent Imbert, Yann Soullard, Romain Tavenard, Eric Anquetil

entry.summary: Builds a temporal convolutional pipeline that reconstructs online handwriting trajectories from the kinematic sensors of a digital pen, explicitly handling the sampling-rate mismatch between pen sensors and the tablet providing ground truth. Enables digital capture of writing on arbitrary surfaces.

entry.title: Enhancing Generative Information Extraction with Two-step Validation: A Product Attribute Use Case

author.name: Yi-Sheng Hsu, Nermeen Abou Baker, Uwe Handmann

entry.summary: Applies generative information extraction to product attribute extraction for digital product passports, where labeled domain data is scarce, and adds a two-step validation stage to filter unreliable generated outputs. Explicitly targets efficiency, generalization, and data-privacy constraints of on-premise deployment.

entry.title: Interpretable Image-Level Acne Severity Grading via EfficientNet-B0 Transfer Learning and Grad-CAM

author.name: Sophie Zeng, Sean Kalaycioglu, Collin Hong, Haipeng Xie

entry.summary: Fine-tunes an ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet-B0 to grade acne severity into four clinical classes on a public dataset, reporting roughly 93 percent test accuracy with Grad-CAM visualizations for interpretability. Positioned as a consistency aid for clinical grading and trial endpoints.

entry.title: Time-delay Control Using a New Nonlinear Adaptive Law for Cable-Driven Robots

author.name: Wenbo Gao, Yaoyao Wang, Jiawang Chen, Wenliang Zhang, Hanzhuo Wang

entry.summary: Presents a time-delay-estimation-based adaptive fractional-order nonsingular terminal sliding mode controller for cable-driven manipulators, whose main new ingredient is an adaptive law with an exponential term in the gain update. The aim is precise model-free tracking despite low stiffness and time-varying disturbances.

entry.title: Compactly supported radial basis functions as probability density functions

author.name: Sergio D\'iaz-Elbal (University of Almer\'ia), Andrei Mart\'inez-Finkelshtein (University of Almer\'ia, Baylor University), Dar\'io Ramos-L\'opez (University of Almer\'ia)

entry.summary: Explores compactly supported radial basis functions, especially Wendland kernels, as a parametric family of probability densities and derives closed-form moments and cumulative distribution functions for univariate and conditional cases. This extends a standard approximation-theory tool into density modeling where compact support can be advantageous.

entry.title: Isn't it a threat to reject unfair offers in the Ultimatum Game?

author.name: Sunny from QAD

entry.summary: Notes a tension in common decision-theoretic advice: rejecting unfair ultimatum-game offers is justified by the same logic used to condemn threats, since both work by making a costly commitment that changes another agent's incentives. The post asks what principled line separates legitimate commitment from coercion.

entry.title: Characterizing Human-Likeness in AI Generated Poetry: A Zero-shot Classification Study

author.name: A. N. Biswas, T. Tabassum, A. A. Shohid, R. M. Mou, A. A. Esha, F. Sadeque, A. Ahmed

entry.summary: Studies which attributes make AI-generated English poetry read as human-like, using zero-shot classification to probe how modern detectors respond to poetic text. Motivated by evidence that poems are the hardest generated form for detectors to flag.

entry.title: Intellectual Property

author.name: Nina Panickssery

entry.summary: A short noir-style fiction piece in which a private investigator takes a case about a suspiciously efficient competitor selling near-identical reinforcement learning environments. It uses the RL-environment vendor economy as a setting to gesture at questions of imitation, espionage, and intellectual property in the AI supply chain.

entry.title: Rethinking the "Second Brain": From Storing Information to Structuring Reasoning

author.name: Sergei Simonovi

entry.summary: Argues that personal knowledge tools store information but do not help structure reasoning, and proposes typing notes as problems, hypotheses, or conclusions and typing links with meanings such as supports or contradicts. The author built a prototype to test whether explicit typing makes reasoning inspectable or just adds friction.

entry.title: What use is prompting if there's ASI?

author.name: wp

entry.summary: Uses computer chess as an analogy for what human expertise becomes once systems exceed human ability, noting that top engines are not really promptable and that human players became consumers of intelligence rather than co-creators. It asks whether prompting and human direction retain value in domains where models surpass their users.

entry.title: The High-Control Dynamics at MAPLE

author.name: Kyle Hubbard

entry.summary: A long first-person account arguing that a Vermont monastic community connected to parts of the AI-risk-adjacent rationalist scene functions as a high-control group, drawing on the author's own membership and interviews with dozens of former residents. It is community-safety documentation rather than technical work.

entry.title: Classification of Disease from Lungs X-ray Images using VGG16, VGG19 and ResNet50 Models

author.name: Nand Lal Yadav, Rajesh Kumar, Satyendra Singh, Sudhakar Singh

entry.summary: The study trains and compares VGG16, VGG19, and ResNet50 on chest X-rays to classify pneumonia, tuberculosis, lung cancer, and normal lungs. It reports comparative accuracies across the three backbones.

entry.title: Automated Multilabel Mpox Research Classification with Explainable Transformer Models

author.name: Tanjim Taharat Aurpa

entry.summary: This study performs multilabel topic classification of about 14,590 Mpox research articles into categories such as outbreak, vaccination, and epidemiology, comparing transformer models and adding explainability analysis.
