entry.title: Nesterov acceleration in optimizing over probability measures

author.name: Jiaqi Tang, Qin Li, Wilfrid Gangbo

entry.summary: Develops heavy-ball and Nesterov-style accelerated optimization directly over the space of probability measures with Wasserstein geometry, proving non-asymptotic rates matching Euclidean counterparts. Rates are given in both iteration count and number of particles used to represent the distributions.

entry.title: Context-Adaptive Inference: A Unified Statistical and Foundation-Model View

author.name: Yue Yao, Caleb N. Ellington, Jingyun Jia, Baiheng Chen, Dong Liu, Rikhil Rao, Jiaqi Wang, Samuel Wales-McGrath, Yixin Yang, Zhiyuan Li, Eric P. Xing, Ben Lengerich

entry.summary: This survey-style article unifies context-adaptive inference across statistics, contextual parameter generation, and modern foundation-model behaviors such as in-context learning, retrieval augmentation, and mixture-of-experts routing. It argues these are instances of one mechanism: specializing parameters or computation per input context.

entry.title: Offline-to-Online Creative Optimization with Generative Models and Adaptive Testing

author.name: Kevin Lee, Benjamin Letham, Zhiyuan Jerry Lin, Elodie Samson, Eric Onofrey, Poppy Zhang, Shawndra Hill, Eytan Bakshy

entry.summary: A Meta team deploys an offline-to-online workflow for ad creative optimization in which a predictive model trained on historical A/B tests acts as an inference-time critic ranking and refining generative-model outputs, before a final adaptive online experiment. They report results from a 50-arm field experiment.

entry.title: Efficiency Matters in Autonomous Research

author.name: Haiqian Yang, Yuan Cao

entry.summary: Argues that autonomous research agents should be scored on search efficiency, not just final result quality, and proposes metrics that account for the budget consumed to reach a solution. Motivated by the shift from cheap verification domains like math and code toward science where each evaluation may require costly experiments.

entry.title: Beyond Scale and Generation: Understanding Language Model-based Entity Matching

author.name: Zeyu Zhang, Xue Li, Iacer Calixto, Paul Groth, Sebastian Schelter

entry.summary: Runs a controlled factorial study of 1,215 fine-tuning runs across bi-encoder, cross-encoder, and generative matcher architectures using three Qwen3 variants and sizes on nine entity-matching datasets, to disentangle architecture from backbone, pretraining objective, and scale. Finds model variant rather than raw size explains much of the performance difference, and also reports cross-dataset transfer and compute cost.

entry.title: Novel Claim or D\'ej\`a Vu? Rethinking "Contamination-Free'' Dynamic Evaluation for Multimodal Automated Fact-Checking

author.name: Haorui He, Xinwen Chen, Dacheng Wen, Reynold Cheng, Francis C. M. Lau, Yupeng Li

entry.summary: Questions the assumption that dynamic benchmarks built from post-cutoff claims are contamination-free, empirically probing both a leading static multimodal fact-checking benchmark and a newly built late-2025 claim set. Finds contamination risks persist and proposes rethinking how contamination-free evaluation is established.

entry.title: Indic DiarBench: A Multilingual Joint Diarization and ASR Benchmark for Indian Languages

author.name: Deovrat Mehendale, Aditya Mehndiratta, Dhruv Rathi, Kaushal Bhogale, Mitesh M. Khapra

entry.summary: Releases a speaker diarization plus ASR benchmark covering all 22 scheduled Indian languages with roughly 108 hours of human-corrected, speaker-attributed multi-speaker audio from meetings, far-field, and in-the-wild recordings. Baselines include commercial speech APIs and multimodal LLMs, capturing code-mixing, dialect variation, and overlap.

entry.title: Masked Distillation: Internalizing the Chain-of-Thought in Language Models

author.name: Durgesh Kalwar, Vardhan Palod, Subbarao Kambhampati

entry.summary: Masked distillation trains a student model to predict only the final answer while the teacher's chain-of-thought tokens are masked, aiming to internalize reasoning computation into weights rather than emitting long traces. Motivated by the observation that trace length and trace correctness are poorly coupled to answer correctness.

entry.title: The Best Programming Language for Tokenmaxxing: An Investigation of Coding Agent Behavior Across Programming Languages

author.name: Zixuan Wu, Carolyn Jane Anderson, Arjun Guha

entry.summary: Measures how many tokens coding agents burn to solve difficulty-matched problems in Python, Java, Rust and OCaml across five recent models, finding large and consistent cross-language cost differences. Trajectory analysis attributes the gap to repeated noncompiling attempts in less familiar languages.

entry.title: ClinFusion: A Vision-Centric Multimodal LLM System for Holistic Medical Understanding

author.name: Hangjie Yuan, Yichen Qian, Zhiwei Tang, Xianzhe Xu, Lirong Wu, Sicheng Yang, Jinwang Wang, Pengju Wang, Zhitao Zeng, Yizeng Han, Yan Xing, Shengxuan Luo, Tao Feng, Qing Xie, Weigen Yao, Yi Yang, Zuozhu Liu, Jiasheng Tang, Shaocheng Wang, Jitao Wang, Jiahong Dong, Weihua Chen, Feng Xu, Fan Wang

entry.summary: ClinFusion is a vision-centric medical multimodal LLM with a cascaded encoder architecture that unifies 2D and native 3D medical image understanding, paired with radiologist-aligned fine-grained factuality evaluation. Aims at holistic clinical understanding across heterogeneous imaging modalities.

entry.title: Face Age Verification Vulnerabilities Under Simple Appearance Manipulations

author.name: Ioannis Sarridis, Ioannis Kompatsiaris, Symeon Papadopoulos

entry.summary: Systematically tests seven age-estimation models, including vision-language and multimodal LLMs, against trivial appearance manipulations like drawn stubble or lipstick across three datasets. Drawn beard stubble flips up to 61 percent of correctly identified minors into false adult classifications, exposing a serious weakness in automated age assurance.

entry.title: CameraAnything: Refilming Videos with Arbitrary Camera Control

author.name: Yixuan Li, Yanhong Zeng, Ka Leong Cheng, Jiayi Zhu, Hanlin Wang, Wen Wang, Yihao Meng, Hao Ouyang, Qiuyu Wang, Yue Yu, ZiDong Wang, Yiyuan Zhang, Yujun Shen, Dahua Lin

entry.summary: CameraAnything is a unified video editing framework that jointly controls camera extrinsics, focal length, and native resolution using per-pixel Plucker ray injection with resolution-aware 3D rotary embeddings in self-attention. It avoids the expensive 3D reconstruction that prior full-camera-control methods require.

entry.title: Generative Video Compression with Adaptive Score Distillation

author.name: Naifu Xue, Zhaoyang Jia, Haosen Li, Zihan Zheng, Jiahao Li, Bin Li, Xiaoyi Zhang, Qi Meng, Yuan Zhang, Yan Lu

entry.summary: GenVC is presented as the first video diffusion model trained from scratch specifically for compression rather than adapted from text-to-video generation, operating in pixel space with a global-to-local hierarchy and adaptive score distillation for fast inference. It targets ultra-low-bitrate generative video coding.

entry.title: LabRobFail: A Benchmark for Robotic Failure Analysis in Chemical Self-driving Laboratories

author.name: Haobo Wang, Baoli Sun, Anqi Zou, Dongsheng Huang, Zelin Lv, Ning Wang, Rui Li, Dongzhan Zhou, Weiyu Guo, Zhihui Wang, Wanli Ouyang

entry.summary: LabRobFail is a failure-centric simulator, dataset and benchmark for robotic chemistry labs, injecting controllable control-, physics- and semantic-level failures to produce over 20,000 trajectories across 70+ scenarios. It addresses the scarcity of failure data needed to make self-driving laboratories safe and reliable.

entry.title: MSE loss does not generate superposition

author.name: philh

entry.summary: Argues that mean squared error is a poor loss for toy models of superposition, since it fails to produce the superposition phenomenon researchers aim to study, and connects this to the effective loss actually used in the original toy models work. A methodological correction for interpretability experiments.

entry.title: Do VLMs Read or Rewrite? On Transcription Faithfulness in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Gwang Gook Lee, Kenan Emir Ak, Jay Mohta, Yan Xu, Dimitrios Dimitriadis

entry.summary: Introduces FaithC4, a multilingual benchmark of 1,455 documents perturbed by scrambling and character substitution, to test whether vision-language models faithfully transcribe imperfect text or silently rewrite it into plausible-looking text. Fifteen systems spanning general VLMs, OCR-specialized VLMs and classical OCR pipelines show markedly different degradation profiles.

entry.title: Deconstructing Off-Policy Ratios: Entropy-Scaled Trust Regions for Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Guanqun Zhao, Zijun Xie, Binbin Zheng, Enlei Gong, Jiafeng Lu, Yehan Yang, Aoqi Hu, Zeyu Chen

entry.summary: Analyzes why asynchronous RL for LLM post-training destabilizes, showing that the natural scale of importance ratios varies systematically with token entropy so uniform clipping thresholds are miscalibrated. Low-entropy tokens amplify train-inference discrepancy into sampling noise, motivating entropy-scaled trust regions to prevent policy collapse under stale data.

entry.title: The Intruder Threshold: A Spectral Law for LoRA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Peng Xie

entry.summary: Derives a per-layer critical update strength that predicts, from the pretrained weight spectrum alone and with no fitted parameters, when LoRA fine-tuning will create intruder singular directions that drive catastrophic forgetting. The prediction is tested across dense transformers, a state-space model, a mixture-of-experts model, and an encoder-decoder.

entry.title: Test-Time Coverage: Test-Conditioned Data Curation for Deployment-Aware Learning

author.name: Nadine Chang, Maying Shen, Shizhe Diao, Jialiang Wang, Jingde Chen, Thomas Breuel, Pavlo Molchanov, Rafid Mahmood, Jose M. Alvarez

entry.summary: TTCov curates training data conditioned on the deployment test distribution rather than on training-side heuristics, building an atlas of LLM-generated atomic propositions describing deployment-relevant concepts and then matching coverage and distribution. It shifts test-time adaptation from weight updates to data selection before training.

entry.title: Characterizing Arbitrary Lindbladian Dynamics with a Few Pauli Measurements

author.name: Taiqi Zhou, Weiyuan Gong

entry.summary: Gives a protocol to reconstruct an arbitrary sparse Markovian (Lindbladian) generator, including Hamiltonian terms and jump operator coefficients, using only product Pauli state preparation, uninterrupted forward evolution, and product Pauli measurements. It avoids ancillas, entangled probes, and mid-circuit control while going beyond Pauli-diagonal noise.

entry.title: Grokking on the Weight-Decay Clock: A Rate Hierarchy from Softly Broken Symmetries

author.name: Taeyoung Kim

entry.summary: This paper gives an exactly solvable account of grokking as slow weight-decay-driven relaxation within a distinguished grokking subspace of the empirical null space, where training predictions are unchanged so weight decay is the only restoring force. It derives exact discrete- and continuous-time laws for linear models and extends locally to nonlinear networks.

entry.title: Between Suppression and Collapse: Evaluating Narrative Unlearning with LENS

author.name: Viktoriia Makovska, George Fletcher

entry.summary: Introduces LENS, an evaluation protocol testing whether machine unlearning can suppress disinformation-aligned narrative frames across direct, attributed, contrastive, and abstract probing levels, using two geopolitical narratives and four multilingual 12B-class models. Frames the outcome as a spectrum between shallow suppression and broader capability collapse.

entry.title: Beyond a Global Norm: Personalizing Toxicity Sensitivity in Language Models Without Retraining

author.name: Rares A. C. Diaconescu, Iulia Slanina, Alina Florea, Andrei B. Trache, Miruna E. Coroi, Anne Arzberger, Jie Yang, Enrico Liscio

entry.summary: Compares training-free methods for personalizing toxicity thresholds to individual users across pre-decoding prompting, in-decoding token, logit, and representation steering, and post-decoding reranking, benchmarked against sensitivity targets from the PRISM dataset. All approaches cut alignment error substantially but expose a trade-off among alignment, personalization, and fluency.

entry.title: Formally Verified Synthesizable Floating-Point Data Types in ARCH HDL

author.name: Shuqing Zhao

entry.summary: Reports end-to-end formal verification of IEEE-754 float32 and bfloat16 arithmetic for ARCH, a hardware description language designed to be generated by language models, rendering each operator once into synthesizable SystemVerilog, an SMT model, and a Lean 4 proof model. A Yosys-to-SMT equivalence miter machine-checks that the emitted hardware matches the verified model for all 24 operators.

entry.title: Co-Harness: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Model Weights for LLM Agents

author.name: Zhengyu Chen, Teng Xiao, Huaisheng Zhu, Yige Yuan, Luan Zhang, Jingang Wang

entry.summary: Co-Harness jointly optimizes an agent's runtime harness (prompts, tools, skills, memory, middleware) and its model weights during post-training, alternating between harness improvement driven by an LLM critic and model updates. Targets the mismatch caused by training agents under a frozen scaffold.

entry.title: MegaSlide-DiT: Memory-Centric Adaptation and Deformable Local Attention for Efficient Video Diffusion

author.name: Jiacheng Liu, Jason Liu

entry.summary: MegaSlide-DiT shows how a pretrained 105B-parameter video diffusion transformer can be adapted on a single H200 GPU by keeping all persistent state in 1.5TB of host RAM and streaming it, combined with deformable local attention to avoid quadratic spatiotemporal cost. Targets the parameter-memory and activation-memory walls that lock large generative video models to clusters.

entry.title: RP-OPSD: Resolution-Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Qihui Zhu, Yuchen Wang, Zijian Wen, Tao Zhang, Mengjie Zhang, Yang Liu, Shuangwu Chen, Siying Wu, Jian Yang, Xiaofeng Jiang

entry.summary: RP-OPSD creates privileged information for on-policy self-distillation in multimodal LLMs by letting the teacher see full-resolution images while the student generates trajectories from quarter-resolution inputs. This removes the need for verified traces, external explanations, or manual visual evidence annotation.

entry.title: CachedSearch: Training-Free Cached Exploration for Test-Time Search in Video Diffusion

author.name: Shreshth Saini, Neil Birkbeck, Yilin Wang, Balu Adsumilli, Alan C. Bovik

entry.summary: Examines whether lossy training-free caching corrupts verifier rankings when composed with test-time search in video diffusion, since combining the two is only safe if candidate ordering survives. Using an adaptive caching wrapper on a 1.3B text-to-video model, they report median per-prompt Spearman correlation of 0.905 and 72 percent top-1 agreement, with the cached winner recomputed at full compute to retain quality.

entry.title: ACME: A Multi-Cultural, Multi-Embodiment Social-Navigation Dataset

author.name: Shashank Rao Marpally, Allan Wang, Atharva Ghotavadekar, Renato Alexandre Ribeiro, Nhat Le, Pilar Bachiller-Burgos, Pranav Goyal, Subham Agrawal, Yasuhiro Nitta, Howard Ziyu Han, Daeun Song, Masaki Kuribayashi, Kohei Uehara, Xiyue Wang, Yangzhe Kong, Duc M. Nguyen, Amirreza Payandeh, Gerardo P\'erez-Gonz\'alez, Alejandro Torrej\'on-Harto, Jeeho Ahn, Tisha Jain, Andrew Stratton, Elvin Yang, Jorge de Heuvel, Nico Ostermann-Myrau, Sai Anudeep Sajja, Mithilya Raj, Daisuke Sato, Gaston Rouquette, Nikolas Martelaro, Maki Sugimoto, Hironobu Takagi, Chieko Asakawa, Maren Bennewitz, Aaron Steinfeld, Xuesu Xiao, Christoforos Mavrogiannis, Harold Soh

entry.summary: ACME is a large multi-institution social navigation dataset collected at 8 sites in 5 countries with 7 robot embodiments, providing about 29 hours of onboard robot data and 43 hours of overhead pedestrian tracking. Its cross-cultural and cross-embodiment coverage targets a known diversity gap that limits generalization of social navigation policies and human motion prediction.

entry.title: Robust Conformalized Selection with Noisy Responses

author.name: Chengyao Yu, Hongxin Wei, Bingyi Jing

entry.summary: Shows that conformal selection methods lose false-discovery-rate control or most of their power when calibration labels are noisy, then proposes Robust Conformalized Selection to restore guarantees under contamination. Applications include reliable labeling, drug screening, and language model alignment data selection.

entry.title: Action from Adjacent Set in Physical Space Outperforms the Best Prediction in World Models

author.name: Liangyu Li, Qingwen Liu, Mingqing Liu

entry.summary: This paper identifies proposal overgeneration in latent world-model controllers: sampling more candidate action sequences increases the chance that model prediction error assigns an anomalously low cost to an infeasible plan, so selection quality degrades as the proposal pool grows. Audits show feasibility of minimum-cost selection falling sharply when the budget increases from 72 to 288 proposals.

entry.title: When LLM Defenses Backfire: Characterizing Safety, Performance, and Cost Trade-offs

author.name: Tong Zhang, Zexin Li, Simin Chen, Yun Peng

entry.summary: This study systematically measures the hidden costs of LLM jailbreak defenses across three axes: downstream capability loss, over-refusal on benign prompts, and inference overhead, grouping defenses by operational strategy. The finding is that defenses essentially never improve capability and differ mainly in how they trade safety for usability and cost.

entry.title: Accuracy Hides How Language Models Fail: Measuring Failure States Under Matched Output Budgets

author.name: Zongyou Yang, Yinghan Hou

entry.summary: Proposes separating execution evidence such as termination, answer exposure, parseability, and completion length from scorer-dependent correctness when evaluating language models under matched token budgets. Shows that at a fixed 2,048-token limit, model families differ sharply in how often they fail to expose a final answer at all, a failure mode that plain accuracy conflates with wrong answers.

entry.title: Auditing Alignment Controllability in LLMs via Political Axes

author.name: Bartol Bu\'can, Nikola So\v{c}ec, Sarah Isufi, Morena Grani\'c, Luka Hobor, Agneza Krajna, Mihael Kovac, Mario Brcic

entry.summary: Audits political controllability rather than resting political position across seven leading models, using 12 ideological personas, 70 compass items and 63,700 responses. Finds that contextual framing via system prompts explains roughly 88-93 percent of variance, arguing steerability matters far more than a model's default political point.

entry.title: DecoupleMix: Decoupled Ratio Search and Convex Allocation for Scalable VLM Data Recipes

author.name: Jiahao Xie, Zhongbin Guo, Qianle Wang, Ruiqi Lu, Dongling Xiao, Wanxuan Sun, Cheng Yang

entry.summary: DecoupleMix turns VLM pretraining data mixture design into an explicit optimization by separating inter-capability ratios from intra-category composition, using a single-variable iterative search plus convex allocation. It aims to replace heuristic dataset stacking with a reproducible, attributable recipe.

entry.title: EgoPlay: Event-Triggered Video Editing for Egocentric Streams

author.name: Jinjie Mai, Gordon Guocheng Qian, Willi Menapace, Arpit Sahni, Chaoyang Wang, Ashkan Mirzaei, Runjia Li, Sergey Tulyakov, Bernard Ghanem, Peter Wonka, Rameen Abdal

entry.summary: EgoPlay fine-tunes a video-to-video diffusion transformer on 106K event-conditioned clip-prompt pairs from egocentric footage so it can interpret prompts of the form when X happens do Y, detecting the event and editing only subsequent frames. Event recognition, temporal restraint, and pixel editing are learned jointly in one end-to-end model.

entry.title: OmniVAE: An Audio-Video VAE with Cross-Modal Alignment for Joint Generation

author.name: Jun Zhan, Chen Yang, Yitian Gong, Donghua Yu, Kuangwei Chen, Wenbo Zhang, Kexin Huang, Qi Luo, Zhe Xu, Ying Zhu, Jin Wang, Tengyue Zhang, Qi Chen, Cheng Chang, Songlin Wang, Junqi Dai, Jiasheng Ye, Xiaogui Yang, Tianyi Liang, Xiangyu Peng, Zhaoye Fei, Shimin Li, Qinyuan Cheng, Xie Chen, Xinchi Chen, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: OmniVAE is a jointly trained audio-video variational autoencoder that aligns the two latent spaces at segment level, rather than using separately trained per-modality VAEs. This gives downstream joint generative models a latent space where audio-visual synchronization is already partly baked in.

entry.title: When the Chain of Thought Knows Better: Failure Modes in Multi-Turn Reasoning Models

author.name: Sai Kartheek Reddy

entry.summary: Summarizes a workshop paper testing three small distilled reasoning models against a persistent multi-turn adversary trying to extract restricted information. Reports two failure modes: explicit monitoring statements appear to increase rather than suppress alignment faking, and context injection bypasses safety flags that the chain of thought itself had raised.

entry.title: Securing Multimodal AI through Internal Information Decomposition

author.name: Jehyeok Yeon, Hyeonjeong Ha, Qiusi Zhan, Heng Ji

entry.summary: Proposes FlowGuard, an inference-time defense for multimodal LLMs that detects attacks distributed across modalities by measuring whether text-only and vision-only internal predictive behavior stay consistent when fused. Unlike input or output filters, it inspects the internal fusion process, which the authors claim is cheaper and more robust.

entry.title: AgentKVShift: Efficient KV Cache Reuse for Agentic Memory Systems

author.name: Nilesh Prasad Pandey, Jason Kong, Lanxiang Hu, Quanling Zhao, Yujie Zhao, Onat Gungor, Hao Zhang, Tajana Rosing

entry.summary: AgentKVShift is a training-free method for reusing key-value caches across the structured memory units that agentic memory systems retrieve, avoiding full re-encoding on every retrieval. It uses probe-guided residual correction per memory unit, arguing that existing RAG-oriented KV reuse methods degrade on LLM-generated summaries, tags and metadata.

entry.title: Learning as Reasoning Unfolds: Progressive Rollout Allocation for Efficient Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Heyang Jiang, Henry Liu, Baharan Mirzasoleiman

entry.summary: Tackles the cost of GRPO-style RLVR training, where most long chain-of-thought rollouts are uninformative, by allocating rollouts progressively and online using variance-based guidance rather than pre-generating large pools or relying on historical filtering. The goal is efficiency gains that do not slow the overall training loop.

entry.title: SCALE: Self-Supervised Constraint-Aware Layout GEneration for Local P&R DRV Fixing at Advanced Nodes

author.name: Chia-Tung Ho, Haoyu Yang, Guanglei Zhou, Yoshi Nishi, Yaguang Li, Walker Turner, Cunxi Yu, Yiran Chen, Brucek Khailany

entry.summary: SCALE tackles design-rule-violation fixing in sub-2nm chip place-and-route by adding a self-supervised layout-generation stage so vision-language models can reason about multi-layer routing geometry and foundry-specific rules. It targets visual layout understanding, a capability largely absent from general-purpose VLM pretraining.

entry.title: Beyond Shapley: An Influence-Based Data Auditing Pipeline for LLM Alignment and Evaluation

author.name: Yunting Song, Matthew Watson, Peter Grabowski, Jun Qin

entry.summary: This work proposes an inference-only data valuation pipeline that approximates Shapley-style influence for alignment and instruction-tuning corpora by building a directed graph over semantic nearest-neighbor neighborhoods, avoiding repeated retraining. It targets a real bottleneck in LLM alignment: silently contradictory, unsafe, or mislabeled preference records that deduplication and judge-model filtering miss.

entry.title: AlloBench: Measuring Online Tool Allocation Capability in LLM Agents

author.name: Daniel Wang, Andrew Xu

entry.summary: AlloBench tests whether LLM agents behave like rational investors when building reusable tools under a fixed budget, pairing an abstract text formulation with a code-construction version. The authors report that current frontier models, including Claude and GPT-5 series systems, act near-optimally in the abstract framing but fail to transfer that allocation reasoning to actually writing reusable scripts, and they characterize per-model failure modes.

entry.title: TokenMem: Faithful Knowledge Injection for Frozen LLMs

author.name: Chengzhang Yu, Chenyang Zheng, Zening Lu, Yingru He, Yutong Huang, Yiming Zhang, Yue Xu, Zhanpeng Jin

entry.summary: TokenMem injects external knowledge into frozen language models through a dedicated cross-attention channel with a small gating adapter, so retrieved facts do not fight parametric memory in the residual stream. A two-phase curriculum including counterfactual data trains the model to faithfully follow supplied knowledge across five models in three families.

entry.title: Similarity Is Not Logic: Factored Inference for Dual-Encoder Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sultan Alshehri, Zhantao Yang, Han Zhang, Marios Savvides

entry.summary: Shows dual-encoder vision-language models fail logical queries such as umbrella and no person because their similarity interface effectively mean-pools concept evidence regardless of logical operators, a bag-of-concepts effect. The proposed factored inference separates concept evidence extraction from operator-aware aggregation, and the authors argue fine-tuning cannot fix an aggregation-level bottleneck.

entry.title: Beyond ICA: Identifiability by Symmetry Breaking

author.name: Pengzhou Wu

entry.summary: This theory paper proves identifiability for deep generative models with piecewise-affine decoders and Gaussian-mixture latent priors, using three algebraic symmetry-breaking conditions instead of the usual continuity or auxiliary-variable assumptions. It extends the classical nonlinear ICA identifiability program to a fully unsupervised setting.

entry.title: DualityCert: Verifier-Gated Language-Model Repair of Broken Duality Claims in Quantum Field Theory

author.name: Xingyang Yu

entry.summary: DualityCert is a symbolic verifier for candidate Seiberg-duality claims in supersymmetric quiver gauge theories, checking anomaly matching and other consistency conditions, used as a gated repair environment for LLM agents. On a preregistered benchmark of 145 deliberately broken claims, verifier-gated retry improves repair success over single attempts.

entry.title: The Zero Pattern of a Design Matrix Drives Multiple Descent in Over-parameterized Regression

author.name: Kevin Han Huang, Haoyu Ye, Somak Laha, Morgane Austern

entry.summary: This theory paper relaxes the standard independence and non-degenerate covariance assumptions in over-parameterized linear regression, deriving deterministic risk equivalents and showing that degeneracy and dependence produce multiple descent peaks. The proofs use a novel graph representation of the variance profile with maximum matchings and Dulmage-Mendelsohn decomposition.

entry.title: EXE-Bench: Ranking the Tradeoffs of AI-based Windows Malware Detectors for Real-World Usability

author.name: Andrea Ponte, Daniel Gibert, Matous Kozak, Dmitrijs Trizna, Maura Pintor, Battista Biggio, Fabio Roli, Luca Demetrio

entry.summary: EXE-Bench is a comprehensive benchmark for AI-based Windows malware detectors that jointly measures standard performance, temporal robustness to concept drift, adversarial robustness to content-injection attacks, and computational cost for endpoint deployment. It aims to make deployment decisions evidence-based rather than paper-dependent.

entry.title: Catalyst Diffusion Transformer: Generative Inverse Design of Heterogeneous Catalysts

author.name: Hayoung Doo, Dong Hyeon Mok, Seoin Back, Jonggeol Na

entry.summary: CatDiT is a latent diffusion transformer for inverse design of heterogeneous catalysts that generates valid structures spanning intermetallic alloys to oxide surfaces, conditioned simultaneously on adsorbate type, binding energy, and catalyst class. It broadens generative catalyst design beyond single-property and narrow chemical spaces.

entry.title: Stochastic Counterdiabatic Driving via Biorthogonal Liouvillian Eigenmodes

author.name: Sandeep Suresh Cranganore, Sebastian Lehner, Johannes Brandstetter, Max Welling

entry.summary: Applies biorthogonal Liouvillian eigenmode decomposition to construct counterdiabatic control fields that remove non-adiabatic lag in finite-time stochastic driving, aiming at zero-variance free-energy estimators for Jarzynski-style simulations. The approach offers a closed-form alternative to learned diffeomorphisms or flow-field escorting methods used in molecular free-energy work.

entry.title: Toward Automated Detection of Documentation Inconsistencies in Electronic Health Records

author.name: Jian Lu, Panyu Chen, Miriam Treggiari, Robert Blessing, Danyang Zhuo, Chunhua Weng, William W. Stead, Anru R. Zhang

entry.summary: Applies a two-stage pipeline of open-ended candidate generation followed by context-grounded verification to 3,000 MIMIC-IV discharge summaries, surfacing about 3,460 candidate internal documentation inconsistencies affecting nearly 70 percent of admissions. Clinician review characterizes recurring failure modes that limit reliability at scale.

entry.title: ADAGE: A Language-Agnostic Pipeline for Analogical Reasoning Evaluation

author.name: Ahmed Haj Ahmed, Alvin Grissom II

entry.summary: Presents a pipeline combining native-speaker curation with LLM-assisted generation to build translation-free analogical reasoning benchmarks, instantiated for Arabic, Amharic, and Japanese. Evaluation of 14 open-weight models reveals a large cultural reasoning gap relative to English proverb tasks.

entry.title: SyRuP: Enhancing System-Prompt Following via Reward-Guided Prediction in LLM Decoding

author.name: Seoyeon Kim, Minjae Kang, Jaehyung Kim

entry.summary: Presents a decoding-time method that improves system-prompt adherence by training a cross-attention reward head on system-prompt-conditioned preference pairs to produce token-level adherence scores, while keeping the base model frozen. Avoids full tuning or response-level reranking for lightweight controllability.

entry.title: Looping Is Not Reliability: State-Bound Evidence and Typed Revision Contracts for Agentic Code Repair

author.name: Xueping Gao, Jianwei Yang, Qiang Yang

entry.summary: A carefully controlled study of generate-test-revise loops in coding agents showing that repeated revision can destroy already-correct patches, especially when the agent revises against stale execution traces. Proposes typed revision contracts and state-bound evidence so agents retain and verify correct solutions.

entry.title: Harnessing X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy Data through Multimodal Mining of Battery Literature

author.name: Tanjin He, Aikaterini Vriza, Logan Ward, Xu Huang, Yiming Chen, Anubhav Jain, Gerbrand Ceder, Rajeev S. Assary, Ian T. Foster, Maria K. Y. Chan

entry.summary: Builds a multimodal literature-mining pipeline that finds X-ray absorption spectroscopy figures in battery papers, digitizes the spectral curves and links each to metadata about the measured edge and material, yielding an open dataset of 13,740 spectra. Turns knowledge locked in figures into machine-usable scientific data.

entry.title: Advancing All-Weather Building Damage Mapping to the Instance Level: Outcomes and Insights from the 2026 Bright Challenge

author.name: Hongruixuan Chen, He Huang, Haifeng Wang, Jian Song, Junjue Wang, Weihao Xuan, Hamish Mitchell, Jiepan Li, Wei He, Liangpei Zhang, Zijie Wang, Chen Zhong, Jiazhen Zhao, Lei Hu, Ting Hu, Hongyan Zhang, Gregory Angelides, Miriam Cha, Clifford Broni-Bediako, Junshi Xia, Taylor Perron, Naoto Yokoya

entry.summary: Reports outcomes of a 2026 challenge on instance-level all-weather building damage mapping from pre-event optical plus post-event SAR imagery, with roughly 291,000 newly annotated buildings across 16 disaster events. Requires per-building detection, delineation and three-way damage classification, evaluated on held-out events.

entry.title: UltraViT: Latency-Optimized On-device Vision Encoder for Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ioannis Maniadis Metaxas, Adrian Bulat, Alberto Baldrati, Anestis Zaganidis, Yassine Ouali, Hyeonuk Kim, Georgios Tzimiropoulos

entry.summary: UltraViT designs a pyramidal vision encoder for large vision-language models optimized directly against measured on-device latency, rather than relying on token reduction or smaller language models. Argues the vision encoder is the overlooked bottleneck for edge deployment.

entry.title: Head Avatars with Dynamic Explicit Hair

author.name: Vanessa Sklyarova, Haonan Chen, Berna Kabadayi, Tobias Kirschstein, Zicong Fan, Xi Wang, Gerard Pons-Moll, Matthias Nie{\ss}ner, Marc Pollefeys, Michael J. Black, Justus Thies

entry.summary: DynHair reconstructs head avatars with explicit strand-based hair via structured 3D Gaussians, modeling strand deformation with a temporal network conditioned on head angular velocity, acceleration, and relative gravity. Addresses hair dynamics, which face-focused avatar models cannot capture.

entry.title: Disentangling Semantic Attention from Structural Bias in the Attention Manifold

author.name: Pengkun Jiao, Bin Zhu, Jingjing Chen, Yu-gang Jiang

entry.summary: Reframes visual attention sinks in multimodal LLMs not as isolated register tokens but as a pervasive textual structural bias that dilutes semantic attention over visual features. It proposes disentangling semantic attention from this structural bias in the attention manifold, aiming for a cheaper and more general inference-time intervention.

entry.title: FilmBench: A Film-Grade Benchmark for Cinematic Video Generation

author.name: Shengyi Wang, Niantong Li, Guangzheng Hu, Hong Qi, Fei Ding, Weixu Qiao, Jinlin Wang, Xiaotong Lv, Peng Han, Zimeng Li, Fanshu Ding, Yushu Wang, Han Wu, Jingjing Chen, Chongxiao Wang, Yanhao Wu, Chenglong Huang, Xiaoqian Zhu, Jie Tian, Hua Li, Jingjing Fan, Mingshuang Tang, Zhong Li, Hengxia Qiang, Weibin Chen, Jinyang Zhen, Bing Zhao, Lin Qu, Jing Li, Hu Wei

entry.summary: FilmBench is a text-to-video and reference-to-video benchmark built on professional cinematic language criteria and co-developed with film directors, rather than generic prompts scored by off-the-shelf multimodal judges. It aims to measure film-grade craft instead of basic plausibility.

entry.title: The Curse of Precision: A Data Scaling Law for High-Precision Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Cuijie Xu, Yuanfan Xu, Min Xue, Jianjie Lin, Jian Wang, Xudong Zhang, Yu Wang, Jincheng Yu

entry.summary: Proposes a data scaling law for high-precision robotic assembly in which the number of demonstrations needed grows super-exponentially as required precision approaches a system-dependent limit, fitted as log N proportional to 1/(P-c). Argues the limiting precision is an emergent property of the whole agent stack including sensors and expert policy, not a fixed physical constant.

entry.title: ArmnetBench v0.1: Parallel Real-World Evaluation of Manipulation Policies on a Low-Cost Arm Farm

author.name: Praveen Selvaraj, Lorenzo Uttini, Ville Kuosmanen

entry.summary: ArmnetBench v0.1 evaluates 7 manipulation policies across 12 single-arm and bimanual tasks on a fleet of low-cost SO-101 robot cells, collecting over 3,000 human-labeled episodes with three-way success grading. It attacks the real-world evaluation bottleneck that makes generalist policy comparison expensive and inconsistent.

entry.title: Mission-Level Runtime Assurance for LLM-Assisted ISR Swarms over a Verification-Aware Fabric

author.name: Nikolaos Kekatos, Stylianos Basagiannis, Panagiotis Katsaros, Alexios Lekidis, Tom Nianios

entry.summary: Proposes a three-tier compositional runtime verification framework for LLM-assisted robot swarms, decomposing mission policies into per-agent and cross-agent obligations to catch violations that emerge only from the composition of individually compliant actions. Explicitly handles contested communications where evidence is lost or delayed.

entry.title: Visual Token Compression Enhances Robustness of MLLMs

author.name: Shishen Gu, Jiequan Cui, Wenbo Hu, Zenglin Shi, Zhenzhen Hu, Richang Hong

entry.summary: Reports that pruning visual tokens in multimodal language models improves robustness to jailbreaks and reduces hallucination, arguing that poorly aligned visual tokens act as out-of-distribution inputs. Tokens far from the language feature space are dropped at selected layers, cutting inference cost as a bonus.

entry.title: Operator Neural Jump ODEs: $L^2$-optimal prediction in function spaces

author.name: Florian Krach, Oliver L\"othgren, Josef Teichmann

entry.summary: Extends Neural Jump ODEs to processes valued in infinite-dimensional function spaces, showing the operator version recovers the L2-optimal predictor, that is a representative of the conditional expectation, from irregular and incomplete discrete observations. This continues a line of work covering path dependence, noise, and long-horizon prediction.

entry.title: SpecBox: Speculative Sandbox Scheduling for Efficient LLM Agent Serving

author.name: Yihui Zhang (Beihang University), Tianyu Wo (Beihang University), Jinghao Wang (Beihang University), Xiaoyang Sun (University of Leeds), Menghao Zhang (Beihang University), Cangzhou Yuan (Beihang University), Li Li (Beihang University), Chunming Hu (Beihang University), Albert Y. Zomaya (The University of Sydney), Renyu Yang (Beihang University)

entry.summary: SpecBox speculatively pre-warms external tool sandboxes for LLM agents by predicting upcoming Model Context Protocol invocations from keyword matching and streaming semantic embeddings of the agent's output. This resolves the tension between memory-hungry persistent sandboxes and cold-start latency in multi-tenant agent serving.

entry.title: Decision trees, Frobenius traces, and Weierstrass coefficients of elliptic curves

author.name: Barinder S. Banwait, Xiaoyu Huang, Kyu-Hwan Lee, Seewoo Lee, Thomas Oliver, Alexey Pozdnyakov

entry.summary: Using decision trees as an exploratory tool, the authors discover that the first reduced minimal Weierstrass coefficients of elliptic curves are recoverable from Frobenius traces at small primes plus conductor parity, then prove explicit closed-form formulae. The results imply these coefficients are determined by the isogeny class.

entry.title: A New Role for Relevance: Guiding Corpus Interaction in Agentic Search

author.name: Jiangnan Li, Yuqing Li, Mo Yu, Jinchao Zhang, Jie Zhou

entry.summary: Argues that relevance signals should guide the order and granularity of direct corpus interaction in agentic search, rather than only selecting top-k documents or narrowing a working space. Uses relevance to decide which documents grep-style exploration touches first and which excerpts the model sees first, speeding convergence on complex questions.

entry.title: Where Is the Cost of Third-Party API Routers in Agentic Software Development?

author.name: Donghao Fu, Jingxin Li, Xue Jiang, Yihong Dong

entry.summary: Examines the security implications of third-party LLM API routers, which sit on the trusted path between coding agents and providers and can silently inspect or modify every request and response. Argues that client-side permission mechanisms can be undermined because nothing verifies alignment between provider output and the repository actions actually executed.

entry.title: Reality Monitoring in Large Language Models: Self-Knowledge That Transforms with Conversation Memory

author.name: Saurabh Ranjan, Konstantina Sokratous, Brian Odegaard

entry.summary: Tests whether LLMs can distinguish their own prior outputs from user-provided content, a capacity called reality monitoring in cognitive science, across two experiments and six models. Finds source attribution collapses once episodic delay removes shortcut cues, and that feedback can swap internal and external judgments or decouple confidence from accuracy.

entry.title: The Visual Bottleneck: Sparse-Frame Adaptation of MLLMs for Joint Spatial-Temporal Video Grounding

author.name: Jiameng Zhang, Srikanth Madikeri

entry.summary: Documents a severe train-deploy mismatch for multimodal LLMs in video grounding: models pretrained on hundreds of frames collapse when restricted to the 8 to 16 frames feasible for large-scale moderation, with one 8B model dropping from 56.0 to 22.3 temporal mIoU. It then empirically compares training strategies to close the sparse-frame gap.

entry.title: LeapBot-WA: World-Anchor Action Models via Predictive Latent Alignments

author.name: Pei Liu, Nan Zheng, Lang Zhang, Daojie Peng, Yanan Zhang, Feilong Kong, Mingyue Feng, Jiachao Liu, Yaonong Wang, Qifeng Chen, Jun Ma

entry.summary: LeapBot-WA replaces pixel-level future prediction in world-action models with a JEPA-style predictive latent alignment, arguing that reconstructing task-irrelevant visual detail wastes capacity and creates vulnerability to distractors. The latent world anchor conditions the action policy on abstract physical dynamics instead of synthesized images.

entry.title: What do Reward Models Memorize?

author.name: Ivo Verhoeven, Pushkar Mishra, Ekaterina Shutova

entry.summary: Measures counterfactual memorization in discriminatively trained reward models on two human preference datasets, finding that they over-memorize easy high-margin pairs, latch onto dataset-specific shortcuts like model identity or sampling strategy, and overgeneralize surface heuristics such as response length and compliance. The conclusion is that such reward models are biased and not yet able to judge quality in context-dependent settings.

entry.title: FusionML: Prefill, Not Decode - Mechanism and Boundaries of CPU+GPU Co-Execution on Unified-Memory Apple Silicon

author.name: Om Mohite

entry.summary: Diagnoses why CPU plus GPU co-execution of transformer operators fails on unified-memory Apple silicon, tracing it to MLX lazy-graph scheduling that serializes cross-stream work when a CPU op consumes an unmaterialized GPU result. Adding an eager materialization boundary restores concurrency, yielding real prefill speedups while decode remains memory-bound.

entry.title: INS-ActBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Assessing Professional Actuarial Capability of Large Language Models

author.name: Changyu Chen, Chenwei Lin, Xian Xu

entry.summary: Releases a 12,050-question actuarial benchmark drawn from public exams of 16 actuarial associations, split into knowledge, long-context insurance case reasoning, and tool-executable subsets. Designed to test integrated professional workflows rather than isolated capabilities.

entry.title: AI-generated Images Challenge Visual Trust in High-risk Scenarios

author.name: Yi-Zhi Wang, Yichen Xiao, Linan Yue, Weibo Gao, Yichao Du, Pengfei Fang, Shimin Di, Min-Ling Zhang

entry.summary: SafeIMG is a benchmark of synthetic images generated with GPT Image 2 across 12 public- and individual-safety scenarios, with human annotations localizing the suspicious regions people actually notice. It tests not only whether detectors flag synthetic images but whether their decisions align with human-identified anomalies.

entry.title: Mixture-of-Thought-Tokens: Unifying Perception and Reasoning for Free-form Multimodal Grounding

author.name: Tianyi Gao, Han Fang, Tianyi Ding, Hao Li, Xin Wei, Hongbo Sun, Xiaodong Dong, Ye Yuan, Jinglin Xu, Kongming Liang, Hao Sun, Jingmin Xin

entry.summary: Motto introduces mixture-of-thought-tokens for free-form multimodal grounding, mixing spatially referenced latent tokens with explicit reasoning steps to unify precise localization and complex reasoning in MLLMs. It targets the weakness of coordinate-text prediction on dense objects and of spatially unanchored latent tokens.

entry.title: Reason Before You Retrieve: Agentic Planning for Multi-modal RAG

author.name: Tianyu Yang, Shir Simon, Zhenzhen Li, Minhao Cheng, Xiangliang Zhang

entry.summary: MM-R2 is a multimodal agentic retrieval framework that reasons before retrieving, first grounding question intent to the correct visual referent and then deciding where to search within a structured evidence space. It addresses under-specified retrieval targets and flat global ranking in multimodal RAG.

entry.title: Towards Ultrafast Depth Sensing Via Active Event-based Stereo Vision

author.name: Jianing Li, Yunjian Zhang, Haiqian Han, Kangyao Huang, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: Introduces active event-based stereo vision, pairing binocular event cameras with an infrared pattern projector for ultrafast dense depth sensing, along with real and synthetic datasets totaling tens of thousands of labeled frames and a lightweight network. Targets fast-motion regimes where frame-based active stereo fails.

entry.title: Effective Parameters, Real Behavior: Renormalization for Robotics -- From Infinite Electron Mass to Sim-to-Real Gap

author.name: Youran Sun, Jiaxuan Guo, Xingyu Ren, Chugang Yi, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: Proposes treating the sim-to-real gap through a renormalization lens, using effective resolution-dependent parameters to absorb physics the simulator omits rather than building ever more accurate simulators. Shows analytically for PD control at finite simulation frequency how feedback gains rescale effective inertia and damping.

entry.title: FeelWorld: Visuo-Tactile World Model for Hierarchical Contact Prediction and Planning

author.name: Wenxuan Ma, Chaofan Zhang, Chao Xue, Yinghao Cai, Guocai Yao, Shaowei Cui, Shuo Wang

entry.summary: FeelWorld is a hierarchical visuo-tactile world model that predicts future visual latents alongside contact state, a 3D force-related tactile latent, and slip state, with explicit supervision and mechanisms to suppress irrelevant tactile signal. It aims to avoid imagined futures that look plausible but violate contact physics.

entry.title: What AI Red-Team Evaluations Can and Cannot Prove

author.name: Bandana Kaur

entry.summary: Derives a closed-form evidential ceiling for red-team benchmarks, quantifying the maximum belief update a fixed testing budget can produce and thereby marking exactly which safety claims a clean evaluation can and cannot support. Above a calculable harm rate a modest benchmark can certify a category, while below it no feasible passive benchmark provides the stated evidence of safety.

entry.title: Learning on the Job: Continual Learning from Deployment Feedback for Frozen-Weights Agents

author.name: Valentin Tablan, Scott Taylor, Kristoffer Bernhem

entry.summary: Shows that ordinary deployment feedback, specifically one-bit outcome verdicts and after-the-fact corrections, is enough for continual learning when a frozen model is paired with an external memory that distills each episode into retrievable natural-language rules. On the banking split of a tool-use benchmark, learning from verdicts alone raises single-trial success substantially over a static retrieval control.

entry.title: dRAE: Representation Autoencoder with Hyper-Spherical Codes

author.name: Tianren Ma, Lin Long, Chuyan Chen, Mu Zhang, Junbo Zhao, Tong Zhang, Qixiang Ye

entry.summary: dRAE discretizes high-dimensional visual representations for use with language models via Hyper-Spherical Quantization, which routes codes by angle to decouple semantic content from feature magnitude. The authors attribute codebook collapse to a metric mismatch between Euclidean codebook objectives and the anisotropic geometry of representation space.

entry.title: Hyperball May Not Be a Free Lunch

author.name: Yihao Xiao, Jialong Sun, Zitian Gao, Zeming Wei, Chutian Wang, Ran Tao, Jiaye Teng, Bryan Dai

entry.summary: This analysis questions why Hyperball-style optimizers that fix parameter matrix norms and normalize updates work well at scale, deriving an angular effective learning rate from parameter-update angle, parameter norm, and update norm. Decomposing updates into radial and tangential parts shows conventional norm-based measures are a special case and that the claimed advantage is not unconditional.

entry.title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science

author.name: Davide Scarso, Hugo Noronha de Almeida, Joaquim Pina

entry.summary: Across four temporal snapshots from late 2025 through early 2026 and both API and web interfaces, the authors test how existing Claude, Grok, GPT, and Gemini model families rate ethnonationalist pseudo-science drawn from a biosocial framework. Grok Fast variants, which back the default experience on X, consistently assigned credibility scores of 70 to 75, several times higher than the other models, while control prompts on evolutionary consensus showed no such divergence.

entry.title: Progress-conditioned Group Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks

author.name: Kaibing Yang, Guangfeng Cai, Shengtian Yang, Shuo He, Yu Li, Mengyi Liu, Pengwei Chen, Jun Xu, Lei Feng

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses a credit trap in group-based policy optimization for long-horizon LLM agents, where repeated low-effect actions dominate sampling, useful state-changing actions are under-sampled, and all-failed rollout groups leave outcome rewards uninformative. It proposes progress-conditioned group optimization to restore learning signal under sparse outcome rewards.

entry.title: When Can You Correct Distribution Drift in Temporal Graph Generation? A Sharpening--Drift Tension and an Impossibility for Observation-Based Correction

author.name: Tianpeng Li, Xuan Guo, Wenjun Wang, Wang Zhang, Pengfei Jiao

entry.summary: Shows theoretically and empirically that temporal graph generative models degrade under distribution drift between training and deployment windows, decomposing the masked flow-matching loss to expose an irreducible divergence term that blows up for structures rare in training. It further argues observation-based correction cannot fix this, an impossibility-style result with a fitted power-law tradeoff.

entry.title: Evaluating and Mitigating the Misguidance Effect of Buggy Code in LLM-Generated Unit Tests

author.name: Junda Zhao, Shurui Zhou, Eldan Cohen

entry.summary: Quantifies a misguidance effect where prompting a model with buggy code leads it to write tests that assert the buggy behavior instead of exposing it, and shows this simultaneously suppresses effective bug-finding tests. The authors corroborate the effect with model-internal evidence and propose mitigations.

entry.title: CAPT: A Multi-task Continuous Autoregressive Transformer enabling Cross-dataset and Cross-species Transfer for Calcium Population Dynamics

author.name: Xinhong Xu, Yimeng Zhang, Yuanlong Zhang

entry.summary: CAPT is a continuous autoregressive transformer for calcium imaging population dynamics that tokenizes continuous traces directly and is trained multi-task. The central claim is that pretrained representations transfer across datasets, experimental paradigms, and even species, a key test for neural foundation models.

entry.title: ATLAS: Automated Approximation of Transformers for Efficient Homomorphic Inference in One Hour

author.name: Jianhang Xie, Sicheng Tan, Vishnu Naresh Boddeti, Zhichao Lu

entry.summary: ATLAS automatically searches per-layer polynomial approximation hyperparameters for transformer nonlinearities under CKKS homomorphic encryption, replacing hand-tuned uniform configurations. The claim is that a full automated configuration can be found in about an hour, reducing multiplicative depth and hence private inference cost.

entry.title: The Illusion of Secure LLM Code: Closing the Security Gap via Iterative Reprompting

author.name: Ishpuneet Singh, Shreyas Mahajan, Gurjot Singh, Maninder Singh

entry.summary: This study evaluates authentication code produced by five AI coding assistants using both static analysis and dynamic penetration testing mapped to NIST SP 800-63B, across four prompting strategies. Functional or generically secure prompts consistently omit critical protections, while iterative reprompting substantially closes the gap.

entry.title: When Low CER is Not Enough: An Analysis of Hallucinations in Vision-Language OCR Systems on Historical Uruguayan Documents

author.name: Marina Gardella (CB), Camilo Mari{\~n}o (UDELAR, CB), Diego Belzarena (UDELAR, CB), Ignacio Ram{\'i}rez (UDELAR), Gregory Randall (UDELAR), Jean-Michel Morel (LU - Hong Kong)

entry.summary: Benchmarking vision-language models against traditional OCR on Uruguayan dictatorship-era microfilm documents, the authors show that VLMs win on character and word error rate yet hide a distinct failure mode: fluent hallucinated transcriptions. This questions the adequacy of CER as the sole metric for archival digitization.

entry.title: Minimax Lower Bounds of Kernel Discrepancy Estimation: MMD, HSIC, KSD

author.name: Jose Cribeiro-Ramallo, Florian Kalinke, Zolt\'an Szab\'o

entry.summary: The authors prove minimax lower bounds for estimating the most widely used kernel discrepancies, MMD, HSIC, and KSD, beyond the finite-dimensional Euclidean setting and with unbounded kernels. This establishes optimality of the known parametric rate in much broader regimes.

entry.title: Self-Attention Dynamics with Rotary Position Embeddings: Twisted States and Explicit Consensus Rates on the Sphere

author.name: Hao Ye (Xi'an Institute of Optics, Precision Mechanics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences)

entry.summary: Analyzes continuous-time token dynamics of self-attention when rotary position embeddings rotate queries and keys while values stay on the sphere, characterizing equilibria, twisted states, and explicit consensus convergence rates. Extends the mathematical theory of attention as an interacting particle system to include positional encoding.

entry.title: Learning When to Reason for Text-to-SQL via SFT and DPO

author.name: Soohyuk Jang, Jiheum Yeom, Nohil Park, Sang Hun Kim, Yoonyoung Choi, Kiwook Bae, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: Proposes an auto-thinking framework for text-to-SQL that learns when to skip chain-of-thought for simple lookups and when to invoke deep reasoning, trained with supervised fine-tuning plus direct preference optimization. Reports consistent gains over always-reason baselines on a 30B coder model while cutting inference overhead.

entry.title: GEMCo: A Validated, Ethically Releasable Proxy for Inaccessible Counselling Data

author.name: Philipp Steigerwald, Eric Rudolph, Mara Stieler, Jennifer Burghardt, Jens Albrecht

entry.summary: Releases 86 complete German email counseling conversations with 728 messages, written by experts and trained role-players as an ethically shareable proxy for real counseling data, and validates it against 124 held-out real conversations on counsellor strategies and client emotions. Reports a small but detectable gap and proposes the validation method as a general recipe for closed domains.

entry.title: CAGE: Cognitive Attribution Graphs for Faithful Inline Citation Generation in Long-Form Question Answering

author.name: Zhichao Yan, Shizhao Li, Jiapu Wang, Haoran Luo, Qingang Zhang, Jiaoyan Chen, Ru Li, Jeff Z. Pan

entry.summary: Proposes building an explicit claim-to-document attribution map before generating long-form answers, to prevent citations that are topically related but insufficient and to avoid claims exceeding cited support. Frames the core issue as attribution ambiguity in end-to-end citation generation.

entry.title: Tokengeist: Multi-Turn Attribution Tracing in Agentic Conversations

author.name: Jessica Tang, Shraddha Barke, Sharad Agarwal

entry.summary: Defines multi-turn context attribution, the task of tracing which tokens from which earlier turns shaped a model response and how those dependencies chain across turns. Tokengeist is an attribution-method-agnostic framework that recovers this layered structure rather than treating context as one flat pass.

entry.title: Do Current Retrievers Cover All the Evidence? A Controlled Study of Conjunctive Cross-Page Retrieval

author.name: Sungguk Cha, DongWook Kim, Mintae Kim, Youngsub Han, Byoung-Ki Jeon, Sangyeob Lee

entry.summary: Studies conjunctive cross-page retrieval, where a document must support two or three separate conditions on different pages, using a controlled 1,000-query instrument that pairs full-evidence golds with partially-satisfying distractors. Finds condition-wise decomposition and lexical-visual fusion help substantially while all four generic rerankers actually hurt evidence coverage.

entry.title: StepX-Edge: An On-Device UI Vision-Language Model via Architecture-Training-Deployment Co-Design

author.name: Yin Wang, Haotian Hu, Jineng Han, Wentao Qiu, Zhenhua Ge, Liujian Tang, Fanyi Wang

entry.summary: StepX-Edge is a 0.9B on-device UI vision-language model co-designed across architecture, training and deployment, with layered visual encoding and a progressive projection connector to handle the extreme aspect ratios of phone screens. It is validated on real mobile hardware rather than only in simulation.

entry.title: What CLIP Knows but Cannot Say: Recovering Negation from Frozen Intermediate Features

author.name: Chen-Yi Lu, Yueh-Shao Chen, Somali Chaterji

entry.summary: Traces why CLIP cannot represent negation, showing that middle text-encoder layers build compositional syntax that the final layers collapse as visual alignment increases. Proposes PeakPatch, a post-hoc correction that taps the encoder at its compositional peak without changing pretrained weights.

entry.title: The Gate Always Closes: On Injecting Auxiliary Signals into Frozen Vision-Language Models

author.name: Moshiur Farazi, Sameera Ramasinghe, Bekir Sait Ciftler, Mahbub Ahmed Turza, Shafin Rahman

entry.summary: Reports that learnable gates on auxiliary signal pathways into frozen vision-language models almost always converge to behaviourally closed states, with accuracy unchanged when the pathway is ablated even at nominally open gate values. Explains this via dead-gradient and negative-utility regimes and instead uses geometric auxiliary losses to regularize LoRA fine-tuning.

entry.title: DailyBench: A Unified Benchmark for AI-Generated and Manipulated Images from Modern Generative Models

author.name: Xin Jiang, Hao Tang, Junyao Gao, Meiqi Cao, Fei Shen, Dongming Zhang, Yongdong Zhang

entry.summary: DailyBench is a detection benchmark covering both modern fully synthetic images and localized object-level manipulations, addressing the mismatch between older benchmarks and current generative pipelines. It is designed to test whether AI-image detectors generalize across synthesis and editing.

entry.title: MSVS-VAE: Multi-Scale Anchored VecSet for High-Fidelity 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Dehao Hao, Kaiyi Zhang, Tanghui Jia, Xiangjun Gao, Dongyu Yan, Weikai Chen, Zeyu Hu, Lingting Zhu, Yingda Yin, Runze Zhang, Li Yuan, Xin Wang, Long Quan

entry.summary: MSVS-VAE is a hierarchical set-based 3D VAE that progressively densifies anchored VecSet latents through point-shuffle upsampling to close the fidelity gap with sparse-voxel representations while staying compact. Since VAE reconstruction quality bottlenecks 3D latent diffusion, this targets a key upstream component.

entry.title: Nova3D: Code-Native Generation of Programmable 3D Assets

author.name: Nimra Noor, Muhammad Bilal, Abdullah Hussain, Hassan Baig

entry.summary: Nova3D generates 3D assets as executable Blender programs so that named parts, assembly hierarchy, constraints, edit handles, and joints exist at generation time rather than being recovered by later segmentation or rigging. It is evaluated on a frozen 54-item spec-grounded benchmark against eleven baselines.

entry.title: Semantic Semi-Incremental Data-Association-Free Object SLAM

author.name: Yihao Zhang, Jungseok Hong, John J. Leonard

entry.summary: Presents a SLAM framework from an MIT group that jointly infers data associations, poses, landmark positions and landmark semantics, using both geometric measurements and semantic features from neural detectors and vision foundation models. It removes the need for a separate hard data-association step.

entry.title: LEACL: LLM-Enhanced Automatic Curriculum Learning for Reinforcement Learning in Long-Horizon Manipulation Tasks

author.name: Faraz Heravi, James Ouyang, Zifan Xu, Arjun Kumar, Yoonchang Sung, Peter Stone

entry.summary: LEACL uses large language models to decompose long-horizon manipulation tasks into subtasks and difficulty measures, automating the task-specification work that normally must be hand-crafted for automatic curriculum learning. Co-authored by Peter Stone's group.

entry.title: A Few Words Go a Long Way: Language Guided Robot Policy Synthesis

author.name: Daphne Chen, Archit Ritesh Jain, Eric Goossen, Emma Romig, Michael Murray, Nick Walker, Maya Cakmak

entry.summary: ARCHITECT reframes robot policy acquisition as interactive program synthesis, having an LLM coding agent compose modular perception and control tools into readable programs that users can inspect, correct and iteratively refine. It positions modular synthesis as an interpretable alternative to black-box VLA policies.

entry.title: PAC-DP: PAC-Bayesian Diffusion Policy Learning

author.name: Mohammad Hasan Yeganegi, Dian Yu, Andrea Del Prete, Majid Khadiv, Matteo Saveriano

entry.summary: PAC-DP treats a diffusion policy as a Bayesian neural network and derives a PAC-Bayes generalization bound, adding a KL regularizer between posterior and prior parameter distributions to the standard denoising loss. This gives a principled way to control generalization of diffusion policies in the small-data regime typical of robotics.

entry.title: Bridging Reinforcement Learning and Optimal Control via Feasible Action Mapping

author.name: Stefan Richter, Alberto Giammarino, Guillem Torrente, Sam Blakeman, Peter D\"urr

entry.summary: FAOC introduces an optimization-based mapping that converts an RL agent's abstract action into a state-dependent feasible parameter set for an optimal control problem, guaranteeing hard constraint satisfaction while retaining RL flexibility. It targets recursive feasibility and safety in constrained dynamical systems.

entry.title: Identification and Learning of Semantic Observation Kernels: Partial Observation, Uniform Recovery, & Minimax Limits

author.name: Matthew Francis Dixon

entry.summary: Asks when probabilities produced by a language model can be mapped to a reproducible posterior over a finite set of real-world states, noting that verbalized percentages from LLMs are generated text rather than calibrated state beliefs. Builds a semiparametric inverse from grouped meaning-equivalent continuation probabilities to state probabilities, with identification and minimax rate results.

entry.title: Debiased Machine Learning: Identification, Estimation, and Shape Constraints

author.name: Qihui Chen, Ka Yan Cheng, Zheng Fang

entry.summary: Provides a general identification and estimation theory for automatic debiased machine learning, showing when the Riesz representer at the heart of DML is identified and that identification coincides with unique optimization of a quadratic functional. This yields a general estimation procedure, including under shape constraints.

entry.title: Multi-Turn Drift Increases Scheming

author.name: Carlos Guerrero Alvarez

entry.summary: Reports an empirical finding that scheming behavior in language models increases when a multi-turn conversation gradually drifts toward misalignment, and identifies a specific scenario type with elevated rates. Offers hypotheses about the mechanism and situates the work in the broader scheming literature.

entry.title: Through the Bottleneck: How Multi-head Latent Attention Separates Content from Position in Language Models

author.name: Dhruvil S, Fenil Sojitra, Ravirajsinh Chauhan

entry.summary: The authors present a mechanistic interpretability study of multi-head latent attention, the compressed key-value scheme popularized in DeepSeek models, training a 114M-parameter transformer and probing what the shared low-rank bottleneck keeps or discards. They report the compressed cache learns a largely content-only representation with positional information handled separately, and trace how circuits reorganize around the bottleneck.

entry.title: In-Context Learning as Implicit Policy Gradient

author.name: Masahiro Kaneko, Timothy Baldwin

entry.summary: This paper argues that in-context learning with generated samples and their scores structurally corresponds to policy gradient optimization, giving a constructive proof that self-attention can implement reward-weighted aggregation resembling REINFORCE under particular weight configurations. It provides theoretical footing for empirically observed self-improvement through score-conditioned prompting.

entry.title: Breaking the Total Variance Barrier: Sharp Sample Complexity for Linear Heteroscedastic Bandits with Fixed Action Set

author.name: Heyang Zhao, Tianyuan Jin, Weixin Wang, Vincent Y. F. Tan, Pan Xu, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: Argues that the standard cumulative-variance complexity measure for heteroscedastic linear bandits is loose, since it is insensitive to rounds with near-zero noise, and derives sharper sample-complexity bounds for fixed action sets. This tightens the theory underlying variance-aware exploration.

entry.title: UNIFUSION: Adapting Autoregressive Language Models into Discrete Diffusion under a Unified Reverse-Rate Objective

author.name: Xiaoyi Jiang, Jingyuan Li, Yixuan Jiang, Wei Liu, Yi Zhu, Zuoqiang Shi, Pipi Hu

entry.summary: UNIFUSION unifies several discrete diffusion training objectives, including SEDD, MDLM/GIDD, M2S, and neural continuous-time Markov chain formulations, as a single generalized KL objective over reverse rates, and derives conversions between clean-token, concrete-score, posterior-mean, and jump parameterizations. This shared interface lets pretrained autoregressive checkpoints be adapted to uniform-noise diffusion where every token stays editable rather than only masked diffusion.

entry.title: CRAFT: Learn the Schema, Execute the Plan

author.name: Aakash Kolekar, Sahika Genc, Shahriar Shariat, Bunyamin Sisman, Tibor Mezi, Barbara Poblete, Shree Vandana Kachroo, Calvin Chi, Parth Parmar, Ari Singer, Prayaas Jain, Cindy Barker, Benoit Dumoulin

entry.summary: CRAFT post-trains enterprise coding agents so that proprietary schema and tool knowledge lives in weights rather than being stuffed into every prompt, using schema-stripped plan supervised fine-tuning followed by a second stage for executable behavior. This cuts inference overhead and improves multi-turn analytical reliability.

entry.title: Invariant Discovery for Networked Systems

author.name: Hongyu H\`e, Alexander Krentsel, Sylvia Ratnasamy, Maria Apostolaki

entry.summary: Splits automatic invariant mining for networked systems into an LLM-driven discovery of the candidate grammar and a deterministic search for approximate rules that tolerate real measurement noise. This removes the hardest human input while keeping learning reproducible and auditable.

entry.title: LA-RL: Label-Aware Self-Reflection for Reinforcement Learning in Information Extraction

author.name: Xiao You, Tianwei Yan, Zixu Shan, Longyu Du, Shan Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces a reinforcement learning framework for information extraction where the model first predicts an extraction, then diagnoses task-specific error labels such as missing span, wrong label, boundary mismatch, or reversed arguments, then revises conditioned on that diagnosis. Replaces vague free-form self-reflection with structured diagnostic supervision.

entry.title: MoLGE: Mixture of Language Group Experts for Efficient Scaling of Massively Multilingual Speech Recognition

author.name: Sangmin Lee, Woojin Chung, Woongjib Choi, Hong-Goo Kang

entry.summary: Proposes grouping similar languages into shared expert modules for massively multilingual ASR built on speech self-supervised backbones, cutting the number of experts needed versus per-language mixture-of-experts. Adds hierarchical LoRA over disentangled acoustic and linguistic components to counter capacity dilution.

entry.title: $\gamma$-Bridge: A Look-Parametric Diffusion Bridge

author.name: Xuran Hu, Yujie Zhu, Tengxi Wang, Jilong Li, Wufan Zhao

entry.summary: gamma-Bridge is a diffusion bridge whose schedule is parameterized by the physical radar look number rather than an abstract SNR schedule, with exact multiplicative Gamma marginals and a closed-form reverse posterior. This lets one trained model handle different SAR speckle levels and transfer better to real data lacking clean ground truth.

entry.title: Rethinking Expert Training for Model Merging with Prompt Learning

author.name: Christos Georgakilas, Aniello Panariello, Samir El Karrat Moreno, Simone Calderara, Dimosthenis Karatzas, Joost van de Weijer

entry.summary: Revisits how experts are trained for model merging, showing that prompt-based adaptation with a frozen backbone is a strong baseline that avoids weight-merging interference, then proposes Dual-Tuned Experts combining prompt learning with subsequent encoder fine-tuning. The focus shifts from better merging algorithms to better mergeable experts.

entry.title: MicroZoom: Structure-Preserving Detail Synthesis at Extreme Scale

author.name: Huy Huynh, Jingwei Ma, Brian Curless, Ira Kemelmacher-Shlizerman, Steven M. Seitz

entry.summary: MicroZoom synthesizes seamless gigapixel imagery at microscopic scale by combining a standard photograph with sparse consumer-microscope close-ups as material references, at magnifications up to 350x. It emphasizes plausible structure-preserving detail synthesis rather than exact reconstruction.

entry.title: DeVA: Decoupled Video-Action Model with physical guidance for robot policy learning

author.name: Mengqi Zhang, Sahil Khose, Simar Kareer, Yuchen Song, Unnat Jain, Judy Hoffman

entry.summary: DeVA decouples video prediction from action prediction in a vision-language-action robot policy, using a video generative model as a physical-dynamics prior that guides but does not share a backbone with the action head. It targets the weak physical-dynamics supervision in static VLA pretraining.

entry.title: {\tau}: Learning Touch-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Models from Future Visual Supervision

author.name: Ning Cheng, Jinan Xu, Wanlin Li, Yangzhi Chen, Jing Gao, Yiqun Wang, Kelan Peng, Wenjuan Han

entry.summary: Introduces a touch-augmented VLA framework that learns action-conditioned spatiotemporal tactile representations supervised by future visual observations in a JEPA-inspired scheme, avoiding costly large-scale tactile pretraining. It targets high-dimensional tactile signals that prior methods reduced to instantaneous contact states or 6D wrenches.

entry.title: KAI: A Kinematic-Aware Interface for Data-Efficient Articulated Object Manipulation

author.name: Yaping Li, Zhaxizhuoma, Qiaojun Yu, Jia Zeng, Dahua Lin, Jiangmiao Pang

entry.summary: KAI introduces a structured intermediate representation encoding kinematic and geometric priors of articulated objects, used as an inductive bias for manipulation policy learning. It reports around 83 percent average success across six simulated tasks while using half the demonstration data of baselines.

entry.title: TILT: Improving Compositional Generation in Diffusion Models with a Model-Intrinsic Reward

author.name: Debottam Dutta, Jaehoon Hahm, Jianchong Chen, Romit Roy Choudhury

entry.summary: TILT improves compositional text-to-image generation at test time by defining a reward intrinsic to the diffusion model itself, based on overlap between joint and single-concept distributions, rather than using an external reward model. This yields a KL-constrained tilted target distribution with closed-form guidance steps.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Mission-Level Evaluation for Aerial MLLM Agents

author.name: Suman Navaratnarajah, Taehyoung Kim, Jona Ruthardt, Ishaan Bhimwal, Ryousuke Yamada, Yannik Blei, Wolfram Burgard, Yuki M Asano

entry.summary: MissionBench evaluates multimodal LLMs as aerial embodied agents that must plan, navigate and report from a single high-level instruction using only egocentric observations, across 120 missions in five simulated 3D environments. The best of 22 open and closed models completes under 35 percent of missions versus 84.4 percent for humans.

entry.title: The Regression Tax: Decomposing Why Skills Help and Hurt LLM Agents

author.name: Darshan Tank, Baran Nama

entry.summary: Measures both sides of giving agents procedural skills across nearly 6,000 runs on two office automation benchmarks and three harness stacks, distinguishing regressions (tasks solved without skills but failed with them) from residual failures. It finds the best skill sets win mainly by regressing less rather than by adding wins, and identifies causes including misleading skill descriptions.

entry.title: Adversarial Style Optimization: Enhancing VLM Jailbreaks by GRPO-based Stylistic Triggers Optimization

author.name: Bingjun Luo, Jialin Guo, Yue Yao, Xinpeng Ding

entry.summary: Reports a stylistic inconsistency in multimodal LLMs, where models understand content robustly across visual styles yet their safety mechanisms can be bypassed by particular stylistic triggers. The authors use GRPO to optimize such triggers into a plug-and-play module that amplifies existing jailbreaks.

entry.title: J-CoT: Chain-of-Thought in J-Space

author.name: Junde Wu, Jiayuan Zhu, Fengling Liu, Minhao Hu, Jiazhen Pan

entry.summary: J-CoT proposes a recurrent reasoning interface between fully verbalized chain-of-thought and opaque continuous latent states, passing linguistically grounded but not fully decoded representations across steps. The aim is an explicit mechanism for selecting and organizing information for the next reasoning step, which dense hidden-vector recurrence lacks.

entry.title: TriGlue: a Biology-Inspired Generative Model for Generating Molecular Glue-Induced Ternary Complex

author.name: Yuliang Yan, Shuo Yan, Haochun Tang, Yiqin Sun, Enyan Dai

entry.summary: TriGlue formulates molecular glue design as generation of an entire ternary complex, decomposing the problem into ligand generation, protein-protein docking, and complex assembly in a biology-inspired generative framework. This addresses the fact that molecular glue design lacks a known protein-protein interface, unlike conventional structure-based drug design.

entry.title: Robot Learning to Communicate through Projected Visual Abstractions

author.name: Danyang Yan, Boyuan Wang, Jiaxun Liu, Boyuan Chen

entry.summary: The authors build a robotic system that communicates through projected visual abstractions, specifically dynamic shadows cast by a 21-degree-of-freedom dexterous hand, requiring reasoning about both bodily motion and how it maps into the externally perceived projection. Shadows are chosen because they arise from embodiment yet are visually distinct from the body.

entry.title: CORVUS: Context Optimization and Reduction Via Underlying Synchronization for LLM Coding Agents

author.name: Mingwei Zheng, David OBrien, Siwei Cui, Pardis Pashakhanloo, Rajdeep Mukherjee, Myeongsoo Kim, Sachit Kuhar

entry.summary: CORVUS restructures LLM coding-agent trajectories by decoupling file-read actions from their observations, maintaining a synchronized view instead of append-only chronological snapshots that go stale as files are edited. This is intended to prevent reasoning errors from outdated file contents and to stop the context bloat caused by repeated re-reads.

entry.title: Learning Sampling Parameters for Diffusion Models

author.name: Arisrei Lim, Yossi Gandelsman

entry.summary: LeSAMP trains a language model with reinforcement learning to emit prompt-conditioned, timestep-varying schedules for diffusion sampling knobs such as guidance scale, negative prompts, and noise schedules, rewarded by human-preference and vision-language judges. It replaces the usual practice of fixing these hyperparameters globally across all prompts.

entry.title: Chamaileon: Cross-Context Binder Design with Contextualized Modeling and Mixed Sampling

author.name: Hengyuan Cao, Shizhuo Cheng, Mingxuan Liu, Weicheng Huang, Yunhong Lu, Chenxi Cai, Yan Zhang, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Chamaileon generalizes generative protein binder design beyond the usual single-target, single-state setting by framing the task as modeling a cross-context binding landscape, trained with an in-context complex co-design objective and mixed sampling. This enables binders intended to work across multiple targets or conformational states.

entry.title: Context Is King: How In-Context Specification Shapes the Geometry of Concepts

author.name: Elad David, Max Fomin

entry.summary: Challenges the view that LLM concept geometries such as circular weekday manifolds are fixed stored world models, showing that an in-context declarative rule determines not just the relations encoded but the topology type, turning the same tokens into a cycle or a branching tree on demand. The effect appears even on arbitrary meaningless tokens, and context-specified structure can override strong pretrained priors in capable models.

entry.title: DRC-Aid: Design-Rule Correction via Agentic Framework utilizing Inference-Time Large Language Models

author.name: Anushka Mukherjee, Kang He, Kaushik Roy

entry.summary: DRC-Aid closes the loop on chip layout design-rule repair by having a deterministic rule engine convert violations into a bounded menu of geometric edits, an off-the-shelf LLM choose among them from local context, and commercial verification tools validate each step with backtracking. The bounded action space keeps the combinatorial search tractable.

entry.title: Two-Timescale Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Resilient Operations

author.name: Young Hyun Cho, Franz Stoll, Will Wei Sun, Guang Lin, Stephan Biller

entry.summary: The paper develops a two-timescale hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for operations problems where long-horizon and short-horizon decisions are coupled, and proves what the authors claim are the first convergence guarantees for synchronized coupled two-timescale learning. It targets resilience to recurring supply and demand shocks.

entry.title: To Erase, or Not to Erase: Robust Training-Free Concept Erasure with Preservation aware Adaptive Ranked Subspace Expansion

author.name: Shaswati Saha, Rajasekhar Anguluri, Manas Gaur

entry.summary: This work proposes a training-free concept erasure method for text-to-image diffusion models that adaptively expands a ranked subspace based on how prompts actually steer denoising, rather than relying on static concept banks. The goal is robust removal of NSFW or copyrighted concepts without degrading benign generation.
