author.name: Haochen Liang, Jie Zhang, Hideya Ochiai

entry.summary: FedTaste tackles multimodal federated learning when clients are missing modalities by transferring group-level relational structure rather than aligning fragile per-sample features. The approach is parameter-efficient and avoids generative imputation or external auxiliary data.

entry.title: PathRIR: Physics-Guided Acoustic Path Selection and Late-Tail Compensation for Fast Room Impulse Response Simulation

author.name: Shaoheng Xu, Chunyi Sun, Jihui Zhang, Amy Bastine, Prasanga N. Samarasinghe, Thushara D. Abhayapala

entry.summary: PathRIR speeds up image-source-method room impulse response simulation by learning which acoustic reflection paths matter and pruning the rest, then using a small MLP to predict and regenerate the missing late reverberation energy. It preserves physical interpretability while cutting cost on complex 3D rooms.

entry.title: When Every Simulation Counts: Value-Based Reinforcement Learning for Accelerated Photonics Inverse Design

author.name: Longying Wen, Feiyang Wu, Jinglin Yu, Chongxian Yuan, Renjie Li, Zhaoyu Zhang

entry.summary: The authors benchmark baseline DQN plus six value-learning variants for inverse design of photonic-crystal surface-emitting lasers under a tight 83-simulation budget, with matched initializations and a shared objective. Dueling DQN emerges as the most reliable under extreme sample scarcity.

entry.title: Distributed Convolutional Rank Regression over Decentralized Networks

author.name: Chunjing Li, Tiange Zhao, Xiaohui Yuan

entry.summary: The paper develops decentralized convolution rank regression over networks, using consensus-constrained optimization with a kernel-smoothed rank loss so nodes share only with neighbors. It establishes finite-sample error bounds and exact support recovery for the sparse LASSO variant, solved with generalized consensus ADMM.

entry.title: Cross-Attention Calibrated Deduplication for Retrieval-Augmented Generation System

author.name: Phuong Le Huy, Nam H. Nguyen, Quan V. Dang

entry.summary: CACD deduplicates RAG chunks using a cross-encoder comparison against a pool of already-retained chunks, preserving token-level interaction rather than collapsing each chunk to a single pooled vector for cosine thresholding. The goal is smaller vector databases and faster retrieval without discarding genuinely distinct near-topic chunks.

entry.title: The balance between compactness and forecast accuracy of data-driven latent-space reduced-order models in controlled wake flows

author.name: Alberto Solera-Rico, Patricia Garc\'ia-Caspue\~nas, Carlos Sanmiguel Vila, Stefano Discetti

entry.summary: Compares POD, convolutional autoencoders, and two variational autoencoder variants as spatial encoders for latent-space reduced-order models of actuated wake flows, then evaluates how well latent coordinates support time-stepping prediction. Highlights a tradeoff between latent compactness and forecast accuracy for real-time flow control.

entry.title: A Model for Imbalanced Label Aggregation: A Focus on Minority-Class Detection

author.name: Gabriel Singer, Samuel Gruffaz, Olivier Vo Van, Nicolas Vayatis, Argyris Kalogeratos

entry.summary: Introduces a generative label-aggregation model for crowdsourcing that jointly captures class-dependent annotator accuracy and item difficulty, targeting settings where the rare minority class matters most. Fills a gap left by prior models that handle one factor but not both.

entry.title: Speech Signals Complement LLMs for Predicting Interpersonal Attraction in Speed Dating

author.name: Yuriko Kikuchi, Takato Hayashi, Ryusei Kimura, Naoya Inoue, Ryo Ishii, Shogo Okada

entry.summary: Tests whether a supervised speech predictor adds information beyond a transcript-only LLM when predicting reported interpersonal attraction in Japanese speed-dating conversations. Finds combining modalities reliably improves pairwise ranking but that per-participant correlation gains are conditional on round and rating dimension.

entry.title: Do Diagrams Help Large Language Models Reason? Evidence from Syllogistic Reasoning

author.name: Risako Ando, Koji Mineshima

entry.summary: Compares natural language, logical notation, linear diagrams, and Euler diagrams as input formats for 285 syllogistic reasoning problems on two older models, finding diagrams do not reliably help. Models handle entailment and contradiction reasonably but fail on neutral cases and commit systematic conversion errors resembling human fallacies.

entry.title: HiTMS: A High-Throughput Multi-Stream Linguistic Steganography Framework

author.name: Ruiyi Yan, Yugo Murawaki, Zhongliang Yang

entry.summary: HiTMS extends generative linguistic steganography from single-stream to multi-stream, spreading a secret across several batched responses over successive interaction rounds to raise throughput while hiding slot occupancy and payload completion. Includes wrapping to ensure recoverability under batched inference.

entry.title: Histopathological Spectrum-Guided Prostate Stratification via Segmentation-Assisted Diagnostic Transformer

author.name: Leyang Li, Lihua Chen, Huangang Hu, Tianhang Hao, Hao Cheng, Xin Zhang, Qianru Sun, Bingxu Lu, Wenlong Yu, Feng Duan

entry.summary: Constructs a prostate cancer histopathology spectrum dataset and reformulates mpMRI assessment as a four-class clinically meaningful classification instead of PI-RADS scoring or binary labels. Proposes a language-guided, segmentation-assisted transformer using zero-shot segmentation for anatomical priors plus multi-modal slice fusion.

entry.title: Post-Operative Glioma Segmentation via Loss Stabilization, Normalization and Subspace Attention

author.name: Alexandru Cri\c{s}an, Diana Borza

entry.summary: Ablation study showing that Generalized Dice Loss is unstable for post-operative glioma segmentation under domain shift, with whole-lesion Dice dropping sharply on an external cohort. Combines brain-masked percentile normalization, voxel-level contrastive learning and a subspace-aware class attention module to recover robustness.

entry.title: Gaze-Anchored Social Net: Decoding Implicit Relations via Joint Modeling

author.name: Yuqi Hou, Zhuo Chen, Han Hu, Je Woo Kim, Jianbo Jiao, Hyung Jin Chang

entry.summary: Proposes ANCHOR, a target-centric framework that jointly models gaze estimation and social relation inference in static multi-person images, arguing social intent drives gaze rather than being a post-hoc label. Aims to replace independent per-person gaze prediction with relational joint modeling.

entry.title: HALLELUAI: A Hallucination-Aware AI System for Ultra-Realistic Image-to-Video Generation at Scale

author.name: Aniket Sakpal, Yang Jiang, Rouzbeh Davoudi, Shayan Hassantabar, Mani Najmabadi

entry.summary: HALLELUAI is a production system that moderates image-to-video generations for aesthetics, motion fidelity, and hallucination risk, then iteratively regenerates failures through prompt refinement and targeted edits. Aimed at scaling quality control for commercial creative video pipelines.

entry.title: mmSimPrior: Learning Simulation Priors for Data-Efficient Real-World Generalizable Radar-Based Human Motion Reconstruction

author.name: Cheng Guo, Qiming Cao, Shengkai Xu, Haoyu Xie, Kaixiang Su, Pu Wang, Hongfei Xue

entry.summary: mmSimPrior pretrains radar-based human motion reconstruction on simulated mmWave data using physics-informed domain randomization, factorizing transferable knowledge into signal, motion, and radar-to-motion mapping priors. Goal is data-efficient generalization to real deployments where paired radar-motion data is scarce.

entry.title: Out-of-Length Scene Text Recognition: A Two-Axis Diagnosis and a Training-Free Fix

author.name: Zobeir Raisi, John Zelek

entry.summary: Diagnoses why scene text recognizers fail on text longer than their 25-character training crops, separating encoder width extrapolation from decoder length extrapolation and showing encoder width dominates. Proposes a training-free fix after showing rotary rescaling and fine-tuning only partially help.

entry.title: GaitFace: A Multimodal Dataset for Long-Range Person Identification

author.name: Alain Komaty, Luis S. Luevano, Vidit Vidit, Anjith George, Zeina Al Amine, S\'ebastien Marcel

entry.summary: Releases GaitFace, a public multimodal dataset of face and gait captured at long range for person identification, motivated by border-control throughput and the restricted access to existing government datasets. Addresses degraded imagery and adverse atmospheric conditions.

entry.title: PathSelect: Sequential Token Selection for Whole Slide Pathology

author.name: Jingzhi Chen, Landi He, Zehong Chen, Peihang Wu, Lijian Xu

entry.summary: PathSelect reframes token pruning for gigapixel whole-slide pathology as a learned sequential selection problem, plugged into a frozen pretrained slide-language model so both the slide encoder and language model stay unchanged. Motivated by the risk that spatial sampling or static pruning discards weak but diagnostic signals.

entry.title: GRAPE: Graduated Routing for Articulated Portrait mesh Estimation

author.name: Yunfei Liu, Lijian Lin, Ye Zhu, Yu Li

entry.summary: GRAPE estimates articulated portrait meshes with graduated routing, addressing the floating-head problem of face-centric morphable models (which conflate head pose with global rotation for lack of neck kinematics) and the weak expressions of body-centric models. Also disentangles jaw articulation from expression blendshapes.

entry.title: A Unified Stereo Geometry Estimation Framework for Disparity and Surface Normal

author.name: Qizhe Wei, Xianda Guo, Shaocong Xu, Hong Li, Runyi Yang, Hao Zhao

entry.summary: GeoStereo couples a feed-forward stereo matching pipeline with a diffusion-based surface-normal branch, using disparity-to-normal initialization and warped left-view conditioning so the two tasks reinforce each other. The goal is more reliable geometry in ill-posed regions where stereo alone fails.

entry.title: MATS: A novel multi-modality multi-task learning framework for 3D perception in autonomous driving

author.name: Junchen Huo, Wanming Hao, Song Wang, Enqing Chen, Shouyi Yang, Guanghui Wang

entry.summary: MATS is a multi-modal multi-task 3D perception framework for driving that replaces a single shared bird's-eye-view map with modality-adaptive fusion and task-specific mixture-of-experts heads. The claim is that one BEV feature map cannot serve detection, segmentation, and other tasks simultaneously.

entry.title: MAViE: A Multi-scale Adaptive Vision Encoder for Fine-grained Visual Perception and Efficient Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Shaofei Lei

entry.summary: MAViE fuses shallow, intermediate, and deep vision transformer features with position-dependent gates and then routes tokens to the language model based on question relevance and information content under an adaptive budget. The goal is fine-grained perception, including text and spatial relations, without long-context latency blowup.

entry.title: Spatio-Temporal Conditional Denoising Transformer for Modality-Missing RGBT Tracking

author.name: Andong Lu, Ziyi Zha, Jiandong Jin, Shihao Li, Chenglong Li, Jin Tang, Bin Luo

entry.summary: SCDT is a spatio-temporal conditional denoising transformer that unifies handling of missing and complete modalities in RGB-thermal tracking, reconstructing absent modalities and enhancing weak ones using spatial and temporal context. It avoids the brittleness of generating full missing modalities in hard scenarios.

entry.title: Occlusion-Point Reuse for Ray-Traced Ambient Occlusion and Shadow

author.name: Haojie Jin, Fujia Su, Zehui Lin, Chenxiao Hu, Jierui Ren, Yuqing Yuan, Yanchen Zhang, Zhongtao Wang, Yisong Chen, Kangying Cai, Guoping Wang, Sheng Li

entry.summary: Introduces an occlusion-point reuse framework for real-time ray-traced ambient occlusion and area-light shadows that reuses samples in the domain of first-hit occlusion points rather than reusing final shading values. This provides a ray-reuse formulation instead of post-hoc denoising of completed estimates.

entry.title: Codebook Capacity Governs Perceptual Quality Across Resolutions in Hierarchical Discrete Video Compression

author.name: Manikanta Kotthapalli, Banafsheh Rekabdar

entry.summary: A controlled study of hierarchical discrete (VQ-VAE style) video codecs finds that perceptual quality tracks codebook capacity almost log-linearly while being nearly insensitive to spatial resolution. This suggests discrete latent codecs may avoid the resolution-specific retraining needed by continuous-latent learned codecs.

entry.title: Mixing Configurations for Downstream Prediction

author.name: Juntang Wang, Hao Wu, Yihan Wang, Dongmian Zou, Shixin Xu

entry.summary: Introduces Configuration-Mixed Prediction and a plug-in module, MixConfig, that avoids picking a single clustering resolution by extracting the finite set of structurally stable partitions from a frozen embedding and learning per-sample mixing weights over them. It turns an ad hoc hyperparameter choice into a learned, context-aware feature augmentation.

entry.title: Attenuated Heterogeneity in Fixed-Effects Causal Forests, and a Cross-Fitted Correction

author.name: Harry Aytug

entry.summary: Shows that averaging honest leaf-level effects across trees in fixed-effects causal forests systematically compresses estimated treatment-effect heterogeneity toward the mean, and that the usual additive recentering does not fix it. Proposes a cross-fitted correction and benchmarks against a generalized random forest.

entry.title: The true "test" dataset for a generalised task

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: Argues that when the intended task is genuinely general, the test set should be drawn from a deliberately different part of the distribution than training, for example training on Python and testing on Java. This reframes generalization evaluation as a test of whether the intended abstraction was learned rather than a narrow proxy.

entry.title: Hidden Boundary Motion in Transformer Optimization: Function-Space Orthogonalization of Affine Weight and Bias Updates

author.name: Zhang Gongyue, Sheng Yixuan, Liu donghan, Wang Zhiyong, Ren Weihong, Liu honghai

entry.summary: The authors observe that when layer inputs have nonzero mean, part of a weight update acts functionally like a bias update, and they decompose gradients into a sample-varying shape component and a shared boundary component. In a small transformer trained from scratch, this hidden bias-like term is a large fraction of the raw weight-gradient norm, suggesting optimizers implicitly conflate two distinct functional changes.

entry.title: Spectral-Aware Analytic Class-Incremental Learning for Long-Tailed Distributions

author.name: Quyen Tran, Hai Nguyen, Quan Dao, Zhuowei Li, Nam Le, Trung Le, Dimitris Metaxas

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses why recursive-least-squares analytic continual learning collapses under long-tailed class-incremental settings, showing tail-class subspaces suffer spectral collapse indistinguishable from noise, and proposes a spectral-aware correction that plain ridge regularization cannot supply. It combines a clear failure analysis with a targeted fix.

entry.title: Finite-Time Analysis of the Natural Policy Gradient in Finite-Horizon Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Asha Barua, Sajad Khodadadian

entry.summary: The paper provides the first finite-time convergence guarantees for exact natural policy gradient in finite-horizon MDPs with known, horizon-dependent dynamics, proving a sublinear rate under constant step size and faster behavior with increasing step sizes. NPG underlies TRPO and PPO, so filling this analytical gap is theoretically relevant.

entry.title: StageGuard: Physiologically Constrained Sleep Staging

author.name: Juntang Wang, Yihan Wang, Hao Wu, Jiayu Gao, Shixin Xu, Dongmian Zou

entry.summary: StageGuard wraps any neural sleep-staging model with physiology-informed structured inference, including a differentiable penalty on implausible transitions, so predicted hypnograms respect known sleep architecture constraints. This matters because epoch-level accuracy can be high while derived clinical endpoints like REM latency and fragmentation are biased by illegal transitions.

entry.title: Learning Reusable Hybrid Motion Priors for Humanoid Locomotion from Motion Imitation

author.name: Valerio Belli (UNIROMA, UCL), Valerio Modugno (UCL), Enrico Mingo Hoffman (HUCEBOT), Fabio Amadio (HUCEBOT)

entry.summary: A three-stage pipeline turns humanoid motion-imitation experts into a reusable hybrid motion prior by distilling them into a frozen proprioceptive encoder plus residual vector-quantized latent structure, which downstream task policies can then reuse. This avoids retraining a bespoke policy and reward for every new locomotion task.

entry.title: Perturbative-NeuSA: A Structured Spectral Framework for Time-Dependent PDEs

author.name: Xianli Zhu, Jia Yin

entry.summary: Perturbative-NeuSA decomposes a time-dependent PDE solution into a cheap low-fidelity background plus a learned high-resolution perturbation, so the network only models unresolved dynamics rather than the entire field. Tests span 2D Burgers, Klein-Gordon, and heterogeneous wave equations.

entry.title: Cortex: Compact Behavior Cloning for Quake with Frozen Visual Features

author.name: Dzmitry Malyshau

entry.summary: Cortex trains an eleven-million-parameter six-layer transformer policy head on frozen DINOv3 features to play Quake from pixels, using a large public behavior-cloning corpus of recorded human play. It quantifies how far pure imitation with no memory or RL can get, training in minutes per epoch on a single consumer GPU.

entry.title: On the Order-Conditional Optimality of Gaffke's Bound

author.name: George Bissias, Erik Learned-Miller

entry.summary: Recasts classical Buehler-style construction of lower confidence bounds in probabilistic terms and proves that Gaffke's bound is optimal for the ordering it induces on the maximum marginal mean of independent nonnegative variables. The framework is intended to be more accessible and extensible than the original formulations.

entry.title: Accuracy potential of visual localization exploiting high-end street-level imagery

author.name: Jonas Meyer, Stephan Nebiker, Pascal Theiler, Norbert Haala

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates the accuracy ceiling of visual localization against survey-grade requirements using precisely georeferenced high-resolution street-level imagery with sub-centimeter ground truth. It contributes both a scalable localization pipeline and a dataset addressing a missing evaluation regime.

entry.title: Frequency-Aware Dual-Stream Learning for Balanced Realism and Fidelity in Electron Microscopy Imaging

author.name: Longmi Gao, Zhengkai Zhao, Pan Gao, Manoranjan Paul

entry.summary: Uses wavelet decomposition to split electron microscopy image restoration into a conditional diffusion branch for realistic low-frequency structure and a transformer branch for faithful high-frequency detail. This dual-stream design targets the trade-off between perceptual realism and quantitative fidelity that causes either over-smoothing or hallucination.

entry.title: A Controlled Visual-Backbone Benchmark for Multimodal Short-Term Solar Irradiance Forecasting

author.name: Oshadha Samarakoon, Dushan Herath, Ishara Ranmandala, Dilshara Herath, Roshan Godaliyadda, Parakrama Ekanayake, Vijitha Herath

entry.summary: A tightly controlled benchmark that holds an entire multimodal solar irradiance forecasting pipeline fixed and varies only the visual backbone, comparing ConvNeXt, Swin, and three Mamba variants. It aims to disentangle backbone contribution from confounded pipeline changes typical in this literature.

entry.title: Quality-Adaptive Multi-UAV 3D Reconstruction with Sparse Workload Redistribution

author.name: Benjamin Sportich, Kenza Boubakri, Olivier Simonin, Alessandro Renzaglia

entry.summary: Proposes a decentralized multi-UAV exploration strategy that adapts viewpoint generation and information gain to a user-specified 3D reconstruction fidelity target using TSDF confidence. Adds two coordination levels including sparse workload redistribution among drones.

entry.title: Development of a Handheld Actuation Mechanism for a Tendon-driven Robotically Steered Guidewire

author.name: Saima Chavenet, Timothy A. Brumfiel, Revanth Konda, Jaydev P. Desai

entry.summary: Describes a handheld actuation device with a compact spooling mechanism that gives clinicians both motorized tip steering and conventional manual control of a tendon-driven robotic guidewire for endovascular procedures. Aims to reduce vessel damage from difficult manual navigation.

entry.title: Transferable Latency Prediction for Fast LLM Screening on Heterogeneous Edge Devices

author.name: Xiaolong Tu, Vinod K. Mishra, Venkat R. Dasari, Anu G. Bourgeois, Haoxin Wang

entry.summary: Presents a runtime-aware latency prediction framework for choosing which LLM to deploy on heterogeneous edge hardware, modeling each request as a hardware-runtime-model-prompt configuration and splitting prefill from decode. It fuses static descriptors with live hardware telemetry through a gated predictor and validates on Pixel phones.

entry.title: Discrete Action Space as a Prerequisite for GRPO Convergence in Small-Model Continuous Control

author.name: Dmytro Filatov, Valentyn Fedorov, Vira Filatova

entry.summary: Reports that GRPO fine-tuning of a 0.5B language model for continuous quadrotor velocity control collapses to the zero action with entropy crashing early in training, and that removing the jerk penalty or KL anchor prevents entropy collapse but still does not enable learning. Replacing the continuous interface with a five-way categorical choice over PID presets makes training converge.

entry.title: Wavelet Phase Diffusion for Structurally and Semantically Consistent Sim-to-Real Translation

author.name: Kaiwen Wang, Frank Bieder, Yinzhe Shen, Carlos Fernandez, Jan-Hendrik Pauls, Omer Sahin Tas

entry.summary: Proposes a wavelet-domain phase-preserving diffusion method for simulation-to-reality image translation that keeps structure and semantics intact while closing the appearance gap. It replaces global Fourier phase preservation, which the authors argue causes ringing and boundary leakage due to global spectral coupling, with spatially localized wavelet phase constraints.

entry.title: DAGForge: Auditable Causal DAG Authoring with Biomedical Literature

author.name: Yi-han Sheu, Michael R. Steigman, Yu Zhou, Bo Wang, Fan-Yu Yen, Jordan W. Smoller

entry.summary: DAGForge is a browser tool for authoring causal directed acyclic graphs in biomedical research, using an LLM to generate pairwise causal judgments grounded in verbatim literature excerpts and assembling them into a constraint-checked graph. Every edge carries confidence, provenance, and a reproducible literature snapshot for expert audit.

entry.title: Control panels to clarify user intent with Large Language Models

author.name: Ben Shneiderman

entry.summary: A short position paper by a prominent HCI researcher proposing visual control panel interfaces for LLMs instead of a blank prompt box, giving users semantic cues about what can be specified. The argument rests on favoring recognition over recall so users can express intent more effectively.

entry.title: Measuring the Dependency Gap: Diagnosing Inter-Column Fidelity in Tabular Generative Models

author.name: Jie Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that popular fidelity metrics for synthetic tabular data are largely blind to inter-column dependency, since a baseline that models every column independently is judged indistinguishable from real data by a logistic-regression classifier two-sample test. The paper proposes a diagnostic that decomposes a stronger gradient-boosted two-sample test into marginal and dependency components.

entry.title: Pixels for Programs? A Cross-Provider Case Study of Input-Token Accounting for Source Code as Text and Images

author.name: Ronak Bhalgami

entry.summary: A reproducible measurement study of how commercial APIs from three major providers count input tokens when source code is submitted as text versus as a compact rendered image, across five languages, nine file lengths and fifteen model aliases. It finds the aliases collapse into roughly five distinct billing signatures, so the aliases are not independent accounting entities.

entry.title: Khondo: A Multimodal Benchmark for Document Packet Splitting of Bangla Forms

author.name: Abu Tyeb Azad, Fahim Ahmed, Ishita Sur Apan, Ezharuddin Jubaer, Sumaiya Karim Katha, Armun Alam, Amin Ahsan Ali, Aman Chadha, Md Mofijul Islam, AKM Mahbubur Rahman

entry.summary: Khondo is the first vision-native, bilingual benchmark for splitting concatenated document packets of Bangladeshi government forms into constituent documents, spanning five shuffling schemes and 14 administrative domains. Zero-shot multimodal LLMs are shown to group pages by source document but struggle with precise boundary and ordering decisions.

entry.title: Multiplicity of Stable Attractors in Disordered Neural Models

author.name: Raffaele Marino, Roberto Livi, Antonio Politi

entry.summary: Using large-deviation statistics and a perturbative expansion in disorder amplitude, the authors estimate how many stable fixed points exist in a disordered neural ordinary differential equation model previously used for computation. They find that at moderate coupling the symmetric gradient case and the asymmetric case, which can in principle host limit cycles and chaos, behave qualitatively alike.

entry.title: IFCLoRA: Topology-Aware Rank Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

author.name: Wei Zhang, Xinwu Liu, Yihang Cheng

entry.summary: IFCLoRA allocates a fixed LoRA rank budget across transformer modules before fine-tuning begins, building a sparse task-conditioned interaction graph from a small calibration set on the frozen model. Combining a global information-flow topology prior with local gradient sensitivity avoids the memory and compute overhead of adaptive-rank methods that track gradient statistics during training.

entry.title: MineValiCoder: Reliable Code Generation with Test Case Quality Mining and Bipartite Graph-Based Mutual Validation

author.name: Zhen Zhao, Qihang Yang, Feifei Dai, Xiangfang Li, Bo Li

entry.summary: MineValiCoder is a closed-loop test-driven code generation framework that mines test-case quality and uses bipartite-graph mutual validation between candidate programs and candidate tests, so faulty tests do not mislead optimization. It targets settings where only natural-language requirements are available and no human tests exist.

entry.title: FMOPF: Latent Flow Matching with Constraint-Aware Interaction Priors for AC Optimal Power Flow

author.name: Zhilin Huang

entry.summary: FMOPF uses latent flow matching with constraint-aware interaction priors to sample from the distribution of near-optimal AC optimal power flow solutions rather than predicting one dispatch point. This gives grid operators a way to reason about feasible-solution diversity for risk and sensitivity analysis under high renewable penetration.

entry.title: Domain-Prior-Regularized Graph Modeling for Anomaly Detection in Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: Youngseok Hwang, Joonsung Kwon, Geonwoo Lee, Hyunwoo Park

entry.summary: DPR-GM improves anomaly detection in small cyber-physical systems by using an LLM to extract directed physical couplings between sensors from design documentation, then regularizing the learned graph toward those priors. This reduces spurious correlations and unstable topologies when labeled anomalies and normal data are scarce.

entry.title: Short-Term Pain for Long-Term Gain: Adaptive Experiment with Post-Commitment Reward Shift

author.name: Puping Jiang, Wei Tang

entry.summary: This paper studies adaptive experimentation where rewards shift after the decision-maker commits to a single option, and proposes an algorithm that reserves part of the experimentation budget to identify the best post-shift arm while minimizing regret in the remainder. It formalizes the tension between short-term performance and long-term commitment value.

entry.title: Sparse Gaussian-Mixture-Model Q-Functions via Hadamard Overparametrization for Online Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Minh Vu, Konstantinos Slavakis

entry.summary: The paper builds an online off-policy policy iteration method using sparse Gaussian-mixture Q-functions, where Hadamard overparametrization enables smooth-regularized sparsification compatible with Riemannian optimization over the parameter manifold, and experience replay handles distribution mismatch. Sparsity lets the method prune a large initial component pool into an interpretable model.

entry.title: Variational-Ising-Attention (VIA):TailoredAttentionMattersfor Science

author.name: Rui Wang

entry.summary: Variational-Ising-Attention replaces softmax's independence assumption with an Ising-style interacting model, deriving attention weights from learnable pairwise couplings via mean-field variational inference. The argument is that scientific tasks with short contexts benefit from collective rather than item-independent attention.

entry.title: Soft-Constrained Optimization of Latent Space in Variational Autoencoders

author.name: Ye Shi

entry.summary: MS-GPT reframes de novo molecular structure elucidation from tandem mass spectra as querying a molecule-language model with the full spectrum-induced fingerprint posterior rather than a single thresholded fingerprint. This directly targets the train-inference mismatch that hampers fingerprint-then-decode pipelines.

entry.title: A Coulomb Particle Model for Learning Kernel Attention in Transformers

author.name: Masoud Badiei Khuzani, Sharath Honnaiah, Atiq Islam, Alex Cozzi, Abraham Bagherjeiran

entry.summary: Learns the distribution of random features for kernel attention by evolving particles under a Hamiltonian that combines kernel-target alignment with a Coulomb repulsion term, yielding a mean-field McKean-Vlasov description. It is instantiated in linearized transformer attention by first learning the kernel then freezing it.

entry.title: DECAF: De-Clustering for Adaptive Representational Unlearning

author.name: Anjie Le, Can Peng, Hongcheng Guo, J. Alison Noble

entry.summary: Argues that many machine unlearning methods leave residual feature-space cluster structure recoverable by a simple unsupervised clustering attack, and proposes a post-hoc method combining input noise, confidence suppression, and entropy-based output diversification to destroy that structure. It operates only on the forget set for on-demand removal.

entry.title: Joint Flow Matching for Generator-Consistent Classification

author.name: Hayden McAlister, Lech Szymanski

entry.summary: Joint Flow Matching assigns opposite temporal endpoint roles to different variables so that a single continuous normalizing flow yields consistent forward and reverse conditionals of the same joint distribution. This supports a unified discriminative-generative model useful for interpretability.

entry.title: Low-Rank Dependence Decomposition via Accelerated Symmetric Non-negative Matrix Factorization

author.name: Lavinia Ghita, Dhruv Desai, Jake Goldberg, Roman Yokunda Enzmann

entry.summary: A large-scale GPU study of over thirty configurations across seven algorithm families for symmetric non-negative matrix factorization on correlation and tail-dependence matrices, using a trace-identity reformulation that eliminates dense n-by-n intermediates. This pushes feasible problem sizes to a hundred thousand on one GPU and a million with multi-node distribution.

entry.title: DocHRL: A Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Framework for Cost-Optimised Document Classification

author.name: Mohammed Yousif, Prabhjot Singh, Arjun Pankajakshan, Madhu Reddiboina

entry.summary: DocHRL uses two-level hierarchical reinforcement learning to route each document to the cheapest adequate classification path, choosing among vision models, LLMs, OCR, and human review. It replaces one-size-fits-all pipelines with per-document cost-aware decisions.

entry.title: FedSLIM: Privacy-Preserving Federated MDL-Based Descriptive Pattern Mining Across Data Silos

author.name: Samar Samir Khalil, Noha S. Tawfik, Marco Spruit

entry.summary: FedSLIM brings minimum-description-length pattern mining into the federated setting, letting parties jointly learn compact descriptive pattern models without pooling raw transaction data. It offers two variants trading off privacy, communication, and optimization fidelity, plus an evaluation setup for federated MDL mining.

entry.title: Approximate reservoir computing with a semiconductor laser for reducing energy consumption

author.name: Tatsuki Ito, Kazutaka Kanno, Satoshi Kawakami, Atsushi Uchida

entry.summary: This study quantizes node states and output weights in a semiconductor-laser reservoir computer to measure the tradeoff between bit precision, sampling frequency, energy use, and chaotic time-series prediction accuracy. It shows approximate computing can preserve accuracy while cutting energy.

entry.title: BHARATI: Morphology-Aware Tokenizers for Classical Indian Languages with Subword Fertility Analysis

author.name: Poornima Kumaresan, Pavithra Muruganantham, Lakshmi Rajendran, Santhosh Sivasubramani

entry.summary: BHARATI presents morphology-aware SentencePiece BPE tokenizers trained on a balanced multilingual corpus covering English and six Indian languages including Sanskrit and Tamil, with attention to sandhi and agglutination. The paper reports subword fertility analysis across three successive tokenizer versions.

entry.title: BERT-based Models vs. Large Language Models for Low-Resource Named Entity Recognition: A Comparative Study on Marathi

author.name: Hariom Ingle, Ronit Ghode, Ishwari Gondkar, Jidnyasa Harad, Raviraj Joshi

entry.summary: This comparative study fine-tunes MahaBERT-v2 on Marathi NER data and benchmarks it against general-purpose LLMs including Gemini, Llama-3.3-70B, and Gemma models. It probes whether large general models can replace small language-specific encoders in low-resource NER.

entry.title: Investigating the Visual Cues of CNNs for Vascular Segmentation: A Case Study in Microscopy and Fundus Imaging

author.name: Weslley dos Santos Silva, Cesar Henrique Comin

entry.summary: The authors probe what visual cues CNNs actually use for blood vessel segmentation in fluorescence microscopy and retinal fundus images, isolating texture and intensity via pixel shuffling and testing shape reliance via sparse contours and centerlines. They quantify how much spatial context the models need.

entry.title: PatiGonit22K: A Comprehensive Dataset for Solving Complex Bengali MWPs

author.name: Swastika Kundu, Azizul Hakim Fayaz, Tashreef Muhammad

entry.summary: Releases an expanded Bengali math word problem dataset of about 22,400 annotated and culturally adapted problems spanning single- and multi-operation equations. Provides a balanced difficulty benchmark for quantitative reasoning in a low-resource language.

entry.title: LLM-Based vs. Lexicon-Based Sentiment Signals for Tail-Risk Detection in Meme Stocks

author.name: Paul Kilian, Markus Kleffmann

entry.summary: Compares VADER lexicon sentiment against multidimensional LLM sentiment extraction, capturing polarity, bullishness, sarcasm likelihood, and topical relevance, on Reddit meme-stock discussion for detecting extreme positive return events. Evaluates the resulting signals against market returns with a focus on the upper tail.

entry.title: Imprompt: A Language Framework for Prompt Programming

author.name: Chentian Wu, Shengyuan Yang, Adithya Murali

entry.summary: Imprompt proposes a language framework for prompt programming in which prompt programs contain only task descriptions and are fully decoupled from execution details. Argues existing frameworks conflate specification with control flow and offers a cleaner foundational design.

entry.title: Open Your Model's Eyes: Video and Context-Aware Multimodal Backchannel Prediction

author.name: Min-Jae Kim, Jun-Yeong Moon, Mujeen Sung, Gyeong-Moon Park

entry.summary: CAMA-BC predicts conversational backchannels using video alongside audio and text, with a two-stage multimodal alignment that first learns conversational context from unlabeled dialogue video and then fine-tunes for backchannel timing. Addresses the omission of facial and gestural cues in current systems.

entry.title: FogDrive: A Multi-Modal Synthetic Driving Dataset for Perception under Graded Fog

author.name: Vansh Panwar

entry.summary: FogDrive is a CARLA-generated multi-modal autonomous driving dataset with 660 scenes and roughly 133k annotated frames across calibrated fog levels, day and night, with paired clean and foggy versions. Designed to benchmark defog-then-detect pipelines and sensor fusion robustness under controlled degradation.

entry.title: Towards Dual-Brain Minimal Sufficient Representation for Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Yihao Wu, Chenyi Xu, Liqi Yan, Chenhuan Cai, Geyong Min, Bin Lin, Fangli Guan, Jianhui Zhang, Pan Li

entry.summary: BrainNav applies a minimal-sufficiency principle to vision-and-language navigation in continuous environments, using instruction-aware selective perception and a compact cross-modal bottleneck to strip task-irrelevant detail. Claims better generalization to unseen scenes at lower compute.

entry.title: RRTrack: Robust and Recoverable Object 6D Pose Tracking for Dynamic Scenes

author.name: Junyue Li, Ye Zheng, Yifan Chen, Zhe Sun, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: RRTrack couples memory-based video object segmentation in 2D with 6D pose refinement in a closed loop, verifying geometric consistency before memory updates so tracking survives fast motion and full target disappearance and reappearance. Trades per-frame estimator cost for efficient recoverable tracking.

entry.title: Embeddings based Anomaly Detection for Cleaning Global Crop Type Reference Datasets

author.name: Syed Roshaan Ali Shah, Kristof Van Tricht, Christina Butsko, Jeroen Degerickx, Zoltan Szantoi

entry.summary: Tests whether geospatial foundation model embeddings can clean noisy global crop-type reference datasets, proposing a locality-aware embedding-based anomaly detection framework for label noise in operational systems like WorldCereal. Motivated by the inadequacy of global rules given regional phenology variation.

entry.title: What Can I Edit? Open-Ended Strategy Discovery and the Emotion Editability Landscape

author.name: Qing Li, Zeyu Dong, Yin Cui, Chuan Yan, Xiaojiang Peng

entry.summary: EmoScope reframes emotional image editing from choosing how to edit to discovering what a given image can afford for a target emotion, using multi-agent affordance reasoning over an image-specific editable space. Argues predefined factor taxonomies and template libraries miss context-grounded strategies.

entry.title: DuoAD: Leveraging [CLS] Dual Characteristics for Training-Free Few-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jyun-Ze Tang, Po-Han Huang, Ming-Ching Chang, Chih-Fan Hsu, Jeng-Lin Li

entry.summary: DuoAD exploits two properties of the vision transformer class token for training-free few-shot anomaly detection: its embedding gives anomaly-invariant global semantics while its attention maps implicitly highlight abnormal regions. Uses these to automate augmentation selection and attention-guided localization without manual tuning.

entry.title: Development of Vision-Language Model-based GNSS Spoofing Detection for Autonomous Vehicle Navigation

author.name: Mohammed Aldeen, Muhammad Sami Irfan, Sagar Dasgupta, Long Cheng, Mizanur Rahman, Mashrur Chowdhury

entry.summary: Builds a vision-language model framework to detect GNSS spoofing on autonomous vehicles by cross-checking front-camera visual cues and in-vehicle sensor readings against GNSS-derived maneuvers, using a three-stage fine-tuning process. Evaluates across three attack scenarios.

entry.title: TreeAdapter: Hierarchical Taxonomy-Guided Adapter Composition for Fine-Grained Species Image Generation

author.name: Yuze Sun, Zhongjie Duan, Yingda Chen

entry.summary: TreeAdapter attaches lightweight adapters to nodes of a biological taxonomy so text-to-image models can share visual features among related species while still capturing leaf-level fine detail. It addresses long-tailed failure when generating rare species.

entry.title: Panda: Unsupervised Pelvic Anomaly Detection for Real-Time MR Imaging

author.name: Anika Knupfer, Maximilian Lindholz, Johanna Paula M\"uller, Jordina Aviles Verdera, Smiti Tripathy, Susanne Schulz-Heise, Jana Hutter

entry.summary: Panda adapts a Dinomaly-style unsupervised anomaly detection framework with a frozen DINOv3 encoder to real-time pelvic MRI, learning normative representations from healthy scans to flag deviations without labels. It targets an underserved clinical area where adverse events are too rare and heterogeneous to annotate.

entry.title: A Reference-Free Framework for Evaluating Single-Frame ISP Pipelines

author.name: Yujin Cho, Sira Ferradans, Jean-Michel Morel, Gabriele Facciolo, Thomas Eboli

entry.summary: Presents a reference-free evaluation framework for camera image signal processing pipelines that measures low-level artifacts from denoising, demosaicing, tone mapping and compression without needing aligned ground-truth pairs. It fills a gap between semantic blind IQA metrics and alignment-dependent full-reference metrics.

entry.title: Not Forgotten: Implementation and Evaluation of a Personalized Episodic Memory for the Humanoid Robot Head Kim

author.name: Steve Aschenbrenner, Marcel Heisler, Thomas Sievers, Christian Becker-Asano

entry.summary: Implements a lightweight episodic memory for an LLM-driven social robot head, combining vector retrieval with a memory-strength score to inject relevant past interactions into the prompt across sessions. Evaluated in a within-subjects online video study with 43 participants.

entry.title: Distributed Coordination for Resilient Multi-UAV Remote Sensing: A Photovoltaic Inspection Case Study

author.name: Guillermo GP-Lenza, Miguel Fernandez-Cortizas, Martin Molina, Pascual Campoy

entry.summary: SwarmLink adds peer-to-peer coordination to existing aerial autonomy stacks without modifying them, so multi-UAV photovoltaic inspection missions can redistribute targets and recover from platform failures without a centralized ground station. Removes a single point of failure in inspection campaigns.

entry.title: Observer-Assisted Relative-Velocity Compensation with LPV-$H_\infty$ Robust Correction for 3D Trajectory Tracking of Underactuated Non-Minimum-Phase AUVs under Ocean Currents

author.name: Mohammad Sabouri

entry.summary: Develops an observer-assisted LPV H-infinity control architecture for 3D trajectory tracking of underactuated non-minimum-phase autonomous underwater vehicles under unknown ocean currents, with LMI-certified synthesis and stability proofs. Provides bounded-error guarantees via singular perturbation analysis.

entry.title: A Cyclic Adaptation-Generalization Framework with Uncertainty-Guided Self-Paced Learning for Long-Term Brain-Machine Interfaces

author.name: Jiyu Wei, Di Hong, Zhanjie Zhang, Dazhong Rong, Qinming He, Yueming Wang

entry.summary: Proposes UnSPC, a framework that combines domain adaptation and domain generalization with uncertainty-guided self-paced learning to counter neural drift in invasive brain-machine interfaces. The goal is to keep neural decoders accurate over months without frequent recalibration.

entry.title: Somebody out there wants you to fetch coffee

author.name: Daniel_Heavens

entry.summary: Argues that the classic shutdown problem desiderata are inadequate because an indifferent agent is vulnerable to trade with external agents who have preferences over its shutdown. This suggests indifference-based solutions are fragile and a stronger criterion is needed for corrigibility.

entry.title: Can we teach a model to encode a semantic feature on a chosen manifold in just three channels?

author.name: Phu Hoang

entry.summary: A safety-puzzle submission that trains a small MLP so a semantic feature about countries is encoded along a chosen nonlinear manifold within three reserved channels, probing whether representation geometry can be deliberately controlled. Includes code and interactive write-up.

entry.title: Discrepancy-Rounded Fair Bandits with Static and Time-Varying Exposure Floors

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Joyanta Jyoti Mondal, Anuj Sharma

entry.summary: This work casts stochastic bandits with hard minimum-exposure floors as a rounding and discrepancy problem, and gives a blockwise algorithm that deterministically satisfies time-varying per-block floors while achieving regret bounds scaling with the discretionary budget rather than the horizon. It matters for recommendation and regulated allocation settings requiring guaranteed provider exposure.

entry.title: Variance-Preserving Orthogonal Selection (VPOS): Greedy Feature Selection via Orthogonal Deflation in PCA Loading Space

author.name: Baran Koseoglu, Berrin Yanikoglu

entry.summary: VPOS greedily selects features in weighted PCA loading space, deflating the chosen direction's variance after each pick so subsequent selections cover orthogonal parts of the covariance structure, with a connection to submodular maximization and a reproducible rule for its single hyperparameter. It reports best reconstruction error on eight benchmarks while running far faster than graph-based selectors.

entry.title: SPRKD: Effective Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks via Saddle Region Approximation

author.name: Aditya Dewan, Arjun Yogeswaran, Benjamin Fedoruk

entry.summary: SPRKD reframes knowledge distillation away from logit mimicry, instead using the teacher to identify saddle regions with strong further-descent potential and guide the student's optimization curvature. The motivation is that standard distillation often acts as mere regularization rather than substantive knowledge transfer for small students.

entry.title: DP-IVON-Gradsq: Differentially Private Squared-Gradient Improved Variational Online Newton

author.name: Nour Jamoussi, Ikram Dridi, Giuseppe Serra, Marios Kountouris

entry.summary: Introduces a differentially private variant of the Improved Variational Online Newton optimizer that builds its curvature estimate from privatized gradients using a noise-corrected squared-gradient estimator. This reduces harmful interaction between DP noise and Bayesian posterior-sampling noise.

entry.title: DriveDNA: A Large-Scale Multimodal Naturalistic Driving Dataset and Benchmark for Driving Style Identification

author.name: Yuhang Wang, Lingyao Li, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: DriveDNA is a large naturalistic driving dataset of 4,121 drives from 465 drivers across 115 vehicle models with 975 hours of synchronized telemetry and forward video, designed so that driver-specific style can be separated from vehicle and situation confounds. It comes with a benchmark for personalized driving-style identification.

entry.title: Adaptive Data Admission and Retention for Streaming Federated Learning

author.name: Zhuoyi Zhao, Ben Liang

entry.summary: Studies federated learning over streaming data with limited client memory and time-varying data-acquisition costs, deriving an error bound that accounts for effective sample size, distinct-sample growth, and reuse imbalance. From it, a drift-plus-penalty policy jointly decides which new samples to admit and what to retain.

entry.title: MEGA-CL: A Molecular Foundation Model for Generalizable ADMET Prediction through Graph External Attention and Contrastive Learning

author.name: Tinghui Jin, Kedu Jin, Ying Li, Guanghui Ren, Jingzhi Xue, Shiyu Zhou, Xiaoli Dai, Li-bin Wei, Xijing Chen, Di Zhao, Jinfeng Liu

entry.summary: MEGA-CL is a graph neural network foundation model for predicting absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity properties, combining self-supervised contrastive pretraining with multi-head external attention and enhanced message passing to reduce over-smoothing. It reports gains over state-of-the-art baselines across 13 datasets and 21 tasks.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Causal Inference and Mediation Analyses of Environmental and Psychosocial Determinants of Subjective Cognitive Difficulties in the All of Us Research Program

author.name: Cong Cao, Shuangge Ma

entry.summary: Uses All of Us longitudinal data to link daily weather and air-pollution exposures to attention and subjective cognitive outcomes, applying fixed-effects, lagged, and event-study designs plus ML heterogeneity exploration, with BRFSS replication. Reported associations are small and largely attenuate under stricter designs, cautioning against causal overreach.

entry.title: Agent Team Work Zone: An Automated, Persistent Workspace for Long-Lived Coding Agent Teams

author.name: Shouren Wang

entry.summary: Describes a persistent workspace system for long-lived teams of coding agents that survives terminal closure, preserves working detail against context compaction, and tracks accumulated agentic technical debt. It targets concrete operational failures observed with Claude Code agent teams.

entry.title: Visual Information Extraction from Documents via Classification-Guided Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Huafu Li, Guo Chen, Jia Xia, Lei Wang, Wei Du, Yun Yao, Weijun Peng, Liming Li

entry.summary: Proposes decoupling document-type classification from content extraction in visual information extraction, using the predicted type to drive in-context-learning prompts for a large vision-language model. Aims for robust zero-shot extraction across highly variable layouts without layout-specific training.

entry.title: Test-Time Adaptation via Dual Distillation for Videos Under Severe Distribution Shifts

author.name: Andr\'e Sacilotti, Samuel Felipe dos Santos, Jurandy Almeida

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-distillation test-time adaptation method for video models facing continuous, temporally correlated data under severe distribution shifts. It targets a setting most TTA work avoids because of temporal correlation and extreme domain gaps.

entry.title: Denoising 3D images: robustness of persistent homology measures

author.name: Ebru Dagdelen, Aakash Karlekar, Manav Arora, Matthew Illingsworth, Jonathan Jaquette, Linda J. Cummings, Lou Kondic

entry.summary: Empirically studies how spatially uncorrelated noise and various denoising choices distort persistent homology summaries of 3D porous-media images, comparing bottleneck and Wasserstein distances, persistence statistics and persistence images. Provides guidance on which topological measures survive the denoising pipeline.

entry.title: Benchmarking Fine-tuning and Retrieval Strategies for a Multimodal Language Model on the NRC Reactor Operator Licensing Examination

author.name: Isak Hwang, Yoon Pyo Lee

entry.summary: The study benchmarks eight configurations of an existing 31B open-weight multimodal Gemma 4 model, including supervised fine-tuning on Gemini-distilled chain-of-thought and various retrieval setups, against 14 US Nuclear Regulatory Commission reactor operator fundamentals exams from 2015 to 2021. Performance is judged against the standard 80 percent human passing threshold.

entry.title: Explicit Iteration Complexity of Exact Data-Driven Inverse Optimization for Integer Linear Programs

author.name: Akira Kitaoka

entry.summary: This theory paper supplies the missing lower bound on the geometric constant that governs iteration complexity of exact gradient-based data-driven inverse optimization for integer linear programs. Bounding that constant as a function of problem size makes the previously abstract finite-termination guarantee explicitly size-dependent.

entry.title: From Hybrid Mechanistic--Data-Driven Modeling Toward Neuro-Symbolic AI: What, Why, and How

author.name: Moein E. Samadi, Andreas Schuppert

entry.summary: This position and framework paper recasts hybrid mechanistic plus data-driven models as instances of a neuro-symbolic interface, putting first-principles knowledge on the symbolic side, learned modules on the belief side, and explicitly representing validity domains and epistemic uncertainty of the mechanistic component. It offers shared vocabulary for comparing and verifying hybrid designs across domains.

entry.title: Same Predictions, Different Reasons: The Effect of Quantization on Model Explanations

author.name: Kazi Kamruzzaman Rabbi, Md. Zami Al Zunaed Farabe, M. Sohel Rahman

entry.summary: This study asks whether post-training quantization preserves not just accuracy but the reasons behind predictions, comparing Grad-CAM and complementary attributions across five CNNs at 8-bit and 4-bit precision. It finds that predictions can match while internal attribution patterns diverge, which has implications for auditing compressed models.

entry.title: Does Graph Compression Preserve Signal Propagation?

author.name: Kawshik Banerjee, Khaled Mohammed Saifuddin

entry.summary: The authors ask whether graph coarsening and sparsification preserve signal propagation dynamics, measuring diversity and mixing behavior directly rather than judging compression by downstream accuracy alone. Across five datasets they find a consistent tension in which sparsification retains signal diversity while coarsening behaves differently, giving practitioners guidance on which compression to choose.

entry.title: On the post-hoc Evaluation of PDE Discovery: A Multifaceted Challenge of Scientific Advancement

author.name: Baptiste Mathevon, Farah Cherfaoui, Amaury Habrard, Marc Sebban

entry.summary: A position and analysis paper arguing that evaluating discovered partial differential equations requires jointly weighing predictive accuracy, physical consistency, interpretability, and out-of-distribution generalization, which existing metrics cover only partially and sometimes conflict. It surveys and critiques current post-hoc evaluation practice in PDE discovery.

entry.title: Flash-CNNCap: Capacitance Extraction via Image Mapping

author.name: Hector R. Rodriguez, Jiechen Huang, Wenjian Yu

entry.summary: Flash-CNNCap recasts parasitic capacitance extraction in chip layout as image-to-image regression over spatial contribution maps, cutting the number of network passes needed for a full capacitance matrix from quadratic to linear in conductor count. Outputs are aggregated by masks into a physically consistent Maxwell capacitance matrix.

entry.title: DynaCalKV: Key-Value Cache Compression via Head Grouping and Adaptive Rank Allocation

author.name: Tan T. Nguyen, Quan V. Dang

entry.summary: DynaCalKV compresses the transformer key-value cache with low-rank factorization that treats keys and values differently and groups attention heads dynamically according to structural similarity rather than a fixed partition. This targets the long-context memory bottleneck during LLM inference.

entry.title: A Vocabulary for Multi-Agent Automated Research Systems

author.name: Bardiya Akhbari

entry.summary: Proposes a standardized vocabulary describing multi-agent automated research systems along eight axes covering agent roles, available operations, permissions, communication, information visibility, action selection, initialization, and evaluation. It frames each run as a trajectory drawn from a distribution, making design choices comparable across systems.

entry.title: Variable Importance Identification Through Lazy Training for Binary Classification

author.name: Anand Singh, Luke Pennella, Eshan Kabir, Xiaoxi Shen

entry.summary: Extends variable-importance testing based on lazy training from regression to binary classification, offering an efficient feature-selection algorithm with controlled error rates under weak assumptions. Theory is complemented by empirical validation.

entry.title: IKS-Instruct: A 24,000-Example Multilingual Dataset for Teaching Language Models Indian Knowledge Systems

author.name: Shwetha Singaravelu, Gayathri Muruganantham, Lakshmi Rajendran, Santhosh Sivasubramani

entry.summary: IKS-Instruct is a roughly 24,800-example instruction-tuning dataset teaching models to deliver educational content grounded in Indian Knowledge Systems across seven languages and 41 Vedic pedagogical techniques, aligned to the CBSE school curriculum. It targets a domain absent from English-dominated instruction datasets.

entry.title: Mwando: Leveraging AI to Preserve and Teach shiKomori

author.name: Naira Abdou Mohamed, Haidar Nassur Said Ali, Mohamed Hazra, Naoufal Mohamed Soibira, Roushnaty Ali Yamani

entry.summary: Describes a multi-agent educational assistant for shiKomori and its four dialects, combining a curated knowledge base of phrases, proverbs, dictionaries, and grammar with vector search, a knowledge graph, and web-search fallback. Evaluated on 500 queries with strong results on vocabulary and grammar lookups.

entry.title: DINOv3-MIL: Per-Kidney Multi-Label Tumour and Cyst Detection from Foundation-Model Patch Tokens on KiTS23

author.name: Vishalakshi M, Sahil Sharma, Pramod Kumar P

entry.summary: Compares three aggregators over frozen DINOv3 patch tokens for per-kidney tumour and cyst detection on KiTS23: a CLS linear probe, gated attention multiple-instance learning, and a prototype head. Attention MIL performs best and concentrates attention within annotated lesions well above chance.

entry.title: CrossSpine: Multi-scale Cross-sequence Attention with Anatomical Priors for Automated Pfirrmann Grading

author.name: Hai Son Nguyen, Duong Ngoc Vu, Trong-Nghia Nguyen, Bien Tran Van, Van-Dem Pham, Trang Mai Xuan, Huan Vu, Thien Van Luong

entry.summary: CrossSpine fuses features from multiple MRI sequences at several spatial scales via cross-sequence attention for automated Pfirrmann grading of lumbar disc degeneration, and adds disc-level anatomical priors so the model learns level-specific patterns. Contributes a curated grading dataset as well.

entry.title: IJCB-AFMFR 2026: Competition on Adapting Foundation Models for Face Recognition Using Synthetic Training Data

author.name: Tahar Chettaoui, Guray Ozgur, Eduarda Caldeira, Arturas Nakvosas, Hatef Otroshi Shahreza, S\'ebastien Marcel, Rishabh Shukla, Aditya Takkar, Rushil Khullar, Lalak Yadav, Gourav Gupta, Anant Gupta, Shiqi Yu, Vitomir Struc, Naser Damer, Fadi Boutros

entry.summary: Summarizes an IJCB 2026 competition on adapting the CLIP ViT-L/14 foundation model for face recognition using only synthetic identity training data, across full-data and limited-data tracks. Eight submissions from four teams were ranked on standard verification and identification benchmarks.

entry.title: Surgical Re-enactment for Operating Room Workflow Datasets

author.name: Jana Nina Friedrich, Andrea Karin Maria Ross, Angelo Henriques, Mario Peter Martin Weisser, Ling Zhang, Mohammad Ali Nasseri

entry.summary: Describes a methodology for re-enacting full surgical procedures in a reconstructed operating room to generate repeatable, annotatable multi-view workflow datasets. It circumvents ethics, sterility and camera-placement barriers that block data collection in real ORs.

entry.title: Co-planning of Flight Corridors and Communication Infrastructure for Urban Drone Logistics Networks

author.name: Yingjie He, Yikang Wang, Zhenyu Gao

entry.summary: Jointly optimizes base station placement and UAV flight corridor design for urban drone logistics using a channel-reciprocity-guided combinatorial multi-armed bandit, rather than planning connectivity and routes separately. Aims to cut both infrastructure cost and flight detours under connectivity constraints.

entry.title: Multi-Domain Physics-Based MDO of Multirotor UAVs: A Deterministic Framework for Discrete COTS Sizing

author.name: Akshay Gupta Burela, P. B. Sujit

entry.summary: AeroEval is a multidisciplinary design optimization engine for multirotor UAVs that resolves structural, electrochemical, aerodynamic and kinematic couplings simultaneously and maps continuous optima to purchasable off-the-shelf components. It uses a calibrate-then-test protocol on held-out designs to avoid circular validation.

entry.title: Trajectory-Aware Retrieval Agents for Temporal Decision- Making

author.name: Jing Wang, Jie Shen, Xing Niu

entry.summary: TLM is a closed-loop retrieval agent for decisions over long, chronologically structured documents, addressing how standard RAG shatters temporal ordering into isolated snippets. It fits a latent growth curve model over retrieved chunk embeddings to detect trends, turning points and evidence gaps, and refines the evidence set using SHAP-guided feedback.

entry.title: Dynamic Capability Scoping for Enterprise AI Agents: A Synthetic Dataset and Three-Source Permission Architecture

author.name: Halil Burak Noyan

entry.summary: Argues enterprise AI agents should receive dynamically scoped least-privilege credentials rather than static role-wide tool access, on the principle that a credential absent from context cannot be misused regardless of the agent reasoning. It sketches a three-source permission architecture with role ceilings, a task-context classifier, and policy-derived prohibitions, plus a synthetic dataset.

entry.title: MotifRole-Diff: Risk-Optimal Role-Aware Corruption for Masked Molecular Graph Diffusion

author.name: Tasfia Nuzhat Ornee, Elias Hossain, Ivan Garibay, Niloofar Yousef

entry.summary: MotifRole-Diff replaces the uniform masking schedule in discrete diffusion for molecular graphs with role-aware corruption rates set by empirically measured denoising difficulty and each token role influence on the decoded molecule. It keeps the architecture, clean sequence space and lossless representation unchanged.

entry.title: Multi-Horizon Consistency as Geometry: When Latent Dynamics Contract, and When They Do Not

author.name: Kavya Bhand, Aadi Joshi

entry.summary: Treats the weight on multi-step latent consistency in video predictors and world models as a diagnostic knob and measures its effect on transition geometry, finding that strong weighting contracts latent dynamics and halves long-horizon error on Moving-MNIST. The same loss does not produce contraction on action-conditioned control environments or real video, even when error improves.

entry.title: Enhancing SLMs for Sustainable Code Optimization in Radio-Astronomy

author.name: Elisa Chiarotto, Jingbo Li, P. Chris Broekema, Rob V. van Nieuwpoort

entry.summary: Investigates whether small language models can help optimize the large radio-astronomy codebase facing a 40-fold compute increase after a telescope upgrade, with sustainability as an explicit objective. The approach assists developers in evaluating and accelerating existing software and adopting hardware accelerators.

entry.title: Co-design of LLM-based preference agents: participation may drive overtrust

author.name: Michael J. Fell

entry.summary: A qualitative study where twelve participants co-designed personal LLM preference agents for household energy decisions, then validated them. Participants engaged willingly and largely believed their agents represented them well, yet independent validation showed mixed human-agent alignment, suggesting participation can create overtrust rather than fix misrepresentation.

entry.title: From Perturbation Correction to Geometry-Aware Sampling: Sharpness-Guided Equilibrium Sampling for Balanced Flat Minima in Long-Tailed Learning

author.name: Jiaxin Deng, Junbiao Pang

entry.summary: Sharpness-Guided Equilibrium Sampling treats the mini-batch sampling distribution itself as a control variable for optimization geometry in long-tailed learning, upweighting rarely sampled classes while suppressing classes with large sharpness-aware-minimization losses. This intervenes before biased batches are drawn, unlike loss or perturbation reweighting methods.

entry.title: Practical Graph Optimisation and AI-Driven Models for Active Directory Security Hardening

author.name: Huy Q. Ngo

entry.summary: This work extends attack-graph hardening for Microsoft Active Directory to more realistic settings, addressing graph dynamism, active defenses beyond simply revoking vulnerable edges, and uncertain or partially feasible remediations. It combines graph optimization with learned models to produce practical hardening recommendations.

entry.title: Towards Trustworthy and Cost-Efficient Data Integration: From Na\"ive RAG to Agentic RAG

author.name: Chuangtao Ma, Arijit Khan

entry.summary: A vision and survey paper tracing data integration from naive retrieval-augmented generation through GraphRAG and knowledge-graph RAG toward agentic RAG, with trustworthiness defined as evidence-grounded, verifiable, hallucination-resistant reasoning. It outlines cost and accuracy challenges for enterprise deployment.

entry.title: Unboxing Diffusion Models for the Arts: Interactive Model Bending and Practice-Based Explainability

author.name: Ahmed M. Abuzuraiq, Philippe Pasquier

entry.summary: This work reframes explainability for artists as material engagement, providing interactive model bending and inspection controls for text-to-image diffusion models integrated into a ComfyUI node workflow with layer selection and intervention. It argues large models can act as creative materials when internal structure is visible and manipulable.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Privacy Game in Federated Learning: A Unified Mean-Field View

author.name: Kun Zhao, Xu Chen

entry.summary: Federated learning privacy choices are modeled as a mean-field game in which each client picks its own privacy budget and interacts with the population only through a single aggregate statistic, making equilibrium computation tractable as client count grows. This bridges noise-injection mechanisms and game-theoretic accounts of client incentives.

entry.title: XMix: Combating Extremely Noisy Labels via Local Smoothness in Self-Supervised Feature Space

author.name: Chengqi Li, Yangdi Lu, Zhihao Shi, Wenbo He, Chamseddine Talhi, Nadjia Kara

entry.summary: XMix uses local smoothness in a self-supervised feature space, rather than potentially corrupted labels, to drive every stage of clean-sample selection for learning under extremely noisy annotations. It aims to avoid the tuning and prior noise-rate knowledge that current selection methods require.

entry.title: ADVERSARIAL: And-Inverter Graph-Assisted Hardware Trojan Detection At Scale

author.name: Yaroslav Popryho, Debjit Pal, Inna Partin-Vaisband

entry.summary: Detects hardware trojans in billion-gate netlists by converting flattened designs into and-inverter graphs and embedding each edge triple with knowledge-graph embedding techniques, giving constant-size node representations with multi-hop context and linear scaling. Scalability is the central claim.

entry.title: MIME: Multimodal Interactive Motion Encoder

author.name: Addison Zucek, Prerit Gupta, Kamila Kuatova, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: MIME is a text-motion encoder built specifically for two-person interactive motion, using stream-based co-attention with explicit interaction features and curriculum contrastive training. It outperforms early and late fusion baselines on Inter-X retrieval across gallery sizes.

entry.title: Frequency-Based Reservoir computing

author.name: Arthur S Powanwe

entry.summary: Proposes a reservoir computing design built from frequency-tuned oscillatory units inspired by brain rhythms, replacing randomly connected reservoirs to make behavior interpretable and hyperparameter tuning more principled. Aims to explain how reservoirs encode dynamics rather than just tuning them empirically.

entry.title: DishSeg24k: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Food Segmentation with Stochastic Expert Decoding

author.name: Yilin Wang, Haochen Shi, Guanyu Chen, Weiqing Min, Jinkai Zheng, Chenggang Yan, Shuqiang Jiang

entry.summary: Releases DishSeg24k, a dish-level food segmentation benchmark with about 24k images, 112k instances, and 278 fine-grained categories in real dining scenes, plus FEAST, a transformer that treats query decoding as a Markov decision process with expert routing. Targets dense overlap, fine-grained similarity, and long-tail distributions.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Object Re-Identification with Prompt-S6 and Semantic-Aware Knowledge Guidance

author.name: Weixiang Zhou, Jiabei Zuo, Yuhao Wang, Cong Wang, Huchuan Lu, Zhixun Su

entry.summary: PRISM performs multi-modal object re-identification using a prompt-conditioned state-space (Mamba-style) backbone for linear-complexity cross-modal interaction, plus semantic knowledge guidance to suppress background interference and align three modalities. Targets the cost and pairwise-fusion limits of prior work.

entry.title: Geometry Meets Semantics: Fractional Gradient Stabilization for Semantic-Driven Bounding Box Optimization in Visual Detection Tasks

author.name: Qi Ming, Haitian Yang, Xudong Zhao, Mingjing Zhao, Liuqian Wang, Nanqing Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a fractional-gradient semantic IoU loss for oriented bounding box regression, injecting semantic similarity into an otherwise purely geometric objective and stabilizing the unstable orientation gradients that cause convergence oscillation. Applies to oriented object detection.

entry.title: XMatchAD: A Cross-Modal Matching Perspective on Reconstruction-based Anomaly Detection

author.name: Mingxiu Cai, Zhe Zhang, Gaochang Wu, Tianyou Chai

entry.summary: XMatchAD recasts reconstruction-based unsupervised anomaly detection as cross-modal matching, treating the input and its reconstruction as two complementary modalities whose correspondence structure reveals anomalies. Targets subtle defects and blurred anomaly boundaries in multi-class settings.

entry.title: Contrastive Parameter Disentanglement for Multi-modal Remote Sensing Image Generation

author.name: Yu Zhang, Wenda Zhao, Haojun Tang, Haipeng Wang

entry.summary: Generates semantically consistent optical, infrared, and SAR remote sensing images from a single text prompt by disentangling shared semantics from modality-specific attributes at the parameter level within an orthogonal subspace. Extends remote sensing generation beyond single-modality synthesis.

entry.title: Effective Receptive Field Ordering Matters for Infrared Small Target Detection

author.name: Guoyi Zhang, Yanjin Du, Zhengyao Zhao, Tongsu Zhang, Guangsheng Xu, Siyang Chen, Xiangpeng Xu, Han Wang, Xiaohu Zhang

entry.summary: Studies the ordering of effective receptive fields during feature refinement as an architectural dimension for infrared small target detection, distinct from receptive field size design, and casts deep feature transformation as progressive residual correction. Derives scheduling principles from scale-frequency correspondence and related properties.

entry.title: MarineEVT: Advancing Event-Centric Marine Video Understanding via Visual Tool Reasoning

author.name: Tuan-An To, Yuk-Kwan Wong, Tuan-Anh Vu, Ziqiang Zheng, Sai-Kit Yeung

entry.summary: MarineEVT introduces an event-centric marine video understanding dataset and a visual tool-reasoning approach for vision-language models, targeting sparse and unpredictable underwater events. It addresses domain expertise requirements and weak temporal localization in video VLMs.

entry.title: DY-LUT: Depth-Aware YCbCr Lookup Tables for Real-Time Underwater Image Enhancement

author.name: Cunhao Zhu, Xiangtao Kong, Dongliang Xu, Zhiheng Zhang, Tianyu Wang, Yue Yao

entry.summary: DY-LUT conditions learnable 4D lookup tables on depth and per-pixel degradation indices in YCbCr space for real-time underwater image enhancement, with lightweight local refinement. It retains LUT efficiency while allowing spatially adaptive, wavelength-aware correction with a 3.56M-parameter network.

entry.title: Direction-adaptive Mamba: Spatial-Frequency Dual-Domain Collaborative Learning for PolSAR Image Classification

author.name: Junfei Shi, Yu Cheng, Haojia Zhang, Wenqiang Hua, Junhuai Li, Maoguo Gong

entry.summary: Proposes DA-Mamba, a state-space backbone for polarimetric SAR classification that adds edge-aligned direction-adaptive scanning and joint spatial-frequency processing. It targets anisotropic scattering patterns that fixed-order Mamba scans handle poorly.

entry.title: Efficient multidisciplinary design via Bayesian optimization

author.name: Nathalie Bartoli, Thierry Lefebvre, R\'emi Lafage, Paul Saves, Youssef Diouane, Joseph Morlier

entry.summary: Describes SEGOMOE, a Bayesian optimization toolkit built on Gaussian process mixtures that handles mixed continuous, discrete, categorical, and hierarchical design variables plus multi-fidelity data and hidden constraints. It is validated on benchmarks and aeronautical multidisciplinary design problems.

entry.title: Filling Before Advancing: Capability-Gap-Driven Post-Training for Scenario-Specialized Remote Sensing MLLMs

author.name: Yuheng Zong, Minghua Wang, Xin Zhao, Zhi-Hui Zhan, Antonio Plaza, Jon Atli Benediktsson

entry.summary: Filling Before Advancing frames adaptation of remote-sensing multimodal LLMs as a capability-gap problem, first closing prerequisite skill gaps before specializing to a target scenario instead of single-stage supervised fine-tuning. It is instantiated for coastal harbor understanding with a new three-layer multi-source dataset.

entry.title: Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support

author.name: Peiyong Wang, Udaya Parampalli, Casey R. Myers

entry.summary: Quantum Spectral Models construct the generator of the data-encoding unitary directly from each input matrix so that spectral values and subspaces are represented explicitly, unlike common coordinate-wise rotation-gate encodings. Three variants based on symmetric, global block, and patch-local block Hamiltonians are analyzed with input-conditioned frequency support.

entry.title: Semalith v1.4: A Calibrated 184M Safety Classifier Achieving State-of-the-Art Prompt-Injection Detection at 44x Fewer Parameters than Llama-Guard-3-8B

author.name: Tejasvi C. Addagada

entry.summary: Semalith v1.4 is a 184M-parameter DeBERTa-based guardrail that classifies prompt injection, general harm, and financial-services regulatory compliance in a single forward pass using a 22-class head with an auxiliary super-category head, trained on a deduplicated 76,000-row corpus mined from 49 public sources. The claim is state-of-the-art prompt-injection detection at 44 times fewer parameters than Llama-Guard-3-8B.

entry.title: Physically Verifiable Evidence and LLM-Based Reporting for Bearing Fault Diagnosis

author.name: Yuntong Chen, Jianyu Liu, Guobin Zhao, Ziang Wang, Chao Chen, Ju Huang, Xitian Tian, Lijiang Huang

entry.summary: DENet outputs physically checkable evidence for bearing fault diagnosis instead of just a class label with a softmax score, and constrains an LLM report generator to that evidence to limit hallucination in maintenance documentation. The framing that predictions must be verifiable against independent physical knowledge before action is the interesting part.

entry.title: Online Policy Evaluation for MDPs with Dynamic UBSR Measures

author.name: Weikai Wang, Erick Delage

entry.summary: The authors develop online, simulator-free algorithms with linear function approximation for evaluating policies under dynamic utility-based shortfall risk measures, prove almost-sure convergence for the base temporal-difference method, and propose accelerated variants. It broadens risk-aware RL beyond restrictive risk classes.

entry.title: Covariance Last-Layer Ensembles: Function-Space Diversity for Efficient Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: H. Martin Gillis, Isaac Xu, Gabriel Spadon, Thomas Trappenberg

entry.summary: Attacks diversity collapse in last-layer ensembles for out-of-distribution detection by enforcing diversity directly in function space through a covariance-based objective, rather than the indirect weight-orthonormality used by orthonormal certificates. The result is cheap single-pass epistemic uncertainty that retains member disagreement.

entry.title: Controllable Diversity in Normalization-Based Implicit Ensembles via Softmax-Temperature Modulation

author.name: Mihai Suteu, Ovidiu Serban

entry.summary: Introduces a normalization-based implicit ensemble in which each member is treated as a task modulated by sigmoid-bounded scalers on a shared backbone, plus a softmax-temperature regularizer that tunes how much members share during training. This lets practitioners trace the accuracy-versus-diversity tradeoff rather than fixing diversity at initialization.

entry.title: Forecasting the Emergence and Evolution of Crash Hotspots: A Unified Deep Learning Framework for Proactive Traffic Safety

author.name: Jingwen Zhu, Keshu Wu, Pei Li, Steven T. Parker, Bin Ran, David A. Noyce

entry.summary: HERALD is a deep learning framework that treats crash hotspots as episodes with a life cycle, jointly detecting emerging hotspots, forecasting next-week locations, and tracking individual hotspots over time. The aim is to let enforcement anticipate rather than trail risk concentrations.

entry.title: EchoBridge: Long-Tail-Aware ECG-Echocardiography Text Alignment for Echocardiography-Derived Cardiac Findings

author.name: Xiaocheng Fang, Jieyi Cai, Guangkun Nie, Haoyu Wang, Jiarui Jin, Yujie Xiao, Bo Liu, Chenyang He, Qinghao Zhao, Gaofeng Cheng, Hongyan Li, Shenda Hong

entry.summary: EchoBridge aligns ECG signals with text from echocardiography reports using shared-plus-private projections and prototype boundary calibration tuned to class frequency, targeting rare cardiac findings. It aims to let cheap ECG recordings predict echo-derived diagnoses.

entry.title: AI-interpreted Optical Scattering for Robust and Focal Depth-Aware Imaging

author.name: Eunji Ko, Patrick Ross, Corey Hart, Wolfgang Losert

entry.summary: Argues optical scattering can be helpful rather than purely harmful in imaging, comparing scattered and unscattered MNIST speckle datasets with an interpretable variational autoencoder latent space. Scattering appears to spread information spatially, improving robustness to pixel dropout and encoding focal-depth cues.

entry.title: GNN-based Multi-Agent Control of Traffic Shockwaves in Sparse Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks

author.name: Prachi Nandi, Madhuri Malakar, Sonakshi Satpathy, Pabitra Mohan Khilar

entry.summary: The paper proposes decentralized multi-agent RL with a graph neural network for connected autonomous vehicles to damp stop-and-go traffic shockwaves without global traffic state information. The design targets early-stage sparse VANET deployments.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Validation-Repair for Healthcare Interoperability: A Multi-Model Study of Schema Compliance in Clinical LLMs

author.name: Jianru Shen

entry.summary: Evaluates whether small open-weight models can emit clinically valid structured outputs (ICD-10, CPT, FHIR) and tests a closed-loop validate-then-repair wrapper across 320 scenarios and three model families. Finds schema noncompliance is a consistent failure mode independent of model family, and that automated repair loops recover much of it.
