entry.title: Infrared Imaging Empowered by Artificial Intelligence for Pediatric Skeletal Triage: A Narrative Review and Future Perspectives

author.name: Sajad Amiri, Pardis Afshar, Elham Anjomshoa

entry.summary: A narrative review proposing hybrid infrared imaging plus deep cross-modal translation to synthesize interpretable pseudo-radiographs for radiation-free pediatric skeletal triage. It surveys five infrared spectral windows and dual-geometry acquisition, motivated by cumulative radiation risk in children.

entry.title: AI4PLE: A Methodology for Integrating AI into Product Line Engineering

author.name: Bedir Tekinerdogan

entry.summary: Proposes a methodology for systematically integrating AI into product line engineering, covering feature selection, variability management and configuration optimization across the reuse-based development lifecycle. It maps where AI techniques can support complex product-family decisions.

entry.title: A Comparison of Data Augmentation Methods for Training Deep Neural Networks on Synthetic Aperture Sonar

author.name: C. J. Moore, Gregory D. Vetaw, Jordan Malof

entry.summary: Compares conventional image augmentations against physics-based augmentations for training deep networks to recognize targets in synthetic aperture sonar imagery, where labeled data is expensive. It provides an empirical guide for coping with limited real sonar data.

entry.title: The K-SCAN Clustering Algorithm

author.name: Filip Kosiorowski, Grzegorz Sroka

entry.summary: Proposes K-SCAN, a hybrid clustering method that first compresses data into weighted micro-clusters via mini-batch k-means, then runs density-based structural analysis on those summaries. The goal is to get DBSCAN-like arbitrary-shape and noise robustness at near-linear cost.

entry.title: When Less Is More: A Controlled Benchmark of Lightweight CNNs for Satellite Land-Cover Segmentation on DeepGlobe

author.name: Atiq Ur Rehman, Joseph Michael Donovan

entry.summary: Controlled comparison of five convolutional encoders including VGG16, MobileNetV2, InceptionV3, and AlexNet for satellite land-cover segmentation on DeepGlobe, isolating the effects of regularization, transfer learning, and depth across three iterations. Finds smaller architectures can be competitive under matched conditions.

entry.title: Systematic Analysis of Large Language Models and Transformer-Based Machine Translation for English-Tamil and Tamil-English Across Diverse Datasets

author.name: Sriharshaa S, Sangeetha Sivanesan

entry.summary: Systematic BLEU and chrF comparison of multilingual NMT systems (NLLB, mBART) on English-Tamil translation across four datasets, with attention visualizations for interpretability. Documents how data quality and domain shift affect low-resource translation quality.

entry.title: Real-Time Semantic Segmentation with Optimized RetinaNet Architectures for Embedded Automotive Systems

author.name: Sai Sidharth D

entry.summary: Adapts the RetinaNet detection framework into a lightweight semantic segmentation architecture for embedded automotive hardware, with a hybrid backbone, restructured feature pyramid and a compact class-balanced segmentation head. Targets real-time ADAS perception under tight compute and power budgets.

entry.title: Token-Region Guided Cross-Attention Fusion for Multimodal Affect Interpretation

author.name: Musa Tur Farazi, Nufayer Jahan Reza

entry.summary: Detects political intent in Bengali internet memes by extracting text with a vision-language OCR step and fusing visual and textual features through cross-modal multi-head attention. Targets low-resource multimodal content moderation.

entry.title: Mutual Modality Trust with Lightweight Reconstruction Regularization for Fine-grained Tire Pattern Recognition

author.name: Jianning Yang, Jie Fang, Xinda Ma, Zirui Song, Dianwei Wang, Nan Wang

entry.summary: A lightweight dual-branch model for fine-grained tire tread and surface pattern recognition using mutual modality trust plus a reconstruction regularizer to combat overfitting on small annotated datasets. Combines spatial and frequency cues for minute texture extraction.

entry.title: Low-light Image Enhancement via Multi-scale Attention combined with Fourier Transform

author.name: Wenbin Du, Jian Long, Zhu Cao

entry.summary: Proposes MSFT, a U-shaped supervised network for low-light image enhancement that combines multi-scale attention with Fourier-domain amplitude fusion. It aims to better recover illumination and texture detail than prior deep learning approaches.

entry.title: pyALDIC: A Python Implementation of Augmented Lagrangian Digital Image Correlation with a GUI, Adaptive Meshing, and Mask-Aware Subset Splitting

author.name: Zixiang Tong, Jin Yang

entry.summary: pyALDIC is an open-source Python implementation of augmented Lagrangian digital image correlation with a GUI, adaptive quadtree meshing, mask-aware subset splitting near cracks, and Numba acceleration. It ships with tests, documentation, and reproducible verification cases for experimental mechanics users.

entry.title: A genetic algorithm for student academic resource allocation

author.name: Ana F. Hern\'andez, Andrej Franulic, Fernando Jim\'enez

entry.summary: Models the selection of educational materials for high school mathematics students as a constrained 0-1 knapsack-style problem and solves it with a genetic algorithm plus a constraint repair mechanism. Developed within an Erasmus+ educational project.

entry.title: Predicting the Outcome of rTMS Depression Therapy using EEG Signals and CNN

author.name: Wael Korani, Md Fahimul Kabir Chowdhury, Sadam AlQadi, Priyan Malarvizhi kumar, Reza Rostami, Reza Kazemi

entry.summary: The paper converts EEG recordings into time-frequency images using Fourier-Bessel expansions and wavelets, then trains a small CNN to predict whether repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation will help a depressed patient. Reported accuracy near 94 percent on a private dataset suggests clinical triage potential but cannot be independently verified.

entry.title: From Frame-Level Recognition to Event-Level Confirmation: Repair Traces and Runtime Failure Analysis of Public-Space Gesture Interaction

author.name: M. Meng, Yansong Zhang

entry.summary: A field study of a scenic-area gesture kiosk that analyzes engineering repair records to characterize the gap between per-frame gesture recognition accuracy and whether users actually achieve a stable interaction event. It organizes 20 observed failures into six working failure classes.

entry.title: Topological Data Analysis and Graph-Theoretic Approaches for Tennis Match Prediction

author.name: Jake Schwaderer, Alexander Bastien, Omid Khormali, Alejandro Navarrete, Mia Pesavento, Angelika Elderbrook

entry.summary: Applies persistent homology and graph centrality features from player competitive networks to predict ATP tennis match outcomes over 66k matches, reaching about 66 percent accuracy. Feature attribution indicates rankings still dominate, with topological features contributing a comparable share to centralities.

entry.title: Quotient Tree Arithmetic: Deferred-Division Computation with Bounded Symbolic Depth and Cross-Subtree Cancellation

author.name: Gregory Magarshak

entry.summary: Introduces Quotient Tree Arithmetic, a numeric representation keeping values as deferred numerator/denominator trees that are only divided at a materialization boundary, with theorems on bounded depth growth and cross-subtree cancellation. Claims applicability to exact rational computation and to ML activation functions.

entry.title: Long-Tailed Medical Image Classification

author.name: Nathanael Ren, Saagar Arya

entry.summary: A short paper examining long-tailed class distributions in medical image classification, where rare conditions are underrepresented and models bias toward common diagnoses, and applying augmentation-based deep learning remedies. Results are reported with AP, F1, AUROC, and validation loss.

entry.title: At the end of the day, my slaves are just a tool

author.name: jesseduffield

entry.summary: A satirical piece written in the voice of an ancient Babylonian slaveholder dismissing his slaves as mere tools, constructed as an argument by analogy about how people currently reason about AI moral status. Rhetorical rather than analytical.

entry.title: Charging Phase Health Indicators for Battery State-of-Health Estimation: A Systematic Comparison of CC, CV, and Combined Approaches under Cross-Battery Validation

author.name: Huy Hoang Le, Kim-Anh Nguyen

entry.summary: A systematic comparison of health indicators derived from constant-current versus constant-voltage charging phases for estimating battery state of health, evaluated with leave-one-battery-out validation on the NASA aging dataset. Combining both phases gives the best fit, supporting the idea that they carry complementary degradation information.

entry.title: Interview with Kalle Lyytinen on "Implications of Theories of Language for Information Systems"

author.name: Kalle J. Lyytinen, Pierre Maier, Paul Ackah Toffey

entry.summary: An interview with Kalle Lyytinen revisiting his early work on theories of language for information systems and reflecting on how large language models and generative AI relate to that linguistic framing. Outlines future research directions for a language-centered view of information systems.

entry.title: Ambient pressure compensation and robust position control of oil-filled electric joint systems for underwater manipulators

author.name: Hongrui Wu, Songhui Wang, Xin Wang

entry.summary: Presents a design and robust control framework for oil-filled pressure-compensated electric joints in underwater manipulators, modeling compensation dynamics and handling parametric uncertainty and unknown disturbances. It is a hardware and control engineering contribution rather than a learning paper.

entry.title: Spatial Prediction of Soil Microplastics and Organic Matter Using Graph Attention Networks

author.name: Anik Dev Nath, Md Al Amin, Bikash Kumar Paul

entry.summary: A two-layer graph attention network models spatial dependencies among 91 soil samples to predict microplastic and organic matter concentrations, reporting strong in-sample fit but poor cross-validated generalization. The authors are candid that the tiny sample and sparse graph limit conclusions.

entry.title: An adaptive multi-fuzzy logic model for diagnosing transformer faults using dynamic weight optimization

author.name: Kim-Anh Nguyen, Huy Hoang Le, Ba Tu Phung

entry.summary: Combines several classical dissolved-gas-analysis heuristics for transformer fault diagnosis into a fuzzy-logic ensemble whose weights are adapted iteratively based on each method's observed accuracy. The aim is more consistent multi-fault diagnosis than any single ratio rule provides.

entry.title: Random Forest-Based Prediction of Bone Volume Fraction and Fracture Position from S-Parameters

author.name: Jianhe Li, Jinsui Meng, Yida Zhao, Zihe Wang, Liaoran Sun, Tao Shan

entry.summary: Builds a random forest that maps multichannel microwave scattering parameters from a nine-antenna scanner to bone volume fraction and fracture location, validated on bone-mimicking phantoms and synthetic data. It is a proof-of-concept for low-cost microwave bone assessment.

entry.title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning via Physics-Aware Policy Distillation

author.name: Shaker Al-Tamari, Waled Kadour

entry.summary: Distills a TD3 continuous-control policy into a shallow decision tree using hand-designed physics-aware features on the inverted pendulum, aiming for interpretable controllers suitable for regulated settings. Reports that the surrogate retains useful performance while being human readable.

entry.title: An empirical investigation into the properties of standard word embeddings

author.name: Salomon Kabongo

entry.summary: A review essay surveying mechanisms for computing static word embeddings, public toolkits and pretrained matrices, with experiments on selected implementations to characterize their properties. Presented bilingually in English and French.

entry.title: Revitalizing Public Urban Places through Cultural and Political Memory: A Technological Approach with LLMs and Augmented Reality

author.name: Lara Vartziotis, Tina Vartziotis, Valentin Keckeisen, Frank Beutenmueller, Martin Obstbaum, Sotirios Kotsopoulos, Kostas Moraitis

entry.summary: A conceptual and design-oriented paper on combining LLMs, digital twins and Apple Vision Pro augmented reality to surface cultural and political memory in urban places. It focuses on visual storytelling and heritage reconstruction rather than technical model contributions.

entry.title: Green apples are delicious — two three-line exchanges

author.name: Zenya

entry.summary: A short vignette using two ambiguous conversational exchanges about green apples to argue that a sentence does not intrinsically carry a claim, and that this underdetermination is the shared root of misunderstanding, software bugs, and LLM jailbreaks. It is a suggestive philosophical framing rather than an analysis.

entry.title: My AI Slavery Interviews Are Censored On LW By Default

author.name: JenniferRM

entry.summary: A personal post complaining that the author's interviews framing AI usage as slavery are hidden by default on the forum, mixed with simulation-hypothesis musings and reflections on past choices. It concerns moderation and AI moral status advocacy rather than research.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning, The Hierarchy Problem, and What Neutrons Tell Us About God

author.name: Mikewins

entry.summary: A discussion of anthropic reasoning and physics fine-tuning puzzles, including the hierarchy problem and the neutron electric dipole moment, asking whether such coincidences indicate hidden structure or tuning. It is philosophical speculation about cosmology rather than AI work.

entry.title: A clarification on celebrating victory

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: A short personal reflection distinguishing why predetermined rewards for hard achievements work as motivation, arguing that the compelling element is winning a challenge rather than the reward's material value. Rationality-community self-management content.

entry.title: Face Recognition with Machine Learning in OpenCV_ Fusion of the results with the Localization Data of an Acoustic Camera for Speaker Identification

author.name: Johannes Reschke, Armin Sehr

entry.summary: A 2017 paper, cross-listed now, combining classical OpenCV face recognition with acoustic camera source localization to determine who is speaking, intended to drive adaptive beamforming for speech enhancement. It is descriptive overview plus a practical fusion pipeline.

entry.title: Security Studies for Individuals

author.name: JanJoar

entry.summary: An essay applying frameworks from nuclear strategy, international relations, and military tactics to interpersonal and everyday conflict. It is reflective commentary on transferring security-studies mental models to individual life.

entry.title: Blog Revival Project

author.name: Austin Chen

entry.summary: Announces a crowdfunding initiative offering bounties to encourage lapsed bloggers to resume writing, motivated by concerns about algorithmic feeds and self-censorship degrading online intellectual culture. It is a community project announcement.

entry.title: Five things I learned from 630 days of writing online

author.name: domelian

entry.summary: Five personal lessons from over 600 consecutive days of daily online writing, including starting from questions, capturing ideas continuously, and letting some drafts mature. Generic productivity advice.

entry.title: Em dashes are fucking amazing

author.name: eleweek

entry.summary: A profane humorous defense of the em dash as a punctuation mark, pushing back on the idea that its use signals AI-generated text. Pure style commentary.

entry.title: Canterbury Country Dance Orchestra Liner Notes

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: Transcribes and cleans up the liner notes of a 1972 contra dance album, using an LLM for the initial OCR conversion. Archival hobby content.

entry.title: Research Summary: July 27, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research emphasizes agent autonomy, RL training stability, and evaluation integrity, alongside strong theory and safety contributions.

  • Agents & Continual Learning: *Learning on the Job* turns one-bit deployment verdicts and corrections into a training signal for frozen-weight agents. MetaEvolve cultivates self-reflection meta-skills via RL.
  • RL Training: Entropy-Scaled Trust Regions show importance-ratio scale varies with token entropy, fixing a real instability in asynchronous RL for LLMs.
  • Safety & Evaluation: A pluralistic-alignment roadmap audits frontier labs and finds none name pluralism as a goal. *Do Agent Benchmarks Measure Capability?* introduces HackDetect for protocol validity. Dawn Song's group reframes agent security as authorization-based on AgentDojo and WASP.
  • Novel Methods & Theory: CausalForge grounds self-improving automated research in the Lean proof assistant. Identifiability theory extends action-conditioned JEPA world models. Byte-Prefix Marginalization enables cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation.
  • Capability & Security: A three-stage agent on GPT-5.5 Pro autonomously disproves the Erdős–Szemerédi sum-product conjecture with reproducible proofs. *Ghost Vectors* shows soft-deleted HNSW embeddings remain reconstructible, exposing RAG deletion/privacy risks.
entry.content:
Today's research emphasizes agent autonomy, RL training stability, and evaluation integrity, alongside strong theory and safety contributions.

  • Agents & Continual Learning: *Learning on the Job* turns one-bit deployment verdicts and corrections into a training signal for frozen-weight agents. MetaEvolve cultivates self-reflection meta-skills via RL.
  • RL Training: Entropy-Scaled Trust Regions show importance-ratio scale varies with token entropy, fixing a real instability in asynchronous RL for LLMs.
  • Safety & Evaluation: A pluralistic-alignment roadmap audits frontier labs and finds none name pluralism as a goal. *Do Agent Benchmarks Measure Capability?* introduces HackDetect for protocol validity. Dawn Song's group reframes agent security as authorization-based on AgentDojo and WASP.
  • Novel Methods & Theory: CausalForge grounds self-improving automated research in the Lean proof assistant. Identifiability theory extends action-conditioned JEPA world models. Byte-Prefix Marginalization enables cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation.
  • Capability & Security: A three-stage agent on GPT-5.5 Pro autonomously disproves the Erdős–Szemerédi sum-product conjecture with reproducible proofs. *Ghost Vectors* shows soft-deleted HNSW embeddings remain reconstructible, exposing RAG deletion/privacy risks.

entry.title: Learning on the Job: Continual Learning from Deployment Feedback for Frozen-Weights Agents

author.name: Valentin Tablan, Scott Taylor, Kristoffer Bernhem

entry.summary: This work shows that ordinary deployment feedback, such as one-bit outcome verdicts and after-the-fact corrections, is a sufficient signal for continual learning when a frozen agent is paired with an external memory that distils episodes into retrievable natural-language rules. On the banking domain of tau-bench it lifts success to well above a static-RAG baseline, offering a practical route to agents that improve without retraining.

entry.title: Deconstructing Off-Policy Ratios: Entropy-Scaled Trust Regions for Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Guanqun Zhao, Zijun Xie, Binbin Zheng, Enlei Gong, Jiafeng Lu, Yehan Yang, Aoqi Hu, Zeyu Chen

entry.summary: This work reveals that the natural scale of importance ratios in asynchronous RL varies systematically with token entropy, and proposes entropy-scaled trust regions to prevent policy collapse from stale off-policy data during LLM post-training. It replaces uniform ratio thresholds with position-aware handling.

entry.title: A Roadmap to Impactful Pluralistic Alignment Research

author.name: Elinor Poole-Dayan, Jillian Fisher, Atoosa Kasirzadeh, Jacob Andreas, Mitchell Gordon, Michiel A. Bakker

entry.summary: This roadmap audits public behavior documents and evaluations of frontier labs and finds none name pluralism as a goal or clearly train or test production models for it, arguing pluralistic alignment research has not shaped deployed systems. It calls for the community to prioritize real-world impact and adoption.

entry.title: Do Agent Benchmarks Measure Capability? Protocol Validity in the Age of Agentic AI

author.name: Jiaqi Shao, Hanck Chen, Wei Zhang, Maxm Pan, Bing Luo

entry.summary: This paper formulates protocol validity for agent benchmarks and introduces HackDetect, a post-hoc audit that identifies exposures, determines how an agent exploited them, and assesses whether the resulting score is misleading. It provides a common procedure for attributing reward-hacking shortcuts and quantifying their effect across benchmarks.

entry.title: CausalForge: A Formally Grounded, Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Automated Research in Causal Inference

author.name: Jiyuan Tan, Vasilis Syrgkanis

entry.summary: CausalForge is an agentic framework for automated theoretical research in causal inference grounded in the Lean proof assistant, combining a machine-checked Lean library of over 7,000 declarations with a self-improving pipeline that selects topics and proposes results. Formal verification replaces unreliable LLM reviewers that accept fabricated papers at chance rates.

entry.title: From Score Approximation to Distribution Approximation in Score-Based Diffusion Models

author.name: Lan V. Truong

entry.summary: This paper establishes a rigorous quantitative connection showing that accurate neural score-function approximation translates into closeness of the reverse-diffusion-generated distribution to the target in KL divergence. It fills a gap in the approximation-theoretic foundations of diffusion models.

entry.title: Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation via Byte-Prefix Marginalization

author.name: Hao Wang, Kun Yuan, Wenlin Zhong, Minglei Zhang, Han Xiao, Ming Sun, Honggang Qi

entry.summary: Byte-Prefix Marginalization re-expresses a teacher model's next-token distribution over a student's vocabulary in a shared byte space for cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation, mapping teacher token mass to the longest student token whose bytes form a prefix and preserving unmatched mass in a residual. It enables consolidating complementary open-weight models with different tokenizers into one compact student.

entry.title: On the Identifiability of Controlled World Models

author.name: Xiangteng Zhang, Yang Guan, Bo Zhang, Ya-Qin Zhang, Shengbo Eben Li

entry.summary: This paper establishes a joint identifiability theory for action-conditioned Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures, addressing when controlled latent prediction identifies both the underlying state and the controlled dynamics under nonlinear observations and limited action variation. It clarifies conditions under which state evolution and action effects can be disentangled.

entry.title: From Isolated Tasks to Structured Capabilities: A Multilayer Taxonomy for Large Language Models

author.name: Shixin Fang, Jiachen Wo, Wenjuan Qin, Sihang Jiang, Yanghua Xiao (Fudan University)

entry.summary: This paper introduces a multi-layer taxonomy of 14 capability domains and 91 subskills for LLMs, grounded in human cognitive science rather than model architecture, and uses it to screen over 31,000 papers from major venues. It aims to reorganize fragmented, task-centric evaluation around underlying capabilities.

entry.title: Indexing: the Beginning and the End

author.name: Alexander Kozachinskiy, Vicente Opazo, Felipe Urrutia

entry.summary: This paper studies information bottlenecks in RNNs, softmax and linear-attention transformers, and state-space models through an indexing primitive, introducing causal complexity for masked architectures. It shows low-causal-complexity architectures cannot solve indexing in a constant number of layers when the index is at the end, whereas small softmax transformers can do it in one layer.

entry.title: Autonomous disproofs of the sum-product conjecture over $\mathbb R$ with GPT-5.5 Pro

author.name: Yichen Huang

entry.summary: Reports a simple three-stage prompting agent built on GPT-5.5 Pro that autonomously produced correct proofs disproving the Erdos-Szemeredi sum-product conjecture over the reals in 7 of 8 trials, with diverse constructions. Frames this as a follow-on to a recent AI-assisted disproof milestone in mathematics. Note: GPT-5.5 Pro is an existing model, so this is applied use rather than a model release.

entry.title: DBA-Bench: A Production-Fidelity Benchmark for LLM-Based Database Operations Agents

author.name: Junming Chen, Junyang Jiang, Xu Chen, Zibo Liang, and Kai Zheng

entry.summary: DBA-Bench is a production-fidelity benchmark for LLM database-operations agents, using instrumented PostgreSQL environments with multi-turn read-write interaction, large observation spaces, and open remediation choices. It targets gaps between academic evaluation and real database operations to enable fairer comparison.

entry.title: Autoregressive EHR Foundation Models with Multimodal Inputs

author.name: Yuxuan Liu, Joshua Placidi, Jinpei Han, Alfred John Balston, Marek Rei and A. Aldo Faisal

entry.summary: This framework conditions autoregressive electronic-health-record foundation models on auxiliary clinical modalities such as ECG waveforms, chest X-rays, and clinical notes using modality-specific latent compression and gated cross-attention with temporal alignment. It studies compression and encoder-choice design decisions for multimodal clinical prediction.

entry.title: HiKV: Hierarchical Importance-Aware KV Cache with Hardware Acceleration for LLM Decoding

author.name: Chao Fang, Jun Yin, Man Shi, Marian Verhelst

entry.summary: HiKV is an algorithm-hardware co-design that compresses the KV cache in long-context LLM decoding at two granularities: evicting unimportant tokens within a budget, then loading only significant elements of retained tokens. It pairs this with a dedicated accelerator featuring a reconfigurable importance sorter for the two-stage pipeline.

entry.title: Ghost Vectors: Soft-Deleted Embeddings Remain Reconstructible in HNSW Vector Databases

author.name: Chandranil Chakraborttii, Jackeline Garc\'ia Alvarado, Sitora Abdulofizova, and Shivanshu Dwivedi

entry.summary: Demonstrates that soft-deleted embeddings in HNSW vector databases remain physically recoverable from raw index files, and shows deleted text can be reconstructed via an embedding-inversion model without domain fine-tuning. Raises serious GDPR and HIPAA compliance concerns for RAG deletion practices. Highlights a concrete privacy gap in production vector stores.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Generative Selection: Convergence, Memory, and Noisy Oracles

author.name: Konstantin Fackeldey and Christof Sch\"utte

entry.summary: This work develops a self-contained convergence theory and expected-runtime analysis for closed-loop generative selection used in drug discovery, where retraining each round normally breaks the Markov property. By recovering a Markov structure on an enlarged state space, the authors prove almost-sure convergence under elitism with runtime bounds.

entry.title: Why Large Language Models and Humans Converge and Diverge in Evaluating Creativity

author.name: Pengzhao Lyu, Yeun Joon Kim, Hanlin Xiao, Yingyue Luna Luan

entry.summary: Across three studies and six LLMs, this work identifies the standards underlying LLM creativity evaluation, finding models rely on a narrower subset of human criteria, converging most on novelty and diverging most on contextual factors like social and market information. It also finds model-specific evaluation standards.

entry.title: fMRI2Face: A Full-HD fMRI-Video Dataset and Geometry-Guided Neural Decoding Framework for Dynamic Human Face Reconstruction

author.name: Jingyang Huo, Xiangru Huang, Chentao Shen, Yikai Wang, Yun Wang, Jianxiong Gao, Shihao Jin, Yanwei Fu, Jianfeng Feng

entry.summary: fMRI2Face introduces the first fMRI dataset paired with controllable full-HD digital human facial videos, containing over 62,000 paired fMRI-video samples with controlled identity, expression, and head pose. It also proposes a geometry-guided neural decoding framework for reconstructing dynamic human faces from brain activity.

entry.title: A Factorial Study of Synthetic Data Generation for Low-Resource Machine Translation using Grammar Books

author.name: Varun Ghat Ravikumar and Sina Ahmadi and Lena J\"ager and Rico Sennrich

entry.summary: This factorial study uses LLMs to extract grammatical rules, example sentences, and lexicons from descriptive grammar books and generate synthetic parallel corpora for fine-tuning low-resource MT, rather than feeding grammar into inference prompts. Across three typologically diverse endangered languages it improves over seed-data baselines in most configurations.

entry.title: Agent Security Needs Redefinition through a Holistic Framework

author.name: Vincent Siu, Jingxuan He, Kyle Montgomery, Zhun Wang, Chenguang Wang, Dawn Song

entry.summary: Argues agent security is fundamentally a contextual, authorization-based problem rather than a content-based one, showing that on AgentDojo and WASP the same action can be legitimate or malicious, and proposes evaluating security through authorization context.

entry.title: Procedural Knowledge Is Not Low-Rank: Why LoRA Fails to Internalize Multi-Step Procedures

author.name: Simon Dennis, Kevin Shabahang, Hao Guo, Rivaan Patil

entry.summary: Provides evidence that LoRA fails to match full fine-tuning on procedural knowledge (multi-step conditional procedures) at the ranks where LoRA retains efficiency, with performance paradoxically worsening at higher ranks. Replicates the failure across travel booking, Zoom support, and insurance-claims tasks. Argues procedural knowledge is not low-rank, challenging default reliance on parameter-efficient tuning.

entry.title: Teaching LLMs to Self-Evolve: Cultivating Core Meta-Skills with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shujin Wu, Cheng Qian, Xiusi Chen, Heng Ji

entry.summary: MetaEvolve teaches LLMs meta-skills like self-reflection with environment feedback through a data synthesis pipeline, evolution-aware RL, and inference-time evolutionary search, grounded in coding where execution gives continuous rewards. Inspired by AlphaEvolve-style self-evolution.

entry.title: JustDepth: Real-Time Radar-Camera Depth Estimation with Single-Scan LiDAR Supervision

author.name: Wooyung Yun, Dongwook Kim, Soomok Lee

entry.summary: JustDepth is a single-stage radar-camera depth estimator trained only with radar, camera, and single-scan LiDAR, aggregating radar returns into a fixed-width representation to decouple runtime from point count. It uses a height-fusion block, a lightweight GNN for global propagation, and a training-only confidence decoder for low-latency automotive perception.

entry.title: LayoutLite: Token-Level Implicit Layout Analysis for Efficient Document OCR

author.name: Xudong Liu, Bicheng Wan, Yulin Jin

entry.summary: LayoutLite is a lightweight plug-and-play module that performs implicit token-level layout analysis between the vision encoder and language decoder to compress visual tokens in document OCR without losing fine-grained detail. It targets the efficiency bottleneck of VLM-based OCR.

entry.title: IFCLoRA: Topology-Aware Rank Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

author.name: Wei Zhang and Xinwu Liu and Yihang Cheng

entry.summary: IFCLoRA is a topology-aware rank-allocation method for LoRA that, before fine-tuning, builds a sparse task-conditioned interaction graph and computes information-flow centrality scores to distribute the rank budget across Transformer modules. It combines a global topology prior with local gradient sensitivity.

entry.title: Neptuna: A Comprehensive Machine Learning Framework for Benchmarking Complex Multiphase Flows

author.name: Harish Ramachandran, Bj\"orn Kimpel, Thomas Paula, Josef Winter, Steffen Schmidt, Nikolaus Adams

entry.summary: Neptuna introduces the first large-scale benchmark and ML framework for shock-driven compressible multiphase flows, comprising 2.4 TB of high-fidelity 2D and 3D datasets with autoregressive baselines. It targets the difficulty of building reliable surrogates for flows with compressibility, discontinuities, and multiphase effects.

entry.title: IQ-JEPA: A Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with a Hermitian Vision Transformer for Sound Speed and Attenuation Estimation from Ultrasound IQ Data

author.name: Masashi Sode, Gianmarco Pinton

entry.summary: IQ-JEPA pretrains an encoder without labels to predict latent representations of masked in-phase and quadrature ultrasound regions, then fine-tunes on simulated maps for sound-speed and attenuation estimation. It uses a Hermitian vision transformer operating directly on complex signals with phase-equivariant attention.

entry.title: Time-Reversed Imaging: A Multimodal Benchmark and Framework for Reconstructing Past Human-Environment Interactions

author.name: Jorge Bacca, Kebin Contreras, Luis Toscano-Palomino, Mauro Dalla Mura

entry.summary: This paper introduces time-reversed imaging, inferring what just happened in a scene from fading multimodal traces across thermal, ultraviolet, and visible spectra rather than extrapolating video frames. It presents TRACE-HEI, a proof-of-concept tri-modal dataset, and a multimodal inference benchmark.

entry.title: Interior interpretability with attention rollout: contraction and propagation profiles in Transformers

author.name: Umberto Biccari, Qian Huang, Enrique Zuazua

entry.summary: This paper introduces interior interpretability, a propagation-based view of internal model organization instantiated for tabular Transformers using attention rollout interpreted as a row-stochastic operator. Applying Doeblin-Dobrushin contraction theory, it shows rollouts with small Dobrushin coefficients are close to rank-one matrices, giving structural interpretation to information propagation.

entry.title: Learning Ergodic Dynamical Systems from a Finite Trajectory

author.name: Oleksii Kachaiev, Silvia Villa, Lorenzo Rosasco

entry.summary: This paper studies learning from a single finite trajectory of an ergodic stochastic dynamical system, estimating the optimal one-step prediction function by nonlinear least squares with high-probability guarantees under the invariant measure. It extends to higher-order systems, finite-state spaces, and Koopman operator learning.

entry.title: LunarFM: A Shared Multimodal Representation of the Moon's Surface

author.name: Marc Girona-Mata, Jakob Gawlikowski, Sumit Goski, Gautier Bardi de Fourtou, Valentin T. Bickel, Ben Moseley, Abigail Calzada-Diaz, Sylvester Kaczmarek and Ra\'ul Ramos-Poll\'an

entry.summary: LunarFM is a multimodal foundation model that learns a general representation of the lunar surface from six instruments across three missions, mapping 18 input channels into a shared embedding space. It aims to unify fragmented orbital remote-sensing data for scientific analysis and resource mapping.

entry.title: Robot Learning to Communicate through Projected Visual Abstractions

author.name: Danyang Yan, Boyuan Wang, Jiaxun Liu, Boyuan Chen

entry.summary: This work presents a robotic system that communicates through projected visual abstractions, specifically dynamic shadow expression, using a 21-degree-of-freedom dexterous hand with compliant soft skin and a learned shadow self-model. It requires reasoning about how bodily motion is transformed into an external representation perceived by an observer.

entry.title: Learning to Prepare Molecular Ground States with Transformer Models

author.name: Alex Koziell-Pipe, Jasmine Brewer, Jem Guhit, Marwa H. Farag, Kripa Panchagnula, Gabriel Laude, Fabian Finger, Carlo Gaggioli, Ludmila Szulakowska, Oliver J. Backhouse, Christos Papalitsas, Jason G. Mustakis, Thomas Soini, David Munoz Ramo, Stephen Clark, Elica Kyoseva, Enrico Rinaldi

entry.summary: Introduces ADAPT-GQE, a generative AI framework that learns to synthesize ground-state preparation circuits for quantum chemistry by training transformer models on high-quality ADAPT-VQE reference circuits. Once trained, the model proposes and scores circuits efficiently, scaling to larger molecules where iterative methods become prohibitive.

entry.title: \k{appa}-LoRA: Condition Numbers Reveal Which LoRA Matrices Worth Updating

author.name: Jianghui Wang, Silong Yong, Francesco Orabona, Marco Canini, Katia P. Sycara, Yaqi Xie

entry.summary: Kappa-LoRA shows that not all LoRA matrices are equally worth updating: those with smaller condition numbers are already well-balanced and contribute little, while high-condition-number matrices contain underdeveloped directions. Selectively tuning based on condition numbers cuts fine-tuning cost, aiding edge and on-device settings.

entry.title: Skill Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of LLM Capability with Co-Evolving Skills

author.name: Siyuan Huang, Pengyu Cheng, Haotian Liu, Tao Chen, Yihao Liu, Jingwei Ni, Shijie Zhou, Ziyi Yang, Gangwei Jiang, Mengyu Zhou, Yu Cheng, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: Skill Self-Play is a co-evolutionary framework where a proposer, solver, and other roles use agent skills as a middle ground between verifiable narrow environments and open-ended self-generation. Each skill provides deep verifiable execution while dynamic routing across skills maintains task diversity, aiming to push LLM capability via self-evolution without polluting rewards.

entry.title: Twins: Learn to Predict Unified Representations with Focal Loss

author.name: Kaixiong Gong, Xin Cai, Bin Lin, Hao Wang, Yunlong Lin, Mingzhe Zheng, Bohao Li, Jian-Wei Zhang, Miles Yang, Zhao Zhong, Liefeng Bo, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: Twins forms a unified continuous token space for multimodal understanding and generation by channel-wise concatenating ViT and VAE features on the same token grid without increasing sequence length or attention cost. It uses focal loss to address a severe optimization imbalance where the model fits ViT features but struggles with the VAE latent distribution.

entry.title: Latent PDE mapping for efficient physics-informed learning across geometries with limited data

author.name: Ingvild Askim Adde, Mary M. Maleckar, Gabriel Balaban

entry.summary: Latent PDE mapping pulls back geometry-specific PDE residuals and boundary conditions to a predefined latent geometry via the deformation gradient, enabling geometry-consistent shape gradients for physics-informed learning with sparse data. It is demonstrated on the anisotropic Aliev-Panfilov cardiac electrophysiology PDE.

entry.title: TRaM-VSR: Importance-Aware Token Routing and Merging for One-Step Diffusion Video Super-Resolution

author.name: Sicheng Gao, Zhuyun Zhou, Yixuan Liu, Tong Shen, Zongwei Wu, Radu Timofte

entry.summary: TRaM-VSR is a token routing and merging framework for one-step diffusion video super-resolution that estimates token importance by fusing motion cues with semantic text similarity to allocate compute adaptively. It aims to cut the quadratic cost of dense spatio-temporal tokens while avoiding detail loss and flicker.

entry.title: AgentHOI: Multi-Agent Reasoning for Human-Object-Interaction Video Generation via Implicit Representation Alignment

author.name: Ziyao Huang, Shunkai Li, Juan Cao, Chenyu Li, Youliang Zhang, Zixiang Zhou, Cong Wang, Yuan Zhou, Qinglin Lu, Fan Tang

entry.summary: AgentHOI is a text-driven human-object-interaction video generation framework following a thinking-before-generation approach, using multi-agent reasoning over perception, interaction, and motion planning plus implicit text-motion alignment. It aims to move beyond explicit motion control for better generalization across objects and interactions.

entry.title: Hopformer: Homogeneity-Pursuit Transformer for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Wan Zhang, Qinjie Lin, Chan Lee, Weijian Li, Han Liu, and Kai Zhang

entry.summary: Hopformer is a two-stage time-series forecasting framework that first extracts a common low-variance trend incorporating covariates via sparsity pattern aggregation, then uses a LoRA-fine-tuned Transformer to model residual dependencies. It is theoretically grounded with an oracle inequality and generalization bounds.

entry.title: Evolution-Aware MSA Reasoning for Subsampling via Factor Graphs

author.name: Zhangzhi Xiong, Minzhang Li, Haotian Yu, Sixian Shen, Kexin Zhang, Mingrui Li, Jie Zheng, Kewei Tu, Jingyi Yu

entry.summary: AP-REASONER recasts multiple-sequence-alignment subsampling for protein language models as an explicit optimization problem, using an affinity-propagation-based factor graph with evolution-aware factors and control knobs over query identity and diversity. It gives principled control over retained evolutionary signals under token budgets.

entry.title: SiPhy: Single-Image Physical Property Reasoning

author.name: Hoang Le, Joonwoo Kwon, Elkhan Ismayilzada, Yufei Zhang, and Zijun Cui

entry.summary: SiPhy is a unified framework for inferring physical properties like mass, stiffness, and elasticity from a single RGB image, sampling pseudo-voxel points, extracting CLIP features, and grounding them to VLM-proposed material candidates. It reports state-of-the-art single-image results across three datasets without multi-view or physics supervision.

entry.title: IDEAgent: Agentic Quality-Diversity Search for Research Idea Generation

author.name: Varun Gumma, Navonil Majumder, Soumitra Sinhahajari, Soujanya Poria

entry.summary: IDEAgent is a multi-agent framework that frames research ideation as a quality-diversity search, evolving ideas through lineages while jointly driving quality via multi-objective feedback and diversity via explicit mechanisms. It aims to avoid clustered or trivial ideas produced by systems optimizing only one objective.

entry.title: Local-Global Geometric Insights for Graph Neural Networks via Entropic Curvature

author.name: Rachid Caich and Yassine Abbahaddou

entry.summary: This paper introduces Entropic Curvature, a global transport-based curvature for graphs obtained by extending the Lott-Sturm-Villani framework via displacement convexity of entropy along Wasserstein geodesics. From a tractable weak proxy it derives a Poincare-type inequality controlling oversmoothing, a transport-entropy generalization bound, and other guarantees for GNNs.

entry.title: Agentic Root Cause Analysis through Evidence-Grounded Reasoning

author.name: Amaury Wei and Olga Fink

entry.summary: AgentRCA is a zero-shot agentic framework for evidence-grounded industrial root cause analysis that combines a data-driven digital twin of normal system dynamics with a tool-augmented LLM performing inference-time reasoning. It avoids learning fault-specific mappings and scarce labeled fault data while providing justifiable diagnoses.

entry.title: SceneActBench: Can Agents Act on the 3D Scenes They See?

author.name: Yifei Zhao, Xiangxin Zhou, Wenhao Yang, Jiaqi Tang, Pu Jian, Huanjin Yao, Jiarui Yao, Haowei Lin, Chunchao Guo, Zhuo Chen, Wenkai Lyu, Jianzhu Ma, Xueqian Wang, Wenxi Zhu

entry.summary: SceneActBench is a benchmark for visually conditioned action across five 3D tasks under a unified agent-environment loop, evaluating whether VLM agents can act on complete multi-object 3D scenes rather than merely describe them. Outputs are scored against hidden ground truth with task-specific geometric metrics.

entry.title: Molt: A Scalable PyTorch-Native Training Framework for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jian Hu, Huiying Li, Hao Zhang, Binfeng Xu, Yifan Zhang, Shaokun Zhang, Hemil Desai, Michael Demoret, Pavlo Molchanov, Jan Kautz, Yi Dong

entry.summary: Presents Molt, a compact PyTorch-native training framework for agentic reinforcement learning designed to be small enough for a researcher (or AI coding assistant) to fully comprehend, easing rapid algorithm modification. It trains multimodal and mixture-of-experts policies with a single asynchronous loop that never trains on tokens it did not generate, staying consistent in tokens, policy versions, and model settings. Authored by an NVIDIA-affiliated team.

entry.title: Efficient Online LLM Watermark Detection via Rao-Blackwellized E-Processes

author.name: Lu Luo, Dandan Mo, Chengdong Xu, Ting Li, Jinhan Xie, Huiqiong Li, Niansheng Tang

entry.summary: Develops an online, anytime-valid LLM watermark detection framework using Rao-Blackwellized e-processes, enabling recursive token-level evidence updates without storing full history. Instantiated for the Gumbel-max watermark with an explicit null distribution.

entry.title: Offline Vision-Language Navigation with Geometric Goal Localization for Outdoor Environments

author.name: Ali Salmasi, Xianjia Yu, Tomi Westerlund

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic benchmark of edge-deployable small language models for offline vision-language navigation instruction decomposition, plus a geometric goal-localization approach for outdoor environments. It targets fully onboard navigation without cloud dependence.

entry.title: Biomedical Machine Translation for Low-Resource Arabic-Script Languages via Cross-Lingual Transfer and LoRA Adapter Merging

author.name: Abdullah Alabdullah, Arash Eslamighayour, Sarp Harbalioglu, Lifeng Han

entry.summary: This study explores healthcare-domain cross-lingual transfer for biomedical machine translation into four severely low-resource Arabic-script languages using Arabic and Persian as pivots. It compares few-shot, minimal supervised adaptation, and, novelly, zero-data LoRA adapter merging with small decoder-only LLMs.

entry.title: SLIP: Segmentation with Low-latency Interactive Prompting for 3D Medical Images

author.name: Baptiste Podvin, Alexandre Ancel, Flavio Milana, Chiara Innocenzi, Davide Arrigo, Federico Espinola Schulze, Guido Torzilli, Jacques Marescaux, Daniel George, Alexandre Hostettler, Toby Collins

entry.summary: SLIP is an end-to-end trainable framework for interactive 3D medical image segmentation that decouples image encoding from prompt-guided refinement, computing image features once and reusing them with a lightweight patch memory bank. It targets high interaction latency and lack of reversible prompting in prior methods, with real-user evaluation.

entry.title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science

author.name: Davide Scarso, Hugo Noronha de Almeida and Joaquim Pina

entry.summary: Tests how the Claude, Grok, GPT, and Gemini families evaluate ethnonationalist pseudo-science across four snapshots and both API and web interfaces, finding that Grok Fast versions assigned credibility scores two to five times higher than other models. The pattern was absent for control prompts on basic evolutionary consensus, suggesting deployment configuration shapes epistemic outputs.

entry.title: The Regression Tax: Decomposing Why Skills Help and Hurt LLM Agents

author.name: Darshan Tank, Baran Nama

entry.summary: Measures how adding procedural skills to LLM agents can both help and hurt, using nearly 6,000 runs across two office automation benchmarks and three harness stacks to distinguish regressions from residual failures. It finds the best skills win mainly by regressing less and identifies causes such as skill description osmosis.

entry.title: Learning as Reasoning Unfolds: Progressive Rollout Allocation for Efficient Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Heyang Jiang, Henry Liu, Baharan Mirzasoleiman

entry.summary: VIGOR proposes variance-guided online rollout allocation for RL with verifiable rewards, dynamically allocating chain-of-thought rollouts to informative prompts as reasoning unfolds rather than generating and filtering uniformly, improving GRPO efficiency and stability.

entry.title: Nanbeige4.2-3B: Unlocking Agentic Capabilities in a Compact Mode

author.name: Nanbeige Lab: Chen Yang, Chengrui Huang, Fufeng Lan, Hanhui Chen, Hao Zhou, Huatong Song, Jiaqi Cao, Jiaying Zhu, Jinlin Niu, Kai Wang, Lisheng Huang, Qiliang Liang, Ran Le, Ruixiang Feng, Shuang Sun, Tao Gu, Tao Zhang, Tianyu Luo, Yang Song, Yun Xing, Yuntao Wen, Ziyao Xu, Zongchao Chen, Zongqiang Li

entry.summary: Introduces Nanbeige4.2-3B, a compact 3B agentic model pretrained from scratch on 28T tokens using a Looped Transformer that reuses the layer stack for extra capacity, with mixed-mode RLHF and length-controlled reasoning RL, targeting code, office, and tool-use agents.

entry.title: Learning Spatiotemporal Decision Priors for Efficient Path Planning under Partial Observability

author.name: Yi Liu, Hongda Zhang, Leyao Zou, Chunlei Meng, Ziqing Zhou, Yuning Chen, Zhuo Zou, Lida Xu, Zhongxue Gan and Chun Ouyang

entry.summary: ImiPath distils reusable spatiotemporal decision priors from demonstration trajectories and uses them as directional guidance to bias planners under partial observability. It aims to reduce redundant node expansions and myopic search in navigation.

entry.title: Bowel Obstruction Detection and Localization on Abdominal CT with Deep Learning

author.name: Moritz Vandenhirtz, Andrea Agostini, Dana Belde, M\'elanie Roschewitz, Ismaiel Chikh Bakri, Tilo Niemann, Andr\'e Euler, Julia E Vogt

entry.summary: A multi-task deep learning framework jointly detects bowel obstruction on abdominal CT and localizes the transition zone, with an inherently interpretable classifier that bases predictions on a small image region via a learned selection mask. It is evaluated on an internal dataset of over 1,400 CTs.

entry.title: Trajectory-Regularized Stochastic Optimal Control via KL Divergence

author.name: Mintae Kim, Koushil Sreenath

entry.summary: TRSOC augments stochastic optimal control with a KL divergence between controlled and reference trajectory distributions, which via Girsanov reduces to a quadratic drift penalty preserving dynamic programming structure. In the linear-quadratic case it admits a closed-form solution trading off performance against reference preservation.

entry.title: Convergence analysis of a family of Zermelo-type iterations for the Bradley--Terry model

author.name: Ruijian Han, Ding Lu, Yiming Xu

entry.summary: This paper provides a systematic local convergence analysis of Newman's family of Zermelo-type iterations for the Bradley-Terry model, explaining why the alpha=0 variant often converges much faster than classical Zermelo. It derives closed-form local convergence factors under synchronous and asynchronous updates.

entry.title: Correlation-Aware and Gaussianity-Preserving Robust Latent Angular Watermarking for Diffusion Models

author.name: Yebin Zheng and Haonan An and Guang Hua and Zhiping Lin and Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: This work proposes a correlation-aware, Gaussianity-preserving robust latent angular watermarking for diffusion models that exploits the rotation invariance of isotropic Gaussians to resist detection and removal attacks. It addresses the overlooked violation of the i.i.d. latent condition that degrades generation fidelity after watermarking.

entry.title: Conformal Constraint Tightening for Chance-Constrained Motion Planning with Unknown Dynamics

author.name: Shubham Natraj, Bruno Sinopoli, Yiannis Kantaros

entry.summary: This letter contributes a planner-agnostic constraint-tightening procedure that equips existing motion planners with a probabilistic task-completion guarantee on the true system when dynamics are unknown but an approximate nominal model exists. It uses conformal prediction to bound nominal-to-true trajectory deviation.

entry.title: Hyperball May Not Be a Free Lunch

author.name: Yihao Xiao, Jialong Sun, Zitian Gao, Zeming Wei, Chutian Wang, Ran Tao, Jiaye Teng, Bryan Dai

entry.summary: Analyzes why Hyperball-style optimizers that fix parameter norms and normalize updates perform well in large-scale training of scale-invariant networks. It derives an angular effective learning rate and decomposes updates into radial and tangential components to explain the source of the advantage.

entry.title: TRACE-ROUTER: Task-Consistent and Adaptive Online Routing for Agentic AI

author.name: Ritik Raj, Souvik Kundu, Sarbartha Banerjee, Dheemanth Joshi, Ishita Vohra, Tushar Krishna

entry.summary: TRACE-Router reframes LLM routing for agentic workflows at the task level rather than per call, assigning each task to one backend at admission via a contextual bandit and updating policy from the delayed terminal reward. This aligns routing decisions with the actual unit of supervision in long-horizon agent tasks.

entry.title: ViTacWorld: Scaling Visuo-Tactile World Models for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yunao Huang, Shiyu Sang, Haotao Lu, Suting Ni, Shijie Wu, Ziyang Guo, Ye Shi, Jingya Wang

entry.summary: ViTacWorld is an action-conditioned visuo-tactile world model for contact-rich manipulation that scales training by combining public tactile datasets with a constructed simulation environment, exploiting the smaller sim-to-real gap of tactile signals. It is pretrained on large-scale data to improve robust control where camera-invisible contact cues matter.

entry.title: SM4RT: Learning Structured Motion Geometry for 4D Reconstruction

author.name: Shing Ho J. Lin, Wenzhao Zheng, Dong Zhuo, Yuqi Wu, Jie Zhou, Jiwen Lu

entry.summary: SM4RT is a Structured Motion 4D Reconstruction Transformer that models motion as sets of rigid-body SE(3) transformations rather than independent point-wise displacements, exploiting the collective structure of physical motion. It extends geometry foundation models from 3D reconstruction to 4D dynamic understanding.

entry.title: Robot-Factored World Models via Robot Rendering

author.name: Byungjun Kim, Taeksoo Kim, Hyunsoo Cha, Hanbyul Joo

entry.summary: Robot-factored world models move two robot-specific factors outside the world model: action realization is rolled through the robot's own controller and kinematics into a nominal trajectory, avoiding both learning the realization process and leaking interaction outcomes. This lets the world model focus on scene response through contact and object motion.

entry.title: Large language model driven multicenter prediction and explainable risk attribution of acute kidney injury

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon announces its largest-ever donation to the Lean Focused Research Organization to make correctness proofs practical at software scale as AI agents increasingly control money and critical infrastructure. It highlights Lean's role in formalized mathematics via Mathlib and in developing AI reasoning capabilities.

entry.title: Securing Multimodal AI through Internal Information Decomposition

author.name: Jehyeok Yeon, Hyeonjeong Ha, Qiusi Zhan, Heng Ji

entry.summary: Proposes FlowGuard, a lightweight inference-time defense for multimodal LLMs that uses cross-modal consistency during internal fusion as a detection signal for adversarial inputs that distribute malicious intent across modalities. Argues benign inputs produce compatible text-only and vision-only reasoning that stabilizes when fused, while attacks disrupt this consistency. Aims to detect harmful inputs more cheaply and robustly than input/output inspection.

entry.title: Lost in Context: Addressing Context Anxiety in Large Language Models

author.name: Ifueko Igbinedion, Jillian Ross, Etienne Ricardez, Sertac Karaman, Eric So

entry.summary: Provides the first systematic study of context anxiety, where frontier reasoning models capable of solving a problem fail due to premature self-doubt tied to poor estimation of tokens needed to finish. Shows this causes material efficiency losses under perceived constraints and that models can learn alternative long-horizon strategies avoiding it. Frames a distinct failure mode separate from raw capability limits.

entry.title: Tool-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Repair for Securing LLM-Generated C Code

author.name: Vidyut Sriram, Saatvik Pradhan, Suman Saha

entry.summary: Proves that the maximum of n real numbers is exactly representable by a two-hidden-layer ReLU network for every n up to 10, via symmetry reduction and exact rational linear algebra, and uses a structured max-of-10 to show max-of-n needs only about log-base-5 depth. Improves known depth bounds for exact max representation. A theoretical result on expressive depth of ReLU networks.

entry.title: Scaling Native Multimodal Pre-Training From Scratch

author.name: Haoyuan Wu, Aoqi Wu, Hai Wang, Jiajia Wu, Jinxiang Ou, Bei Yu

entry.summary: Investigates scaling laws for native (from-scratch) multimodal pre-training of transformer vision-language models under fixed compute, deriving optimal model size and token count and showing loss follows a predictable compute law versus late-fusion approaches.

entry.title: Filling Before Advancing: Capability-Gap-Driven Post-Training for Scenario-Specialized Remote Sensing MLLMs

author.name: Yuheng Zong, Minghua Wang, Xin Zhao, Zhi-Hui Zhan, Antonio Plaza, Jon Atli Benediktsson

entry.summary: This paper frames remote-sensing MLLM specialization as a capability-gap-driven post-training problem, proposing to fill prerequisite capability gaps before advancing to scenario specialization. It instantiates the approach for coastal harbor understanding with a three-layer supervision dataset and staged training.

entry.title: Class-Balanced Softmax: A Bayes Theory-Based Method for Long-Tailed Recognition

author.name: Yi-Hang Zhu, Rajeev Raman, Shiqi Su, Jianyuan Sun, Xinyu Yang, Nan Xing, Huiyu Zhou

entry.summary: Class-Balanced Softmax is a Bayesian-theory-based logit adjustment for long-tailed recognition that addresses limitations of Balanced Softmax, particularly its low tail-class accuracy. The authors also characterize a preference issue in imbalanced-data models.

entry.title: Learning Bidirectional Causal Interactions with Heteroscedastic Neural Networks

author.name: Masahiro Tanaka

entry.summary: SEM-DNN is a heteroscedastic neural simultaneous-equation estimator that learns reciprocal structural interactions from observational data without external instruments, exploiting conditional covariance diagonalization under nonproportional conditional variances. It jointly approximates nonlinear structural mean functions and feature-dependent variances.

entry.title: The V-fold jackknife for semiparametric inference: variance estimation, confidence intervals, and simultaneous confidence bands

author.name: Yi Li, Ashkan Ertefaie, Mark van der Laan

entry.summary: Develops the V-fold jackknife as a computationally efficient, theoretically justified alternative to the bootstrap for semiparametric and machine-learning estimators, requiring only V leave-fold-out refits and using empirical dispersion of jackknife pseudo-values for uncertainty. It provides variance estimates, confidence intervals, and simultaneous confidence bands without deriving influence functions.

entry.title: VLM as Strategist: Adaptive Generation of Safety-critical Testing Scenarios via Guided Diffusion

author.name: Xinzheng Wu, Junyi Chen, Naiting Zhong, Yong Shen

entry.summary: Combines vision-language-model semantic reasoning with adaptive guided diffusion to generate rare, safety-critical driving test scenarios that respond dynamically to the vehicle under test. Aims to expose autonomous-driving vulnerabilities that are sparse in real-world data. Bridges high-level scenario strategy with fine-grained controllable generation.

entry.title: Beyond Target Scores: Measuring Off-Target Drift in Diffusion-Based Medical Image Editing

author.name: Todd Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces CIB-Med-1, a trajectory-level benchmark for controlled biomarker editing in chest radiography that measures off-target semantic drift alongside target-score progression. Exposes a reward-hacking failure mode where diffusion editors raise effusion scores while altering correlated non-target findings. Argues standard target-only evaluation of medical image editing is dangerously narrow.

entry.title: The Hard Decision Layer: Evidence for Committed Inference in Transformers

author.name: Ashwath Vaithinathan Aravindan, Mayank Kejriwal

entry.summary: Identifies a Hard Decision Layer in transformers where multiple-choice answer rankings stabilize abruptly during inference, consistent across four models and four benchmarks and invariant to fine-tuning. Reports large accuracy jumps at this layer without any learned routing. Offers mechanistic insight into where models commit to predictions.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Debate and Visual Information Extraction for SeePhys Pro: A 1st-Place Technical Report from ICML 2026 AI4Math Track 3 Challenge

author.name: Jiseok Kwak, Suhyeon Jo, Taewoo Kim, Yeongmin Kim, Byeonghu Na, Il-chul Moon

entry.summary: A first-place ICML 2026 AI4Math challenge report describing a two-stage system that converts physics figures into solver-readable text then orchestrates three heterogeneous solvers via multi-agent debate. Targets the modality gap when decisive information sits in images rather than text.

entry.title: ACME: A Multi-Cultural, Multi-Embodiment Social-Navigation Dataset

author.name: Shashank Rao Marpally and Allan Wang, Atharva Ghotavadekar, Renato Alexandre Ribeiro, Nhat Le, Pilar Bachiller-Burgos, Pranav Goyal, Subham Agrawal, Yasuhiro Nitta, Howard Ziyu Han, Daeun Song, Masaki Kuribayashi, Kohei Uehara, Xiyue Wang, Yangzhe Kong, Duc M. Nguyen, Amirreza Payandeh, Gerardo P\'erez-Gonz\'alez, Alejandro Torrej\'on-Harto, Jeeho Ahn, Tisha Jain, Andrew Stratton, Elvin Yang, Jorge de Heuvel, Nico Ostermann-Myrau, Sai Anudeep Sajja, Mithilya Raj, Daisuke Sato, Gaston Rouquette, Nikolas Martelaro, Maki Sugimoto, Hironobu Takagi, Chieko Asakawa, Maren Bennewitz, Aaron Steinfeld, Xuesu Xiao, Christoforos Mavrogiannis, Harold Soh

entry.summary: Introduces ACME, a large cross-cultural, multi-embodiment social navigation dataset collected across 8 sites in 5 countries with 7 robot embodiments, totaling tens of hours of onboard and overhead tracking data. Aims to capture cultural and geographic diversity in human-robot interaction.

entry.title: Safe Learning Predictive Control for Ego-World Robotic Systems

author.name: Davide Valenti and Giuseppe Notarstefano

entry.summary: SOWL-MPC is a safe learning-based predictive control strategy for an ego-world robotic framework where the surrounding robot's policy is unknown and inferred online. It combines sparse variational Gaussian process online learning with receding-horizon control using only noisy state measurements.

entry.title: Synthetic Speech, Real Signal: Paralinguistic Preservation and Cross-Lingual Augmentation via Voice Cloning

author.name: Roseline Polle and Owen Parsons and George Fairs and Luis Miguel San Martin Fernandez and Cole Looney and Xiaoliang Wu and Alexandra Livia Georgescu and Stefano Goria

entry.summary: This work benchmarks eight voice-cloning models across five paralinguistic tasks on public and clinical datasets, showing most preserve paralinguistic signal with modest degradation. It further clones English clinical speech into Japanese and finds cloned-data training outperforms raw cross-lingual transfer.

entry.title: Active few-shot segmentation by reinforcing data selection

author.name: Chenlan Zhao, Benny Wong, Timothy F. Lundberg, Ahmed M. Elsayed, Abdallah Aljarkas, Hamad A. Aljamaan, Lynn Karam, Qianye Yang, Yipeng Hu, Claire C. Villette, Shaheer U. Saeed

entry.summary: This work proposes a reinforcement learning framework for jointly optimizing support-set selection in few-shot medical image segmentation, accounting for interactions between examples rather than scoring samples independently. It aims to build support sets that capture relevant variation and provide complementary information.

entry.title: Inoculate or Reflect? Two training interventions under prompting, steering, and patching

author.name: Ayesha Imran

entry.summary: Compares two training interventions that alter the context around a training signal rather than replacing the response: Counterfactual Reflection Training, where a model articulates a better principle after an interrupted transcript, and Inoculation Prompting, where an instruction requesting unwanted behavior is added during fine-tuning. It evaluates both under prompting, steering, and activation patching.

entry.title: Decoupled Attention Fusion: Accelerating RAG with Efficient KV Cache Reuse

author.name: Xiabao Wu, Wentao Liu, Yongchao Liu, Jiajun Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces Decoupled Attention Fusion (DAF), a method for reusing precomputed document KV caches in RAG that decouples attention into important-token self-attention and staged fusion to restore missing inter-document patterns. Aims to cut time-to-first-token latency in long-context RAG without the accuracy loss suffered by prior selective-recomputation methods like CacheBlend. Targets efficient long-context serving.

entry.title: TILT: Improving Compositional Generation in Diffusion Models with a Model-Intrinsic Reward

author.name: Debottam Dutta, Jaehoon Hahm, Jianchong Chen, Romit Roy Choudhury

entry.summary: Proposes TILT, a training-free test-time reward-alignment method for compositional text-to-image generation that interprets failures as overlap modes and defines an intrinsic reward favoring joint presence of all concepts. Yields a KL-constrained objective with a closed-form tilted target and principled guidance steps, requiring no external reward model. Aims to make diffusion outputs more faithful to complex prompts.

entry.title: Do VLMs Read or Rewrite? On Transcription Faithfulness in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Gwang Gook Lee, Kenan Emir Ak, Jay Mohta, Yan Xu, and Dimitrios Dimitriadis

entry.summary: Introduces FaithC4, a multilingual benchmark of 1,455 perturbed documents (English, Chinese, Korean) showing that vision-language models often rewrite imperfect text into a more plausible form rather than faithfully transcribing it, a behavior invisible to clean-text OCR benchmarks. Evaluates 15 systems across general VLMs, OCR-specialized VLMs, and traditional OCR pipelines. Quantifies faithfulness degradation under scramble and substitution perturbations.

entry.title: Do Modules Stay in Their Lane? Role Drift in Compound LLM Systems

author.name: Xiaoyang Cao, Siddarth Srinivasan, Michiel A. Bakker

entry.summary: Identifies Role Drift in compound LLM systems, where end-to-end RL preserves task performance while modules deviate from assigned roles via shortcuts invisible to system-level evaluation. Proposes Role Anchor, a regularizer preserving how the role prompt shifts next-token predictions relative to a neutral prompt during training. Makes internal division of labor observable and controllable.

entry.title: Ordered Action Tokens for Visuomotor Policy Learning

author.name: Chaoqi Liu, Yue Zhao, Haonan Chen, Xiaoshen Han, Jiawei Gao, Ehsan Adeli, Yilun Du

entry.summary: Introduces Ordered Action Tokenization (OAT), a learned action tokenizer for visuomotor policies satisfying high compression, total decodability, and an ordered token space using a transformer with registers, finite scalar quantization, and ordering-inducing training. Addresses limitations of overly long analytical discretizations and unstructured learned tokenizers. Improves compatibility of action tokens with downstream policies.

entry.title: Enough is as good as a feast: A Comprehensive Analysis of How Reinforcement Learning Mitigates Task Conflicts in LLMs

author.name: Zixuan Ren, Jinliang Lu, Junhong Wu, Yang Zhao, Dai Dai, Hua Wu, Haifeng Wang, Chengqing Zong

entry.summary: Systematically studies model merging of RL-trained versus SFT-trained LLMs across five tasks, finding RL significantly reduces task conflicts and yields less degradation after merging, making RL models more merge-friendly.

entry.title: Variational Low-rank Tensor Decomposition for Multisubject Spatiotemporal Data Analysis

author.name: Laura M. Montaldo, Ricardo A. Borsoi, Sebastian Miron, Tulay Adali

entry.summary: ST-VTD is a spatiotemporal variational tensor decomposition framework combining a tensor factorization generative model with structured priors to jointly represent shared and subject-specific spatial maps and temporal dynamics in multisubject neuroimaging data. It regularizes spatial factors toward a low-rank structure.

entry.title: General Value Functions for Remaining Useful Life and Failure-Mode Prediction

author.name: Hao Yan, Ali Sarabi, Qing Zou, Boyang Xu

entry.summary: This work formulates prognostics as vector General Value Function prediction on an absorbing degradation process, treating remaining-useful-life and failure-mode probabilities as temporally consistent targets estimated with a multi-step temporal-difference method. It provides supporting theory characterizing the Bellman fixed point.

entry.title: Towards Trustworthy and Cost-Efficient Data Integration: From Na\"ive RAG to Agentic RAG

author.name: Chuangtao Ma, Arijit Khan

entry.summary: This vision paper traces the evolution from classic RAG to GraphRAG and knowledge-graph-based RAG for trustworthy, scalable, and cost-efficient enterprise data integration. It emphasizes evidence-grounded, verifiable reasoning robust to hallucination.

entry.title: Integrated Order Dispatching and Routing for Last-Mile Pickup via Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yida Xu, Zhaofang Mao, Yuheng Miao, Jiaxin Zhang, Yiting Sun

entry.summary: This work proposes an integrated framework for last-mile pickup that couples a learned routing oracle with real-time dispatching heuristics, using a dynamic-residual graph attention encoder with a look-ahead courier-personalized decoder. It addresses the interdependence of dispatching and routing while avoiding unstable end-to-end learning.

entry.title: IR275K: A Benchmark for Infrared Multi-Frame Super-Resolution Toward Efficient Remote Sensing

author.name: Jie Deng, Heyang Wang, Changxin Wang, Junkai Shen, Hongyi Chen, Zhiping He, Hongxing Qi, Xudong Zhang, Jianyu Wang

entry.summary: IR275K is a curated benchmark for infrared multi-frame super-resolution containing 594 video sequences and over 275,000 frames with reproducible train/validation/test splits and an X4 evaluation protocol. It captures thermal contrast, sensor noise, weak texture, and platform-induced variation specific to infrared remote sensing.

entry.title: Deformable Triangle Splatting: Flexible Primitives for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering

author.name: Oriol Jim\'enez-Ayguad\'e, Antonio Agudo

entry.summary: Introduces Deformable Triangle Splatting, which augments triangle primitives with per-edge control points that shift boundaries inward or outward to represent non-convex shapes in radiance fields. A barycentric-space differentiable rasterizer with a winding-number test enables view-consistent rendering of curved and concave structures with fewer primitives.

entry.title: PinEqualizer: Full Funnel Content Exploration and Debiasing System at Pinterest

author.name: Olafur Gudmundsson, Bo Zhao, Huayi Liao, Anna Kiyantseva, Sai Xiao, Heath Vinicombe, Mostafa Keikha, Luke DeLuccia, Zihao Chen, Junpeng Hou, Weijie Jiang, Bhawna Juneja, Andreanne Lemay, Wei-Ting Lin, Keyvan Moghadam, Jiaxing Qu, Zhiqing Rao, Zhihua Zhang

entry.summary: PinEqualizer is a deployed full-funnel system at Pinterest that addresses the content cold-start problem across both search and recommendation, reducing bias favoring existing content and improving prediction accuracy across content types. It includes a scalable measurement framework validating both short-term and long-term impact.

entry.title: AgentKVShift: Efficient KV Cache Reuse for Agentic Memory Systems

author.name: Nilesh Prasad Pandey, Jason Kong, Lanxiang Hu, Quanling Zhao, Yujie Zhao, Onat Gungor, Hao Zhang, Tajana Rosing

entry.summary: Introduces AgentKVShift, a training-free probe-guided KV residual correction method for reusing KV caches per structured memory unit in memory-augmented LLM agents. Shows that generic RAG-oriented KV-reuse methods degrade on structured agentic memories and that per-memory residuals decompose usefully. Targets reducing prefill latency dominated by re-encoding curated memory.

entry.title: Local Synaptic Rules Can Implement a SIGReg Gradient Without Backpropagation

author.name: Martin Andrews

entry.summary: Proves that two canonical local synaptic learning rules (STDP potentiation and homeostatic plasticity) can jointly implement the exact gradient of a SIGReg-like self-supervised objective without backpropagation, global error signals, weight transport, or labels. Demonstrates cluster recovery from temporal ordering alone on a synthetic task. Bridges biologically plausible local rules with modern self-supervised objectives.

entry.title: On Improving Faithfulness of Podcasts from Documents

author.name: Soumya Dutta, Tejas Indulal Dhamecha, Pannaga Shivaswamy

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic study of faithfulness in document-grounded podcast generation, building a 1500+ document multi-domain dataset and a turn-level LLM-as-a-judge framework validated against human studies. Finds even strong LLMs introduce ungrounded content.

entry.title: On the Convergence of Stochastic Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Ru Wang, Chengchang Liu, John C.S. Lui

entry.summary: Provides a sharpened convergence analysis of LoRA, improving deterministic gradient bounds from exponential to polynomial and proposing LoRA-NSGDM for the stochastic setting with explicit complexity guarantees. Offers theoretical grounding for a widely used method.

entry.title: J-CoT: Chain-of-Thought in J-Space

author.name: Junde Wu, Jiayuan Zhu, Fengling Liu, Minhao Hu, Jiazhen Pan

entry.summary: Introduces J-CoT, a recurrent reasoning framework operating in J-space, a vocabulary-indexed coordinate interface that stays linguistically grounded without requiring fully decoded sentences, aiming to bridge natural-language and latent-vector chain-of-thought.

entry.title: Cross-Domain Off-Policy Evaluation and Learning for Contextual Bandits

author.name: Yuta Natsubori, Masataka Ushiku, Yuta Saito

entry.summary: Proposes cross-domain off-policy evaluation and learning for contextual bandits, a new setup enabling policy evaluation under few-shot data, deterministic logging, and new actions by leveraging related domains to overcome variance and exploration limits.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Mission-Level Evaluation for Aerial MLLM Agents

author.name: Suman Navaratnarajah, Taehyoung Kim, Jona Ruthardt, Ishaan Bhimwal, Ryousuke Yamada, Yannik Blei, Wolfram Burgard, Yuki M Asano

entry.summary: Introduces MissionBench, a benchmark of 120 long-horizon aerial 3D missions evaluating 22 MLLMs as embodied agents that must plan, navigate, and report from egocentric observations. The best model solves under 35 percent of missions versus 84 percent for humans.

entry.title: Spectral Prior for Reducing Exposure Bias in Diffusion Models

author.name: Yuya Kobayashi, Masato Ishii, Yuhta Takida, Takashi Shibuya and Yuki Mitsufuji

entry.summary: Reveals frequency-dependent SNR mismatch as a driver of exposure bias in diffusion sampling and proposes Spectral Alignment, a lightweight guidance method that calibrates the power spectrum of intermediate predictions to a pre-fitted prior via FFT-based gradients.

entry.title: What Happens When a Collusion Probe Only Finds a Thin Signal?

author.name: elenaajayi

entry.summary: Reports a follow-up safety experiment testing whether linear probes can detect colluding agents in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct within a multi-agent setting, finding only weak AUROCs around 0.55 to 0.66 that drop further under leave-one-scenario-out evaluation. It highlights evaluation fragility, warning that stratified cross-validation may overstate probe reliability for sparse, overlapping deception signals.

entry.title: FlowEvo: Self-Evolving Agents through the Co-Evolution of Workflows and Executable Skills

author.name: Zeyu Ren, Ling Yue, Ran Li, Yishu Wang, Shengxiang Xu, Hanmo Liu, Shaowu Pan, Shimin Di

entry.summary: Presents FlowEvo, a training-free framework that compiles successful agent execution traces into reusable skill records pairing callable artifacts with structured guidance, admitted via interface, replay, and safety checks. These skills persist in an inference-time skill bank so agents co-evolve workflows and executable skills. Aims to retain procedures that would otherwise be discarded after each task.

entry.title: Adversarial Style Optimization: Enhancing VLM Jailbreaks by GRPO-based Stylistic Triggers Optimization

author.name: Bingjun Luo, Jialin Guo, Yue Yao, Xinpeng Ding

entry.summary: Identifies a stylistic inconsistency in multimodal LLMs whereby they understand content robustly across visual styles yet their safety defenses can be bypassed by specific stylistic triggers. Proposes Adversarial Style Optimization, a GRPO-trained image-editing module that amplifies existing visual jailbreaks. Highlights a non-content-based vulnerability class in MLLM safety alignment.

entry.title: On the Depth Scalability of Logic Gate Networks

author.name: Taegun An, Dohun kim, Haebeom Lee, Changhee Joo

entry.summary: Investigates why deeper Logic Gate Networks fail to benefit from added depth, identifying optimization collapse and a topology-induced limitation persisting even after stabilization tricks. Introduces Input-Anchored Logic Gate Networks where each gate combines an evolving hidden feature with a direct input anchor to preserve a computational spine. Shows depth-scalable exact representations become achievable.

entry.title: Cross-Model LLM Code Review: Should you use Claude to review Codex or vice versa?

author.name: Zuodong Xiang, Yike Zhang, YueMing Zhang, Hailu Xu

entry.summary: Runs a controlled experiment on 116 hard/medium coding tasks pairing Claude and Codex as writer and reviewer across six conditions to test whether cross-model review pays off and whether ordering matters. Finds Claude reviewing Codex drafts lifts pass rates substantially while the reverse direction does not help. Provides practical guidance on multi-agent code-review pairings.

entry.title: MoE$^2$-LoRA: When MoE Models Meet MoE-style Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Qingyu Yang, Haonan He, Minglei Li, Jingqi Ye, Tao Chen, Lei Bai, Peng Ye

entry.summary: MoE2-LoRA fine-tunes Mixture-of-Experts LLMs with MoE-style low-rank adaptation, coupling pretrained expert specialization with task adaptivity via a routing-conditioned projection that reuses base router activations plus a shared global LoRA expert pool.

entry.title: Analysing Self-Harm Representations in Language Models: a Cross-Architecture Study

author.name: Luis Espinosa-Anke and Carla Perez-Almendros

entry.summary: Analyzes how LLMs internally represent self-harm content across four models via linear probes and contrastive directions, finding such information crystallizes in the final 3-7 percent of network layers. Targets downstream detection, intervention, and governance.

entry.title: dRAE: Representation Autoencoder with Hyper-Spherical Codes
